x: Agents Burrow is built so an AI agent can create, inspect, test and ship a game without a window or GPU. There are three levels, all deterministic (same seed + same commands = same session_hash ). tool for transport burrow CLI ( --json ) project workflow: new, test, build, script, assets, doctor process, exit codes 0/1/2 burrowd engine sessions: build voxel worlds, observe, snapshot, replay MCP over stdio; optional JSON-RPC on a unix socket or loopback with a Bearer token burrowedit -headless -agent the editor document: nodes, components, voxel tools, Play MCP over stdio or unix socket burrow agent --stdio [project] starts the editor server for a project; burrowctl is a stateless JSON CLI over the same session API as burrowd . Use llms.txt llms.txt is the compact briefing to give to a model: coordinate conventions, cheap-to-expensive ways to observe, the tool lists, error format. Put it in the system prompt or let the agent read it first. Writing game code? Start with the cards llms-gogame.txt (plain-Go game) and llms-script.txt (WASM scripts), and copy from the recipes . Small or fast models (GLM flash, Haiku...) do better with the task cards: llms-voxel.txt (build a world), llms-project.txt (game project and scripts), llms-editor.txt (editor tools). Each is under 300 words with copyable calls. Suggested system prompt: "You drive the Burrow engine through tools. Use names not ids, coordinates x right/y up/z toward viewer, observe cheap before expensive, on error read hint and valid[] and retry, never invent API names (search the docs)." plus one card. Recipes Build a world, look at it, keep it (burrowd): vox_session_create {generator:"flat", seed:1} vox_act {commands:[{kind:"fill_box", data:{min:[0,9,0], max:[4,12,4], block:"stone"}}, ...]} (atomic; batch up to 4096 commands) vox_observe {min, max} for RLE text, then vox_screenshot {ascii:true} , and png:true only when the picture matters vox_snapshot before risky edits; vox_diff from:"last" ; vox_restore or vox_undo Weather (optional, deterministic, off until enabled): vox_act {commands:[{kind:"weather_set", data:{enabled:true, type:"storm", instant:true}}]} , then vox_step ; in the editor use editor_weather . See weather.md . Water (flows by itself): vox_act fill_box / set_block with water , then vox_step ; read a cell with editor_water in the editor. See water-physics.md . Documentation: editor_docs_search {query} finds sections of the embedded docs (guides, tutorials, the generated reference ); editor_docs_read {page, anchor} reads one. They are read-only and work in every mode. Edit a project through the editor (burrowedit): burrow agent --stdio mygame # or: burrowedit -headless -agent stdio -project mygame editor_create_node , editor_set_component {path, component, data} , editor_tool_apply {tool:"box", start, end, block} , editor_save , then editor_play -> editor_step {ticks} -> editor_state (hashes) -> editor_stop ( engine_hash and doc_hash return to their pre-play values); editor_verify_replay checks that the journal reproduces the live state. Every mutation is one undo step and a journaled command. Paths are node paths like /Tower/Door . Errors are {code, message, hint, valid[]} : read hint and valid , then retry. Verify a change (any agent, no GPU): burrow test --json # {"ok":true,"hash":"...","runs":[...],"report":{...}} burrowplay -headless -ticks 600 -hash mygame burrowplay -headless -ticks 600 -journal j.json mygame && burrowplay -replay j.json -expect <hash> mygame Write a behaviour : burrow script new bot , edit scripts/bot/main.go , burrow script build , attach it with editor_set_component (component script , {"module":"assets/scripts/bot.wasm","props":{...}} ), burrow test . See scripting.md . Edit without hand-written JSON : burrow config set runtime.plugins.controller false , burrow scene set-component scenes/main.voxscn /Sun render.pointlight intensity=3 (both validated, atomic). Find names with burrow docs search <terms> and burrow ui icons ; make the app icon with burrow icon from logo.png . For terrain use editor_ground_at {x,z} (ground height), editor_find_view {near:[x,z]} (a clear high camera) and editor_place_on_ground {node} instead of probing with raycasts. Ship : burrow build -o game && ./game -headless -ticks 200 -hash prints the same hash as burrow test . Safety Servers never open TCP without a token; sockets are created 0600 in a 0700 directory; the editor confines file tools to the project; request lines, batch sizes and screenshot sizes are capped. The full tool list and limits are in agent/README.md and editor/README.md .

h: Limits and what is not covered
x: Animation Package anim is a generic animation system for any voxel game: keyframe tracks on any component property of the scene schema, clips, a player with queue / speed / loop / ping-pong / events, crossfade, layers (masked, additive), a state machine, tweens, skeletons of rigid voxel parts imported from MagicaVoxel, two IK helpers, the .anim asset format, an editor timeline and script / agent control. .anim file --(assets loader, hot reload)--> anim.Library (clips, machines) | +------------------------------------------+--------------------------------+ | SIM domain | FRAME domain | anim.player component (hashed) --tick--> "anim.step" system | anim.Animator (layers, machine) | integer time, fixed step, quantised writes -> scene properties | frame dt -> Pose -> Skeleton -> matrices v v StateHash / journal / snapshot / replay drawn only: never touches sim state The domain rule (read this first) sim domain (gameplay) frame domain (visual) use it for moving platforms, doors, timed hazards, anything the game logic or physics reads creature and character poses, UI motion, cosmetic effects state lives in the anim.player component of a scene node an anim.Animator you own (never saved, never hashed) clock the fixed tick: every tick adds exactly anim.TickUS = 50 000 microseconds the frame dt you pass to Step writes scene properties (transform, any component field), quantised to 1/4096 nothing: you read Pose() and draw in StateHash yes , while a player exists (name, clip, time, fade, queue, parameters, last events) no snapshot / restore / replay exact: it is a plain component and every control action is a journaled command not applicable Rules the implementation keeps, and your code must keep too: Time is integer microseconds ( int64 ) everywhere. Playback, crossfade, events and the state machine never use a float clock. A speed multiplier is applied as round(dt * speed) , one rounded product, so it is identical on every CPU. Sim writes go through anim.Quantize (a multiple of 1/4096) and the interpolation maths forbids fused multiply-add (explicit rounded products), so two machines agree bit for bit. A sim player is stepped by the anim.step system in entity order , not store order. Events are bounded. Player.Fired holds at most MaxFired (256) events per tick, the rest are counted in dropped ; when one advance covers more than 64 loop cycles the skipped cycles report nothing, and a crossfade's fading-out clip never reports events. Fired is cleared on the first tick after it was filled and by Stop . Control is journaled. anim_play , anim_stop , anim_speed , anim_param , anim_trigger are sim commands; scripts use the host functions below (their effect is applied like entity_set_component ). Do not mutate anim.player behind the journal. The clip library is versioned, not shared mutable state. Library.Add stores deep copies and publishes an immutable version identified by Library.Hash() ; recent versions are retained ( Retained ). The sim system never reads "the library now": it reads the version pinned in its own state ( anim.lib extra: rolled back, snapshotted, hashed once pinned). anim.SyncCommands(e) returns the anim_lib commands that pin the current version; run them through the journal before the ticks that must see new clips ( animplay.Plugin does it every frame, starting with the version the engine began with; the editor does it at Play and before player commands). A replay re-applies them and so plays old ticks with the old clips; a version that is no longer retained is an explicit error, never a silent divergence. For a sim you drive by hand, call SyncCommands after changing the library. Ticks that run before the first sync use the version present when Install ran. An engine that never calls anim.Register does not register the component, so its StateHash is unchanged: every existing golden stays valid. A visual animation must never write a scene component. If something visual needs a scene node (a light colour, a sprite), animate it in the sim domain on purpose, or keep the value in your own frame-side data. Root motion A clip drives a character's movement with the reserved track property root.move (vec3, Target empty): a velocity in blocks per second in the local frame of the target node, rotated by that node's yaw ( transform.rot.y , degrees). Target empty is the node that owns the anim.player ; a path ( "kid" , "a/b" ) targets a descendant, so one player can walk several characters. While the clip plays, anim.step writes the world-space result to physics.character.root_move (quantised). The character system adds it to move for that tick and never stores the sum, so collisions, steps, gravity, water and moving platforms still apply. A script can keep writing move (input) at the same time: the two add up. The target needs a physics.character . Without one nothing moves (counted as Missing ). root_move is cleared the tick after the clip ends, is stopped ( AnimStop ) or is replaced by a clip with no root.move track. Facing is the node's yaw: at yaw 0 the vector is the world vector (the avatar template walks towards -Z). Rotate the node (script or physics.character intent) to turn a dash. Sim domain only. A frame-domain Animator carries root.move in its Pose() without moving anything: read it to drive visuals. Replay-safe: anim.player hashes a root flag only while root motion is active, and root_move only when non-zero, so worlds that never use it keep their StateHash . {"format":"burrow.anim","version":1, "clips":[{"name":"dash","length":0.4, "tracks":[{"target":"","prop":"root.move","kind":"vec3", "keys":[{"t":0,"v":[0,0,-14],"i":"smooth"},{"t":0.4,"v":[0,0,-2]}]}]}]} Script: AnimPlay(self, "dash", AnimPlayOpts{Mode: AnimOnce}) starts it; the dash then walks the character for the clip's length. Quick start lib := anim.NewLibrary() doc, _ := anim.Decode(fileBytes) // a .anim file _ = lib.Add( "assets/lift.anim" , doc) // source label = project path (hot reload replaces it) // sim domain, inside sim.Config.Setup: sch := scene.DefaultSchema() _ = anim.Register(sch) // anim.player, hashable _, _ = scene.Install(e, sch) _ = anim.Install(e, sch, lib) // system "anim.step" + the commands e.Do(scene.AddComponent{Path: "lift" , Name: anim.CompName, Data: [] byte ( `{"clip":"shuttle","playing":true}` )}) e.Do(anim.Play{Path: "lift" , Clip: "shuttle" , Mode: "pingpong" , Fade: 0.25 }) // journaled control With an engine.App add &animplay.Plugin{Library: lib} after engine.ScenePlugin : it registers the component, installs the system on every sim engine of the app (live and replays), and hot-reloads .anim files of an assets.DB resource. // frame domain an := anim.NewAnimator(lib) an.Base().Player = anim.Player{Machine: "locomotion" , Playing: true } an.Layer( "nod" ).Additive = true an.Base().Player.SetParam( "speed" , 1 ) // state machine parameter an.Layer( "nod" ).Player.Play( "nod" , anim.ModeOnce) an.Step(dt) // frame seconds pose := an.Pose() // *anim.Bag, sorted (target, property) -> Value mats := skeleton.Solve(pose, rootMatrix, nil ) // one matrix per bone examples/anim_demo does both: a platform shuttles in the sim domain ( go run ./examples/anim_demo -verify checks twin, replay and a mid-clip snapshot without a window) while a voxel creature on it idles and walks in the frame domain. Tracks, keys, interpolation A Track animates one property of one target. Target is a node path relative to the node that owns the player ( "" = itself) or a bone name; Prop is component.field[.sub] exactly as the schema names it ( transform.pos , transform.rot.y , light.color , physics.body.mass ). anim.CheckProp validates a property and a kind against the schema; the editor and tools use it. kind value interpolation typical property float number all modes transform.pos.x , any float field vec3 [x,y,z] all modes transform.pos , transform.scale , vec3 fields quat [x,y,z,w] (a file may give Euler degrees [x,y,z] ) slerp, shortest path; cubic and bezier ease the slerp transform.rot (written back as Euler degrees) color [r,g,b,a] , 0..1 per channel any array/object field of four numbers bool true / false always step bool fields int integer rounded int fields Each key has the interpolation of the segment that starts at it: i behaviour linear (default) straight line step hold the value until the next key smooth smoothstep ease in/out cubic cubic Hermite with tangents in / out (value units per second); absent tangents are automatic (Catmull-Rom) bezier CSS-style cubic-bezier(x1,y1,x2,y2) easing of the progress ( ease , default 0.42,0,0.58,1), then linear Outside the first and last key the value is clamped. Keys must have strictly increasing times; Decode sorts them and then validates. The Player anim.Player is a plain value: clip, playhead ( t , microseconds), direction, mode ( once , loop , pingpong , empty = the clip's default), speed (0 = 1), a crossfade ( prev , fade , fade_dur ), a queue , an optional machine with state and params , and the events fired by the last Advance . It serialises to JSON, hashes canonically and is the anim.player component. Play , CrossFade(clip, mode, fadeUS) , Enqueue , Stop , SetSpeed , SeekTo , SetParam , SetTrigger . Events are markers on the timeline. They fire once when playback crosses them (also on the first frame for time 0, on each loop wrap, and in both directions in ping-pong) and are listed in Player.Fired for that tick; a script or a system reads them there. A once clip that ends keeps its last pose, stops ( playing:false ) and starts the next queued clip. Blending, crossfade, layers Mix(a, b, w) blends two bags; Overlay(base, layer, ref, w, additive, mask) puts a layer over a base. The Animator keeps a list of Layer s, mixed in creation order: a layer has its own Player , a Weight , an optional Mask (targets equal to or below the listed names) and an Additive flag. Additive adds (pose - reference) * weight , where the reference is the first frame of the layer's clip (vectors and colours add, rotations compose). Properties present on one side only are kept unchanged. State machine A Machine has parameters ( float , int , bool , trigger ), states (a clip and a mode each) and transitions from (a state, "" or * = any) to , with conditions on parameters ( == != < <= > >= , true , false ), an optional exit_time (a fraction of the current clip) and a fade in seconds. The first transition whose conditions hold is taken, once per tick; a trigger tested by that transition is consumed. A machine works identically in both domains ( Player.Machine / anim_param / anim_trigger ). Tweens anim.Tween{From, To, Dur, Delay, Ease, PingPong, Repeat} is a small value stepped with Step(dtMicroseconds) : keep it in sim state and step it with anim.TickUS , or in frame state and step it with the frame time. Easings: linear in_quad out_quad inout_quad in_cubic out_cubic inout_cubic smooth out_back out_bounce . anim.Tweens runs callbacks ( Start , Cancel , Step(dt seconds) ) for the frame domain. Skeletons of rigid voxel parts anim.SkeletonFromVox(file, name, unit) reads the scene graph of a MagicaVoxel file ( importers.VoxFile.Graph , the transform-node hierarchy that Instances flattens): every named transform node (an object or group you named in MagicaVoxel) becomes a bone whose joint is the node's translation; nested nodes become child bones; unnamed nodes only contribute their transform; the models below a bone are its rigid parts ( Skeleton.Parts , each with a Local matrix to bone space, world units, +Y up). unit is the world size of one voxel. Bone names must be unique. Axes follow package character : MagicaVoxel Z up, facing -Y, becomes +Y up, facing -Z. Skinning is rigid: a part follows exactly one bone, so a pose is one matrix per bone and there are no vertex weights. Skeleton.Solve(pose, root, dst) returns the model-space matrix of every bone; the pose values are absolute local transforms ( transform.pos|rot|scale on the bone's name), anything missing keeps its rest value. RestPose() returns the rest bag (to edit or to blend against). IK helpers write rotations into a pose: Skeleton.TwoBoneIK(pose, root, upper, lower, end, target, pole, weight) : leg and arm reach; the middle joint bends towards pole ; a target beyond reach stretches the chain towards it (returns false). Skeleton.LookAtIK(pose, root, bone, target, up, forward, maxDeg, weight) : shortest-arc aim of a bone's forward axis (default -Z) with a turn limit. anim.LookAtRotation and anim.SolveTwoBone are the pure maths. Package character keeps its procedural gait animator (it is code, not keyframes, and its tests and goldens pin it) and adds an adapter: (*character.Clip).ToAnim() converts the keyframed one-shot clips (attack, wave, cheer...) to anim.Clip s with identical sampling, and Pose.ApplyBag writes an anim pose (role names as bones) onto a character pose. The .anim format Stable and versioned ( "format":"burrow.anim" , "version":1 ). Decode rejects unknown fields, other formats and future versions, bounds every size (8 MiB file, 4096 tracks, 65 536 keys per track, 4096 events), sorts keys, validates, and Encode(Decode(x)) is canonical: decoding that output and encoding again gives the same bytes. Times are seconds (rounded to the microsecond). { "format" : "burrow.anim" , "version" : 1 , "clips" :[{ "name" : "shuttle" , "length" : 8 , "loop" : true , "tracks" :[{ "target" : "" , "prop" : "transform.pos" , "kind" : "vec3" , "keys" :[{ "t" : 0 , "v" :[ 0 , 0 , 0 ], "i" : "smooth" },{ "t" : 2 , "v" :[ 8 , 0 , 0 ], "i" : "smooth" },{ "t" : 8 , "v" :[ 0 , 0 , 0 ]}]}], "events" :[{ "t" : 2 , "name" : "arrive" , "arg" : "east" }]}], "machines" :[{ "name" : "locomotion" , "params" :[{ "name" : "speed" , "type" : "float" }], "states" :[{ "name" : "idle" , "clip" : "idle" },{ "name" : "walk" , "clip" : "walk" }], "transitions" :[{ "from" : "idle" , "to" : "walk" , "conds" :[{ "param" : "speed" , "op" : ">" , "value" : 0.1 }], "fade" : 0.2 }]}]} (the snippet is JSON, shown with the go nocheck marker only so the docs checker skips it). .anim files are an asset kind ( animation ) of the asset database: GUID sidecar, thumbnails-less, listed by the Content browser. The loader returns an *anim.Doc . animplay.Plugin and the editor reload a changed file into the library (source label = project path); a file that does not parse keeps the previous content and the error is available from Library.Errors() and the console. Clip names are unique across sources. Editor Tools > Animation Editor , or double-click a .anim in the Content browser, opens the animation editor full screen, like the model editor (Ctrl+Space or Back to world returns; the Animation layout keeps it docked under the viewport). The header holds the file, the clip ( + Clip adds one), the node the clip animates (the crosshair button uses the selection), Dope sheet / Curves, the ⋯ file menu (new, open, save as, delete clip) and Save. The preview above the timeline shows the animated node and its children alone in a studio (dark backdrop, grid floor; drag turns around it, the wheel zooms, a double-click frames it again), with the motion path of the node (a dot every 1/10 s, keys as diamonds) and ghosts 0.3 s before (blue) and after (orange). Show the world swaps it for the world viewport when the scenery matters (a platform that must meet a ledge); Isolate the node comes back. The studio is drawn from the game's own render items ( core.AnimFrame3D : the render input hook keeps the node's meshes, sprites, voxel models and lights), so it shows exactly what the game draws. Animation settings , on the right, edits the selected key (value, easing with a preview of the curve, bezier presets and handles, cubic tangents Auto / Flat, Copy / Paste / Delete), the tracks (add one for a property of the selected node, remove one), the clip (length, loop in the game, node), the motion presets and the events (name, argument, move to the playhead, delete). Rail tools : Select keys (V), Add key (K: a click on a lane keys it there), Event (E: a click on the Events lane adds one) and Record (R). Dope sheet : an Events lane, then the tracks grouped by the node they animate (the group row shows every key time), a diamond per key. Click selects (Shift adds), drag moves the selected keys (snaps to 1/30 s, hold Alt for free), Delete removes them (the shortcut does not delete the node while the pointer is over the timeline). With the pointer over the timeline, Space plays or pauses, Home and End jump to the ends, Left and Right step a frame (Shift: a second), Up and Down jump to the next and previous key, K keys the selected track at the playhead and F zooms to the whole clip. Ctrl+click on a row adds a key. The ruler scrubs; the wheel zooms, Shift+wheel pans. Curves : the value of the selected track over time; the channels of the track (X, Y, Z, ...) are listed under it, click one to draw it; drag a key in time and value. Transport bar : start, previous key, Play, next key, end, the playhead and the clip length, Loop, Preview (writes the pose at the playhead onto the scene; Play advances it with the frame time), Path and Ghosts, Key (the selected track), Key all, Fit. The preview is remembered: ending it (toggle off, save, Play, any ordinary edit) restores the scene exactly, so scrubbing never leaves a trace in the .voxscn . Record : with Preview on, editing a property of a node below the root (gizmo, Inspector, editor_set_component ) creates a key at the playhead for the property that changed (transform position / rotation / scale, any float, int, bool or vec3 field). Only the key goes into the undo history (the scene shows the preview pose, so keeping the edit would write that pose into the document); a drag updates one key; an edit that also changes fields that cannot be keyed is reverted with a console warning. In the game gives the node its animation player ( anim.player ): Plays at start runs the clip as soon as the level runs, Script starts it leaves it waiting for a script ( burrowsdk.AnimPlay(e, "clip", burrowsdk.AnimPlayOpts{}) , the call is shown with a Copy button). The game loads clips from the saved .anim files. Models in parts (a weapon's magazine and bolt, a door's leaf, a creature's limbs): a node that draws a .bmodel split into parts in the model editor (Parts tab: names, pivots, parents) offers Split into animatable parts (Animation settings, Tracks section, or the Outliner's context menu). One undo step turns it into a node per part at its pivot, parented as in the model, each with a voxels child drawing the part ( model.Rig , core.RigNode ); the voxels stay exactly in place. The Node picker of the Tracks section then chooses which part the next track animates. Motion presets generate a tween in one undo step from the playhead to the end of the loop, keyed from the current pose: Bob (pos ±0.5 up/down), Shuttle (pos ±2 on x), Spin (a full turn around y in quarter turns) and Pulse (scale x1.25 and back); the last key repeats the first one's value, so the loop is seamless. Every edit is an undoable core.Op ( AnimKeyOp , AnimMoveKeyOp , AnimDeleteKeyOp , AnimTrackOp , AnimEventOp , AnimClipOp , AnimPlayerOp ), so Ctrl+Z works across scene and animation edits, and record mode folds the property edit and its key into one undo step. Scripts Scripts run in the fixed tick, so they control the sim player (host module vox , additive; script/host_anim.go , sdk/burrowsdk/anim.go ): anim_play(entity, clip, flags) (mode bits 0-1, queue bit 2, crossfade milliseconds in bits 8-23), anim_stop , anim_set_speed , anim_set_param , anim_trigger , anim_time (the playhead in microseconds). Events of the last tick are in the fired array of the entity's anim.player component. See script/ABI.md . burrowsdk.AnimPlay(self, "shuttle" , burrowsdk.AnimPlayOpts{Mode: burrowsdk.AnimPingPong, FadeMillis: 250 }) burrowsdk.AnimSetParam(self, "speed" , 1 ) Agents editor_anim lists clips, machines and players and controls a player (play, stop, speed, param, trigger; one undo step in edit mode, plain journaled commands while playing). editor_anim_edit is the timeline as a tool (open, save, clips, keys, events, scrub, preview, record; edit mode only). The sim commands anim_play , anim_stop , anim_speed , anim_param , anim_trigger are also available to any game that installs anim ( vox_act can carry them once its engine does; the burrowd default session has no scene, so it does not). Limits and what is not covered No vertex skinning (rigid parts only), no inverse-kinematics solver beyond two-bone and look-at, no retargeting between skeletons. Cubic interpolation of rotations is an eased slerp (no tangents); use more keys for tight paths. Tracks cannot drive anim.player or entity-reference fields ( CheckProp rejects them, the sim system refuses to write them). Component JSON is read-modify-written with numbers preserved (integers above 2^53 survive). A property track needs the property to exist: a missing node or component counts in ApplyStats.Missing and is skipped silently. The sim system writes through the scene API of the node tree: only nodes below the player's node are reachable. Held items (first person) render.viewattach draws a node and everything under it in front of the active camera, as if the viewer held it: a weapon or a tool, hands, a compass, a cockpit. offset is in camera space (x right, y up, z backward: a negative z is in front), rot turns it (degrees), scale sizes it (the node's own scale is not used: a unit cube with scale 0 fills the screen), off draws it at its place in the world instead (third person). Only the drawing moves: physics, scripts and the node's animation keep it at its place in the scene, and its parts keep their animated poses relative to it, so a rigged weapon plays its reload clip in the player's hands. In the editor the node stays at its place while editing; Hold in first person (Hierarchy context menu) adds the component and Preview as held shows it from the editor camera to tune the offset; in Play it follows the player's view. A reload, for instance: split the weapon model into parts (body, magazine, bolt), make a reload clip that moves the magazine out and in and the bolt back, with events mag_out , mag_in , bolt (argument sound=... ) for the sounds, set In the game to Script starts it , and call burrowsdk.AnimPlay(gun, "reload", burrowsdk.AnimPlayOpts{Mode: burrowsdk.AnimOnce}) from the script that reads the reload key; queue idle after it with Queue: true .

x: Anti-aliasing and temporal upscaling Render-only (frame domain): nothing here touches the simulation or StateHash . It applies to the HDR shader levels ( -shaders low|medium|high|ultra ) of the Vulkan renderer; -shaders off , -look classic and the soft CPU renderer keep the aliased reference (the soft renderer ignores every setting below). Foundation for the planned ray-tracing stage: jitter, a velocity buffer, a reactive mask and a history already exist. Settings flag (env) values default -aa ( BURROW_AA ) off , fxaa , smaa (SMAA 1x), taa the shader level: low fxaa, medium smaa, high and ultra taa (native resolution), off none -upscale ( BURROW_UPSCALE ) off (bilinear stretch), fsr1 , fsr2 , dlss , xess off ; below 100% -render-scale : fsr1 at medium and high, fsr2 at ultra ( -upscale fsr2 asks for it at any level) -render-scale ( BURROW_RENDER_SCALE ) native , quality (67%), balanced (59%), performance (50%), 0.5..1 or 50..100 native Flags exist on examples/voxel_sandbox and burrowplay ; burrowedit -aa off|fxaa|smaa sets the viewport. The project file ( vox.project , runtime ) takes aa , upscale and render_scale (validated; the flags win). Live: engine.RenderSettings has the string fields AA , Upscale , RenderScale ; the render system re-resolves them every frame and calls vulkan.Renderer.SetAntiAliasing , so Go plugins and the editor can change them at run time. The wasm scripts (ABI v1) are simulation-domain and deliberately get no render setting. Editor: the viewport menu lists "Anti-aliasing: off / fxaa / smaa", the agent tool editor_viewport_screenshot takes an aa argument. The editor viewport is an offscreen target that is rendered on demand, so temporal modes and scaling stay game-only there (default off keeps editor screenshots unchanged). Combinations are normalised ( render.AASettings.Effective ): an upscaler replaces the AA mode ( fsr2 is itself the AA, fsr1 runs on the finished image), a scale below 100% with -upscale off and fxaa/smaa becomes fsr1, taa with a scale is a temporal upsample (history at display resolution). A missing device feature falls back to the built-in TAA (stderr says so); dlss / xess do the same, see below. Frame layout main pass (render resolution, projection jittered by Halton(2,3)) -> aa-velocity (+ object velocity) -> (upscaling) bloom / exposure / DoF + motion blur at the RENDER resolution, DoF result feeds the HDR stage -> HDR stage: taa | fsr2 | stub (render -> display resolution, before the tone mapping; fsr2 sanitises NaN / Inf first) -> (native temporal) bloom / exposure / DoF + motion blur at the display resolution -> composite (display resolution; samples the bloom bilinearly) -> LDR stage on the display-encoded image: fxaa | smaa | easu(fsr1) | bilinear, then rcas sharpening -> HUD and canvas at native resolution, over the result Without anything to do after the composite the composite writes the swapchain directly (as before); otherwise it writes ldr (RGBA8 UNORM, display encoded) and the LDR stage writes the swapchain. GPU timestamps: aa-velocity , taa , fsr2-* , fxaa , smaa-edges/weights/blend , easu , rcas , upscale-blit , hud . Velocity and jitter The projection of the scene UBO ( S.vp ) is jittered by render.Jitter (Halton 2,3, 8*(display/render)^2 phases like FSR 2); S.vpU is the unjittered matrix, S.prevVP the previous unjittered one, S.invVPJ the inverse of the jittered one. Every pipeline that reads S.vp (terrain, water, glass, rain, scene meshes, sprites) is jittered for free. post_vel.frag writes, per render pixel, rg = previous uv - current uv of the unjittered surface point (world position from the depth buffer and invVPJ , projected with vpU and prevVP ): exact for static geometry, whatever the camera does. CPU twin and unit test: render.VelocityUV , TestVelocityReprojectionStaticScene (error 0.018 px, float32 depth). a holds the view depth in the previous camera (disocclusion test), b the reactive mask. Moving scene meshes (hybrid frames, rworld.Draw.Entity ): shaders/vel_mesh.vert draws each opaque mesh with its current and its previous model matrix (remembered per entity) into velocity-objects , depth tested against the main pass; the velocity pass prefers it. Masked and custom-shader materials keep the camera velocity. Renderer.RegisterVelocityPass is the hook for other draw paths (the dynamic voxel bodies of dynvox.go : TODO, register a function that draws them with the vel_mesh contract). Animated vertices: wind sway (at most 7 cm) and water waves are not in the velocity (their amplitude is below the variance clip); water, glass and rain/snow are flagged reactive instead. The reactive mask is the colour difference between the scene copy (taken before the water, glass and rain) and the final HDR image, so the copy is also taken for glass and precipitation when the frame is temporal. Water without a scene copy (nothing transparent in view) needs none. Mip LOD bias of upscaled rendering: render.MipLODBias = log2(render/display) - 1 (temporal) or log2(render/display) (spatial) on the block textures and scene meshes. Robustness Camera cuts. A teleport, respawn or scene load must not blend with the old view: Renderer.ResetHistory() , app.FrameState.CameraCut and an automatic detection (translation above 24 blocks, yaw or pitch above 75 degrees, FOV above 25 degrees between two frames) drop the history for that frame (TAA ignores it, FSR 2 clears its images). Unit test TestAACameraCutDetection , GPU check aa-cut ( ResetHistory really drops a converged history). The editor viewport has no history (offscreen, non-temporal), so its camera jumps need no hook. Failures. A configuration whose setup fails (injected in the GPU test with fsr2TestFail ) is not retried every frame: the post state is rebuilt native, or the HDR stage falls back to the built-in TAA for any FSR 2 / DLSS / XeSS setup error (also a device without subgroup quad operations or storage image formats). AntiAliasingActive() and AntiAliasingStage() report what really runs; the warning is printed once per reason. NaN / Inf. post_taa.frag tests bit patterns (comparisons and max are undefined on NaN in SPIR-V) on the current samples, the history, the velocity and the stored depth; FSR 2 gets its colour through post_sanitize.frag . Captures. Renderer.Screenshot() re-renders with the jitter of the frame just drawn and does not advance the sequence, so a golden never depends on how many screenshots were taken before it. Tiny render sizes. The FSR 2 luminance pyramid image is at least 64 px (mips 4 and 5 exist) and its mip dimensions are clamped to 1; checked by the aa-tiny GPU test at 72x48. Modes FXAA : an original FXAA-style filter (contrast gate, edge walk, shift across the edge) on the tone mapped image. 0.13 ms at 1280x720 (idle), 0.9 ms at 2560x1440 in the shared run below. SMAA 1x : the reference implementation (edges, weights, blend; HIGH preset, area and search tables embedded) on the tone mapped image. TAA ( post_taa.frag ): Gaussian reconstruction of the 3x3 jittered samples (narrow at native, wide when upsampling), velocity of the closest sample, Catmull-Rom history, variance clipping in YCoCg (mean +- 1.25 sigma, inside the min/max box, clipped along the ray to the mean), Karis weighting c/(1+max c) , rejection by disocclusion (history view depth vs the reprojected depth), screen exit and the reactive mask, feedback 0.9. Sharpening is RCAS (strength 0.25 by default) after the tone mapping. FSR 1 : EASU then RCAS from the official ffx_fsr1.h , on the finished image, so the whole post chain runs at the render resolution. FSR 2 : AMD's official compute passes ( shaders/third_party/fsr2 , MIT, unmodified except two storage format qualifiers) driven by render/vulkan/fsr2.go , a Go port of the host side of ffx_fsr2.cpp (resources, constants, dispatch order, Lanczos and maximum-bias tables). It needs shaderStorageImageExtendedFormats and write-without-format (enabled when present) and subgroup quad operations. Its RCAS and auto-reactive passes are not used (Burrow's RCAS and velocity-pass mask replace them). Quality presets: quality 67%, balanced 59%, performance 50%. MSAA : not offered. The HDR frame is RGBA16F with depth read by the AO, scene copy, sun shaft and velocity passes: multisampled targets would need resolves of colour and depth and a second copy of every post input, cost 4x the bandwidth of the opaque pass, and do nothing for the cutout leaves or the shader aliasing (specular, water) that dominate this renderer. Upscaler interface (DLSS, XeSS) vulkan.Upscaler ( render/vulkan/aa.go ): Name , Temporal , Stage (HDR before the tone mapping, or LDR after), Setup(r, postState) , Record(*UpscaleInputs) , Close . A temporal HDR stage gets the jittered HDR colour, depth, velocity (uv, previous minus current), reactive mask, the jitter and frame index, a reset flag and writes Out at the display resolution; it adds its passes to the render graph ( rgRes.storage marks compute written images). taa and fsr2 implement it; -upscale dlss|xess select unavailableUpscaler , whose Setup fails with ErrUpscalerUnavailable so the renderer falls back to the built-in TAA. DLSS needs NVIDIA's NGX / Streamline SDK under NVIDIA's licence: it is not downloadable by this project and was not fetched. A backend wraps it (and XeSS) behind this interface once the SDK is obtained from the vendor. Untested on NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and Windows hardware. Tests render (no GPU): jitter sequence (range, centring, period, FSR 2 phase counts), JitterProjection , InvertMat4 , velocity reprojection of a static scene under camera motion and jitter, mip bias, render-scale / -aa / -upscale parsing, preset mapping, combination rules; assets/project (runtime fields), engine (live settings). render/vulkan : SPIR-V binding reflection of the FSR 2 passes, embedded tables; make render-test (GPU, validation on) renders a voxel scene with every mode and checks golden-ish thresholds (the mode changes the frame, stays within a mean abs difference of the native frame: fxaa/smaa/taa < 6, upscaled < 14-18; static scenes converge: TAA/FSR 2 change < 0.6 between frames; switching back restores the native frame exactly) with zero validation messages. Measurements (M2 Max, MoltenVK, 2560x1440, radius 12, no validation, -cam 0,58,100,0,8 , GPU ms) The machine was shared with other builds and GPU jobs during the run (the native baseline measured 12.4-14.3 ms against 5.4 ms idle in rendering.md ): compare rows with each other, not with older tables. Runs are repeatable to about 1 ms. medium main post total notes off ( -aa off ) 6.1-7.3 5.6 12.4-14.3 fxaa 7.7 6.6 15.4 fxaa 0.88, hud 0.40 smaa 6.7 10.4 18.4 edges 0.73, weights 1.59, blend 1.15, hud 1.04 taa 6.2-6.6 9.7 17.5-18.4 velocity 0.87, taa 1.64, rcas 0.76, hud 0.55 fsr1 quality 5.0 8.4 14.7 easu 1.25, rcas 0.80 fsr2 native 6.4 19.2 26.4 fsr2 quality 4.3-4.8 17.6 22.5-22.9 velocity 1.15, reactive 0.41, luma 0.33, reconstruct 0.57, depth clip 1.34, lock 0.65, accumulate 2.59, bloom at display res fsr2 performance 3.8 15.7 20.6 accumulate 2.57 ultra main post total off 14.5 6.1 21.4 taa 14.8 11.2 26.7 fsr2 native 14.9 18.2 33.8 fsr2 quality 9.1 16.3 26.2 fsr2 performance 7.5 16.4 24.7 FPS is 1000/total (GPU bound). When upscaling, bloom, exposure and DoF / motion blur now run at the render resolution before the upscale (re-measured, medium, same shared machine, GPU ms; main / post / total): off 6.0 / 6.5 / 13.4, taa 6.5 / 9.4 / 16.8, fsr2 quality 4.0 / 15.2 / 20.0 (was 22.5-22.9), fsr2 performance 3.5 / 14.2 / 18.5 (was 20.6). The upscale saves the main pass (ultra: 14.5 to 9.1 / 7.5 ms, sky and clouds dominate) but FSR 2 itself costs about 6-7 ms at 2560x1440 here (accumulate 2.4-2.5, depth clip 0.7-1.1, lock 0.3-0.6, reactive + sanitize 0.8, velocity 1.0), more than the main pass saves at medium; FSR 1 and the bilinear stretch are the cheap upscalers on this GPU, FSR 2 pays off where the main pass is expensive (ultra, clouds, heavy water) and on GPUs whose compute throughput is higher (untested). Default upscaler below 100% (re-measured, idle machine, -gen v2 -shaders high -retina -novsync , spawn view, 2560x1440, GPU ms) The 22.5 ms figures above were taken on a loaded GPU (other jobs running): on an idle M2 Max the same scene takes 7.5 ms native. Relative costs hold. config main post total notes native (taa) 4.0 3.5 7.5 velocity 0.23, taa 0.85, rcas 0.11 75% fsr1 (new default) 3.4 2.3 5.7 easu 0.47, rcas 0.15, no velocity / history 75% fsr2 ( -upscale fsr2 ) 2.5 4.1 6.6 accumulate 1.48, depth clip 0.45, reconstruct 0.15, luma 0.07, lock 0.09, reactive + sanitize 0.08 50% fsr1 3.0 2.1 5.2 easu 0.68 50% fsr2 1.7 3.5 5.3 accumulate 1.87 FSR 2 at 75% saves 1.5 ms of main pass and spends 0.6 ms more in post: it only barely beats native at medium and high, so FSR 1 is now the default there (always faster than native); FSR 2 stays the default at ultra, where the main pass is heavy. Trade-off: FSR 1 is spatial, so there is no temporal supersampling, and the preset's TAA is not stacked on it (as before for fxaa / smaa at a sub-native scale). In the sequences no ghost trail follows the foliage, the shoreline or the water curtain; the cost of the temporal modes is a slight softening of fine texture in motion (RCAS 0.25 compensates), and at 50% a visible thinning of leaf cut-outs. Limits Hybrid frames (scene components) are native resolution only; every AA mode works there. Cloud drift and rain streaks are not in the velocity (clouds are low contrast; rain is flagged reactive). The sun glint and SSR of the water are reactive too, so water is less anti-aliased than terrain. FSR 2 untested on AMD, NVIDIA, Intel, Windows; Metal (Apple Silicon) only.

Everything else is the standard library.

Assets Everything a game loads lives under the directories listed in asset_dirs of vox.project (default assets , scenes ). The database assets.DB scans those directories, gives every file a stable GUID stored in a <file>.vmeta sidecar (commit these: they keep references valid when you move or rename files), imports files lazily through typed loaders and tracks dependencies. Handles are typed and reference counted; a polling watcher drives hot reload (the editor and assets.Plugin use it; scripts recompile when their .wasm changes). kind extensions notes texture .png decoded with size caps, mip chain voxel model .vox (MagicaVoxel) read and write mesh .obj (+ .mtl ) bounded parser mesh .gltf / .glb (glTF 2.0) bounded parser; node hierarchy, skins, animations, see glTF models scene / prefab .voxscn / .prefab validated against the component schema world .voxworld terrain overlay, see concepts.md font .ttf rasterised with golang.org/x/image ; a Go font is embedded audio .wav parser only script .wasm loaded through the script runtime animation .anim JSON clips and state machines ( format burrow.anim , versioned), bounded and validated; hot reload replaces the clips of that file, see animation.md Every importer is pure and bounded: corrupt input is an error, never a panic. Commands burrow assets list [dir] # JSON: every asset, importer, dependencies burrow assets check [dir] # dry-run import of everything; exit 1 on problems burrow assets import [dir] # assign GUIDs (writes .vmeta) and import burrow assets atlas dir -o atlas.png -json atlas.json -gutter 1 -max 2048 # pack every PNG below dir These wrap burrowasset . Atlas packing is deterministic (sorted inputs, power-of-two size). In a running game burrowplay scans the project with a dry-run database (it never writes sidecars into your project) and registers every PNG under asset_dirs with the renderer under its project path, so {"render.material": {"texture": "assets/tex/brick.png"}} works; the builtin meshes are cube , sphere and plane . Scripts are resolved by project path. In burrowplay (windowed, headless and from a .voxpak ) the renderer's asset resolver is layered: the builtin meshes and project PNGs first ( rworld.MemAssets ), then every other project file through the assets.DB ( .obj meshes, .vox models, material JSON, <ref>.vert.spv / .frag.spv shader pairs) via engine.LayeredAssets and rworld/dbassets . Library users wire the same with engine.RenderWorldPlugin{Assets: &engine.LayeredAssets{Primary: mem, Lazy: ...}} . The models template shows an .obj , a .vox and a sprite. glTF models .glb and .gltf files (Blender, other DCC tools) import as one document: scenes and nodes (TRS or matrix), meshes with several primitives ( POSITION , NORMAL , TEXCOORD_0 , COLOR_0 , indices of any component type, triangles, strips and fans), materials ( baseColorFactor , baseColorTexture , emissive, alpha mode), skins and animations (translation, rotation, scale; LINEAR , STEP , and CUBICSPLINE read as its values without tangents). A .gltf may use base64 data URIs and .bin / image files in its own directory (never outside it, no .. ); copy the .bin into the project next to the .gltf . Files are untrusted: size, counts, accessor ranges, strides and indices are bounded and corrupt input is an error, never a panic. Sparse accessors, morph targets, cameras, lights and KHR extensions are ignored or refused. A render.mesh ref names the file and optionally a mesh (index or name) and a rigid part: assets/robot.glb the first mesh, all primitives merged assets/robot.glb#2 mesh 2 assets/robot.glb#Body the mesh named "Body" assets/robot.glb#Body:5 the rigid part of joint node 5 of that skinned mesh Vertex colours are kept; the material comes from the node's render.material (a mesh with several materials gets its first one when imported as a scene). Hot reload works like for .obj . Skinning is rigid, not smooth. The renderer has no GPU vertex skinning. Every triangle of a skinned mesh follows the one joint with the largest summed vertex weight, and that joint's scene node draws its triangles (expressed in the joint's local space). Animations move the joints, so the parts move as solid pieces; there is no blending between joints, so bends show seams. Smooth deformation, morph targets and animated weights are not supported. Import into a scene. In the editor, right-click a .glb / .gltf in the Content browser and choose Add glTF scene , or drag it into the viewport (Project > Import File... accepts .glb , .gltf and .bin ). Editor.ImportGLTFScene(path, parent) (package editor/core ) does it as one undo step: a root node named after the file with one child node per glTF node (same hierarchy and rest transforms; 1 metre is 1 scene unit, scale the root to fit), render.mesh + render.material on the nodes that draw something, and an anim.player on the root. The animations are written to <file>.anim next to the asset (clips named like the glTF animations, tracks transform.pos|rot|scale on node paths below the root) and open in the animation editor like any .anim . Embedded textures are saved next to the file as <file>_tex<N>.png|jpg . Existing files are never overwritten. Custom shaders burrowshader -write-include ./shaders writes the scene3d.glsl interface; burrowshader -I ./shaders my.vert my.frag compiles (with a glslc on the PATH, else with the compiler built into Burrow: nothing to install) and burrowshader -pair my verifies the pair. A material references it as "shader": "dir/my" . Shader assets ( .shader ) A project shader is one text file, shaders/<name>.shader : parameter annotations in comments plus #stage vertex|fragment sections of GLSL. The editor compiles it (glslc on the PATH when there is one, else the built-in compiler) whenever it is saved and writes <name>.vert.spv / <name>.frag.spv next to it (these are what a game loads and burrow build packs, and burrow build compiles every .shader of the project first and fails with file:line diagnostics; games never compile). A material without a #stage vertex section reuses the built-in mesh.vert . // @kind material // @param float glow = 0.25 range(0,1) "Glow" // @param color tint = #ffffff // @texture albedo "Albedo" #stage fragment layout (location = 0 ) in vec3 vWorld; layout (location = 1 ) in vec3 vNormal; layout (location = 2 ) in vec2 vUV; layout (location = 3 ) in vec4 vColor; layout (location = 0 ) out vec4 outColor; void main() { vec4 c = pc.base * vColor * texture(tex_albedo, vUV); outColor = vec4 (c.rgb * param_tint + vec3 (param_glow), c.a); } Do not write #version or include scene3d.glsl in a material: both are added, with one param_<name> define per parameter and tex_<name> per texture, and BW_OUT(rgb, a) , which writes a colour the way the target wants it (linear for sRGB / HDR targets). Parameter types: float int bool vec2 vec3 vec4 color color4 ; they pack in order into a 16-float block (vec3/vec4 never cross a 4-float row). The renderer uploads all 16 floats and binds up to 4 textures per material: floats 0..3 are the push-constant pc.params , floats 4..15 a per-draw dynamic uniform block ( layout(set = 3, binding = 3) ), texture slot 0 is uTex (set 1) and slots 1..3 are set 3 bindings 0..2 (a white image where the material sets none). Compile errors show as file:line ; the SPIR-V is then checked (reflection) against the Scene3D interface of the kind. The compiler Shaders compile with glslc when one is on the PATH ( $BURROW_GLSLC , the PATH, a cached download), else with glslang built for WebAssembly and embedded in the editor and burrow ( shadersys/glslang , run with wazero): offline, no install, every platform. Both produce the same interface (SPIR-V 1.0 for Vulkan 1.0, optimised). make glslang-wasm rebuilds the module reproducibly (wasi-sdk and glslang at pinned versions, checksum in glslang.wasm.sha256 , checked by a test). BURROW_GLSLC_URL + BURROW_GLSLC_SHA256 still download a glslc into the cache; BURROW_OFFLINE forbids it. Tools The editor has three full-screen tools (Content panel: double-click, or Tools): the shader editor ( .shader : code with GLSL highlighting, compile on idle, gutter marks and a clickable problem list, live preview, parameters from the annotations, built-in modules read-only with Override in project , templates unlit / lit_standard / toon / dissolve), the shader graph ( .shadergraph.json : nodes to GLSL, Convert to code ) and the material editor ( .material.json ). See materials.md . Overriding a built-in pipeline shader Every built-in vertex/fragment module is listed read-only in the Engine folder as builtin:<module> (for example builtin:mesh.frag ) with its GLSL source. Copy it to shaders/override/<module>.shader (keep its // @kind pipeline:<module> header), edit, save: it compiles to shaders/override/<module>.spv . At load (and on hot reload) the engine reflects the override and compares it with the built-in: same stage and entry, only the built-in's inputs, the same outputs, only the built-in's descriptors, no larger push block. A mismatch, a compile failure or a driver rejection logs the reason and keeps the built-in. Includes ( common.glsl , water.glsl ...) resolve to the engine's own files.

h: Every sound comes from an entity
Built-in sandbox ambience ( audio/audioamb , installed with Plugin.Hooks )
x: Audio Burrow's audio subsystem is frame domain : it never reads or writes simulation state, so it can never change a StateHash . The simulation can only request sounds ( audio.SoundEvent , deterministic per tick) and the frame domain turns requests into voices. Packages: audio (mixer, decoders, synthesis, backends; no engine dependency) and audio/audioplug (the engine plugin). Quick start Enable it in vox.project (the sandbox template does): "runtime": { "plugins": { "audio": true } } . This installs the mixer, the audio_source / audio_listener scene components and, in windowed runs, the sandbox ambience. In code: package main import ( "burrow-engine/audio" "burrow-engine/audio/audioamb" "burrow-engine/audio/audioplug" "burrow-engine/engine" ) func main() { app := engine.New(engine.Options{Seed: 1 }) app.AddPlugin(&engine.ScenePlugin{}) app.AddPlugin(&audioplug.Plugin{Component: true , Backend: "null" , Hooks: []audioplug.Hook{audioamb.New()}}) // a deterministic gameplay system asks for a sound; the frame domain plays it app.AddFixedSystem( "bell" , func (c *engine.FixedContext) error { if c.Tick% 100 != 0 { return nil } return audioplug.Emit(c, audio.SoundEvent{Kind: audio.EvPlay, Sound: "assets/confirm.wav" , Bus: "ui" }) }) if err := app.RunHeadless( 300 ); err != nil { panic(err) } } Plugin.Component registers the scene components. The component registry is part of StateHash ; audio is off by default ( runtime.plugins.audio: true enables it, the ambience and music need it), and any .voxscn / .prefab of the project mentioning audio_source / audio_listener registers the components too (scanned once at build, so headless and windowed runs register the same set and a later scene never fails with "unknown component"). audio: false together with such a scene is a build error. The editor always registers them (like character ), so its document hash differs from a runtime that does not use audio. Backend is auto (a sound device if one opens, else silent), device or null ; the environment variable BURROW_AUDIO=null forces silence and BURROW_AUDIO_DEVICE=<id> picks the output (the editor's Audio tool sets it from Output > Device ). Mixer model concept details buses sfx (default), music , ambient , ui , all summed into master . Volume 0..4, mute per bus. ducking DuckRule{Source, Target, Gain, Attack, Release} : while a voice plays on Source, Target is lowered. Default: UI lowers music (0.6) and ambient (0.7). voices at most MaxVoices (default 32). A new sound outranks a playing one with a lower Priority , or an equal priority and a louder gain; the quietest lowest-priority voice is stolen (5 ms fade), otherwise Play returns ErrNoVoice . spatial listener position and orientation, distance attenuation ( inverse , linear , exponential , none ; min_dist , max_dist , rolloff ), constant-power stereo panning, optional doppler ( Plugin.Doppler ). Silent past max_dist (linear fade over the last 10%). occlusion sources with occlusion raycast through the voxel grid (each opaque solid block adds 0.35); the voice is low-passed (20 kHz down to 500 Hz) and attenuated up to 6 dB, smoothly. At most 12 rays per frame. music Mixer.PlayMusic(params, fade) crossfades; OGG files over 256 KiB on the music bus are decoded progressively. loops, one-shots Loop repeats seamlessly; one-shots free their voice at the end. Pitch resamples on the fly (linear). formats WAV (PCM 8/16/24/32, float 32/64, extensible, mono/stereo) and OGG Vorbis; Clip.Resample converts rates. The listener is, in order: the node of an audio_listener component (highest priority), the editor camera override, the active camera node, then the player camera. Positions use the engine convention (x right, y up, yaw 0 looks -Z). Every sound comes from an entity A sound is never "just played": it is emitted by an entity placed in the scene, and its mode says who hears it. mode who hears it position global every player none (plain stereo) local one player: the player field, 0 = the player that owns the entity (found by walking up to a player component), else the local player of the client none localized everyone, attenuated by distance (the default) the entity's world position plus an optional offset Each client decides for itself whether it is a listener ( audio.Audible , audioplug.Resolve ): a local sound aimed at another player is simply not played here. All of this is frame domain, so the StateHash never changes. This covers music, ambience, script and visual-script sounds, footsteps, block break / place / hit impacts and UI sounds. audio.SoundEvent.Entity is mandatory for EvPlay ( Validate rejects an entity-less play), Mode and Player choose the audience and X, Y, Z is the offset from the entity. Scene components audio_source : asset , bus , volume , pitch (0 = 1), loop , mode ( global|local|localized , default localized), player , spatial (deprecated alias: true = localized, false = global, only read when mode is empty; Source.MigrateMode rewrites it), autoplay , muted , min_dist , max_dist , rolloff , model , priority , occlusion . A source plays from its node position (it follows the node; velocity feeds the doppler). Editing volume/pitch/muted/position updates the live voice, changing the asset or the spatial settings restarts it. In the editor, sources sound only in play mode. A local source is silent on the clients of other players. audio_listener : priority . Both appear in the inspector through the component schema. Music and ambience are entities audio.music (prefab builtin:music.prefab ): mode ( local default, or global ), player , context (empty = automatic day / night / cave from the clock and the cover above the listener; or day , night , cave , menu or any custom music.<name> of the sound pack), sound (a project asset looped instead of the pack's music), volume , crossfade (seconds, 0 = the pack's), disabled . The sound pack's music scheduler (gaps, tracks, crossfade) runs on each client that is a listener of the entity. Several entities: the lowest entity id that this client hears wins. audio.ambient (prefab builtin:ambience.prefab ): mode , player , volume , and switches weather (rain, wind, thunder), water (streams and waterfalls scanned around the listener), lava , cave (random cave noises underground), disabled . player.sounds on the player prefab: overrides ( event , sound , volume , pitch ) replace single pack events ( step.grass , player.jump , block.break.stone , ui.click ...) for that player; an empty sound silences the event; mute silences the player's footsteps, impacts and UI sounds; pack is the project path of a sound pack folder ( sounds.json or the folder layout, no .. , relative) whose events replace the project's mapping for that player's own sounds (events it does not map keep the project's; overrides still win). Without the component the sound pack decides, as before. All three are scene-level data (like the env.* components): decoded in every scene, not part of the StateHash. New projects and the templates carry a Music and an Ambience node. With no audio.music / audio.ambient entity there is no music or ambience. Compatibility: a project whose scenes never mention these components keeps the old always-on music and ambience (also a packed game) until a scene gets such an entity; from then on the entities alone decide. burrow migrate turns the old scene.settings.music into a Music node with audio.music {context} ; a modal screen's music still picks the context of an automatic audio.music . Sound events from the simulation audioplug.Emit(fixedCtx, SoundEvent) (or scripts, below) sends the event with engine.SendFixed : one ordered list per tick, byte identical across replays, delivered to the frame domain as the audio.SoundEvent event type. Kinds: EvPlay , EvStop , EvSet , EvBus , EvStopAll , EvListener , EvMusic (host code only: scripts do not send it any more, see audio.music ). audio.MakeHandle(source, tick, seq) makes a deterministic handle so a later EvStop / EvSet can address the voice. With no audio plugin the events are ignored. Scripts Host functions in module vox (ABI additive, see script/ABI.md ): audio_play , audio_stop , audio_set , audio_bus , audio_music (removed: always DENIED , the music is the audio.music component of an entity), audio_listener . Breaking change: audio_play must name an entity in its options ( entity , self or another node); without one it fails with INVALID . Go SDK in sdk/burrowsdk/audio.go ( PlayOn(entity, name, SoundOpts) replaces AudioPlay / AudioPlayAt / AudioMusic ; SoundOpts.Mode , Player , Offset ): h, _ := burrowsdk.PlayOn(self, "assets/thunder.wav" , burrowsdk.SoundOpts{Bus: "ambient" , Volume: 0.8 , Offset: &[ 3 ] float32 { 10 , 5 , - 3 }}) burrowsdk.AudioSet(h, 0.4 , - 1 ) // quieter, pitch unchanged burrowsdk.AudioStop(h, 0.5 ) Built-in sandbox ambience ( audio/audioamb , installed with Plugin.Hooks ) rain loop from render.WeatherFX (rain intensity), wind loop from the wind speed and gusts, thunder on weather.ThunderEvent (placed at the strike bearing); flowing water: the fluid cells around the listener (17 x 9 x 17) set the loudness of a stream loop at their centroid; vertical liquid columns drive a waterfall loop; still water is silent; footsteps from the player controller every 2.1 blocks walked, on the ground only (never in fly mode), on the material of the block under the feet, and a landing thud; block break / place / hit sounds from the edits of the player. These are emitted by the player entity (the player node of this client): footsteps localized at its feet, impacts localized at the block (an offset from the player), UI sounds ( ui.click , ui.hover , ui.open , ui.close , ui.back , ui.error , ui.slider , ui.tick , sent as an audio.UIEvent by the game UI) local . The footsteps of the other players are derived from the motion of their nodes (a stepper per player id), so every client hears them without any network traffic. Audio.Emitted lists the last emissions (entity, event, mode, position) for tools and tests. Without a player node (a bare simulation) a legacy project plays them from the listener, any other client plays nothing. music, cave noises, lava, streams and the weather sounds run only for the audio.music / audio.ambient entity in effect for this client (see above). The hook plays nothing by default : its sounds come from a sound pack (below); an event the pack does not map is silent. Sound packs Burrow's game binaries ( burrowplay , Burrow.exe , voxel_sandbox ) embed a small default sound pack ( assets/sounds/default/ , ~6 MB, CC0 files from Kenney and Juhani Junkala, credits in its CREDITS.md ; -tags nosounds compiles it out): footsteps per material, block break / place / hit, jump / land, UI click, a cave creak and six calm music tracks. It is the base layer: a user pack overrides it per event (events the user pack does not map still play from the default). It also has rain, wind and thunder, flowing water and lava loops (original filtered noise, generated by assets/sounds/gen/weather.py ). Not covered yet, therefore silent: water splash / enter / exit (map them in your pack). -sounds off (or none , also in BURROW_SOUNDS and runtime.audio.pack ) disables every pack, the default one included. A user sound pack is a folder of your own .ogg (Vorbis) / .wav files on your machine that the game maps to engine events. You are responsible for the rights of the files you use. A pack is read at run time from where it is; it is never bundled into an export : burrow build refuses to pack a project whose asset folders contain a sounds.json or a .burrow folder, or that contain the configured pack folder (any of the four locations below), and scripts/dist-windows.sh and scripts/dist-engine-windows.sh ( make dist-all ) refuse to zip one. Keep the pack outside the project. A project that owns its pack can declare it with runtime.audio.default_pack (a project folder; its sounds.json is then allowed). Plain audio files in a project's own asset folders are never refused. Where the game looks, first match wins: -sounds <dir> ( voxel_sandbox , burrowplay ) environment variable BURROW_SOUNDS runtime.audio.pack in vox.project (absolute, ~/... , or relative to the project folder; a packed game ignores relative paths) ~/.burrow/sounds , if it exists voxel_sandbox needs -audio ; burrowplay needs runtime.plugins.audio: true (the sandbox template has it). runtime.audio (all optional): pack , music_gap_min / music_gap_max (seconds of silence between tracks, default 90..240), music_fade (3), music_volume (0.6). Folder layout (no sounds.json ) Without sounds.json the folder is read by convention (the folder itself, or a sounds/ subfolder). The numbers at the end of a file name are variants ( grass1.ogg , grass2.ogg ): step/grass1.ogg stone1.ogg wood1.ogg sand1.ogg gravel1.ogg snow1.ogg cloth1.ogg (wool1 also) -> step.<material>, block.hit.<material> (quiet) dig/stone1.ogg grass1.ogg wood1.ogg gravel1.ogg sand1.ogg glass1.ogg ... -> block.break.<material>, block.place.<material> liquid/swim1.ogg splash.ogg water.ogg (loop) lava.ogg (loop) -> step.swim, water.splash, fluid.water.flow, fluid.lava random/splash.ogg click.ogg -> water.splash, ui.click damage/hit1.ogg -> player.hurt ambient/cave/cave1.ogg cave2.ogg ... -> ambient.cave ambient/weather/rain1.ogg (loop) thunder1.ogg wind1.ogg (loop) -> ambient.rain, ambient.thunder, ambient.wind music/game/*.ogg (subfolders ok) -> music.day, music.night, music.cave (streamed) music/menu/*.ogg -> music.menu The table is data ( audio/soundpack/autodetect_table.go ): edit the rules to fit another naming scheme. Only .ogg and .wav are read. sounds.json When present it replaces the autodetect. Reloaded while the game runs (checked every 2 s; a broken file keeps the previous mapping and warns). { "version" : 1 , "fallback" : "none" , "music" : { "gap_min" : 120 , "gap_max" : 300 , "fade" : 4 , "volume" : 0.5 }, "materials" : { "my_custom_block" : "metal" , "red_*" : "cloth" }, "material_fallback" : { "cloth" : "grass" }, "events" : { "step.grass" : [ "step/grass1.ogg" , { "file" : "step/grass2.ogg" , "weight" : 2 , "volume" : 0.8 , "pitch" : [ 0.9 , 1.1 ] } ], "block.break.stone" : [ { "file" : "dig/stone1.ogg" , "attenuation" : { "ref_dist" : 3 , "max_dist" : 24 } } ], "ambient.rain" : [ "ambient/rain.ogg" ], "music.day" : [ { "file" : "music/a.ogg" , "stream" : true }, { "file" : "music/b.ogg" , "stream" : true } ] } } A variant is a file name or an object: file (relative path, slash separated), weight (default 1), volume (default 1), pitch ( [min, max] or [value] ), stream (decode progressively: use it for music), attenuation ( ref_dist , max_dist , rolloff , for sounds placed in the world). Events: step.<material> , block.break.<material> , block.place.<material> , block.hit.<material> (mining ticks), player.jump , player.land , player.hurt , water.splash , water.enter , water.exit , ambient.cave , ambient.rain , ambient.thunder , ambient.wind , fluid.water.flow , fluid.lava , ui.click , ui.hover , ui.open , ui.close , ui.back , ui.error , music.day , music.night , music.cave , music.menu . Materials: stone wood grass dirt sand gravel snow cloth glass metal water swim (plus your own). The material of a block comes from its name ( soundpack.MaterialOf : red_wool is cloth, oak_planks wood, sandstone stone, ...), overridden by materials (exact name or prefix* ). An event with no entry for a material tries material_fallback (default: dirt, snow, cloth -> grass; sand -> gravel; gravel, glass, metal, wood -> stone; swim -> water), then the plain family event ( step , block.break , ...). The default pack ships ui.click and small procedural sounds for ui.hover , ui.open , ui.close , ui.back , ui.error , ui.slider (a slider value change, at most one every 60 ms) and ui.tick (a choice stepper step), generated by go run ./assets/sounds/gen/uisounds into assets/sounds/default/sfx/ui_*.wav . A pack on top that does not map one of them keeps the default sound; a pack without a default underneath plays its ui.click softer and at a fixed pitch instead (map the event, even to nothing, to override). player.hurt and ui.click are mapped but nothing in the sandbox fires them yet (scripts and games can). Behaviour Variants are chosen by a seeded RNG per event (weighted, never the same file twice in a row). This is frame domain: it never touches the simulation or StateHash . Footsteps: one per 2.1 blocks walked (distance, not frames), on the ground, never in fly mode; swimming strokes in water; jump, landing, water enter / exit. Block sounds come from the edits of the player (seen as changes under the crosshair); hit ticks play while the attack button is held on a block. Music: a random track of the context (cave when under a roof of 6+ solid blocks, night / day from the weather clock, day otherwise), faded in and out, one track at a time, a random silence of music_gap_min..max seconds between tracks, a context change fades the track out. ambient.cave plays at random (25..80 s) underground. Rain, thunder and wind follow the weather; water and lava loops follow the nearby liquid. "Dark" is not tested: the block light is renderer-only. Limits: sounds.json 1 MiB, 1024 events, 256 variants per event, 4096 in total; 32 MiB per file (64 MiB streamed), decoded clips of at most ~2 minutes (use stream ), the OGG/WAV decoder limits above; paths with .. , absolute paths, \ , drive letters and every symbolic link are refused; the autodetect reads at most 8192 files, 6 levels deep. Decoded clips live in a 64 MiB LRU cache and are decoded on first use. BURROW_SOUNDS_TRACE=1 prints every resolved sound on stderr (with the null backend, BURROW_AUDIO=null , it shows what would play). Music contexts The audio.music component ( context empty) picks the music context day , night or cave ; a non-empty context fixes it. Two frame-domain requests override the automatic choice, when the sound pack has music.<context> (otherwise day/night continues): the music field of the running scene's scene.settings component, and the topmost modal game UI screen's music ( (*uiplug.GameUI).ModalMusic() , which wins over the scene). "menu" plays music.menu ( music/menu/*.ogg ). The time of the env.time node also decides day or night for the music. The request is the engine.SceneRuntime.Music resource field, set by internal/game . Backends and testing audio.NewBackend(kind, rate) : device plays through miniaudio via gen2brain/malgo (public domain; CoreAudio, WASAPI, PulseAudio / ALSA) in builds with cgo (the editor and the game), which lists the outputs ( audio.OutputDevices ) and opens the chosen one ( audio.SetPreferredDevice , or live with the backend's SetOutputDevice ; a device that is gone falls back to the system default). Builds without cgo (servers, tools) keep ebitengine/oto v3 (Apache-2.0), which only plays on the system default. null renders nothing until you call Pump . Mixer.Render is deterministic, so tests render offline: build a mixer, Play , Update , then RenderFrames(n) and compare with a golden WAV ( audio/testdata , refresh with go test ./audio -run Golden -update ; the comparison tolerates 3 LSB because FMA differs between CPUs). Real sound output cannot be verified in CI. Editor and agents Tools > Audio: a full-screen tool like the model editor. Mixer : one channel strip per bus (Master, Music, Sound effects, Ambient, UI) with the voice count, a level meter ( BusInfo.Level , the peak of the last ~100 ms), a fader in dB (+6 to silence; double-click resets to 0 dB), Mute and Solo ( Mixer.SetBusSolo : while any sub-bus is soloed the others are silent; a muted bus stays muted; the master cannot be soloed; Alt+click Mute solos; solo is a session tool and is not saved). Sounds and Audio settings: the project's .wav / .ogg files with a play/stop preview (on the ui bus), a bus hint and the length ( Audio.Duration ), and the output (backend, voices, sample rate). Stop all stops every voice. In the asset browser, a .wav / .ogg selection shows a play button; double-click auditions it. The mix (bus volumes and mutes) is saved in vox.project under settings.audio_mix ( audio.Mix : {"volumes":{"music":0.5}, "muted":["ui"]} , only what differs from the default) and applied when the tool opens; every edit is one undo step. To start a game with the saved mix set audioplug.Plugin.Mix . MCP tool editor_audio ( state , list , play , stop , bus , music , render ): in a headless editor render {ms} renders the mixer offline and reports peak and rms , so an agent can check a sound without a speaker. A null backend has nobody pulling audio, so the plugin advances the mixer with a virtual clock ( Mixer.Discard ) every frame: one-shots end and stopped voices are freed in headless runs too. Robustness Sound loads are bounded: at most 8 uncached disk reads per frame ( ErrBusy , retried next frame), a 256-entry negative cache whose entries expire after 3 s ( Audio.Invalidate(name) forgets one sooner), compressed music kept once for streaming, one EvMusic per frame and none for the music already playing. OGG output is limited to 2000 frames per input byte. Non-finite or overflowing geometry is inaudible rather than poisoning the mix, samples are clamped to +-8 and denormals flushed. State reports the backend and its device error. Voice chat Proximity voice chat between players is a separate plugin built on this mixer: each remote speaker is a spatial stream voice on the sfx bus, placed at the speaker's position and fading to silence at the voice radius. See Voice chat . Limits Mono or stereo only; no HRTF, reverb zones or streaming WAV. Decoders are bounded ( audio.MaxFrames ) and never panic on hostile input (fuzzed). Decoding a clip happens on first use in the frame thread.

h: Design: what is the state of a block?
x: Block shapes (stage B2) Phase 2 of the Minecraft block set: the blocks that are not full cubes. B1 ( blocks.md ) gave 338 cubes; B2 adds slabs, stairs, walls, fences, fence gates, doors, trapdoors, pressure plates, buttons, carpets, snow layers, glass panes and iron bars, torches, ladders, vines, cross plants (flowers, grasses, saplings, mushrooms, corals), two-block tall plants, the cactus and the lily pad: 254 palette items, 1109 registry blocks. It is opt-in ( runtime.blocks: "shapes" ). Design: what is the state of a block? Constraint: ids, hashes, goldens, journals and worlds of every project without the opt-in must not change, and the registry must not explode. Options evaluated: option chunk format / hash / journal / undo / .voxworld verdict a state field stored beside the 16-bit id (id + 4..8 bits) every layer changes: chunk palette/RLE, StateHash overlay, Change / SetBlock , diff, snapshot, journal JSON, undo, .voxworld , wire protocols rejected: touches the frozen formats of all projects one id per stored state, generated from compact data nothing changes: BlockID stays uint16 , a SetBlock is still (pos, id) , the palette-compressed chunk, hash, journal, undo and .voxworld carry it as any block chosen derived state stored too (fence connections: 16 states, stair corners: 5 shapes, wall posts) 16-fold or 5-fold id growth for no information the neighbours do not already hold rejected: derived at meshing/collision time Chosen model: Stored state = registry id. The states a player chooses (stairs: 4 facings x 2 halves; slab: bottom/top; door: 4 facings x 2 halves x 2 hinges x open; trapdoor, gate, torch, button, ladder, vine, snow layers 1..7, tall plant lower/upper) are separate registry blocks. 1109 ids = 1.7 % of the 65536 space, assigned after the extended set, append-only ( blockset/testdata/shape_ids.golden fails when one moves). The id of a state is a pure function of the order of blockset/shapes.json (the items, generated, appended alphabetically) and of the frozen state order of package shape (loops in shape/catalog.go ). Names. The default state keeps the bare item name ( oak_stairs : facing north, bottom), every other state is oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top] (props in the family's fixed order). So set_block , scripts, MCP and the palette work with the bare names; blockset.Resolve / StateName map (item, props) to a block. Derived state is never stored. Stair corner shapes (straight, inner left/right, outer left/right; the vanilla rule), fence/wall/pane connections (a 4-bit mask; walls also decide their post) are computed from the horizontal neighbours by shape.Model.Key , in the mesher (from the padded chunk), in collision and in raycasts (from the reader). It is a pure function of the neighbours, so it is canonical; an edit already re-meshes the chunks around it (the streamer re-meshes the neighbours of a changed voxel), so connections and corners update with no extra bookkeeping. Hash/format impact. Zero without the opt-in: no block is registered, voxel.Block.Shape is omitted from JSON when 0, Registry.HasShapes() is false and every shape-aware path falls back to the old code. With the opt-in a world is a normal world of more ids: snapshot, restore, replay, undo and VerifyReplay need nothing new. Existing ids that change model. Under shapes the generator-v2 plants ( flower_red/yellow/white/blue , mushroom_red/brown , tall_grass , dead_bush ) and cactus keep their id and become cross plants / a cactus ( Registry.Update : not solid, fragile; cactus solid). Worlds are unchanged, only the model of the cell changes. Behaviour change when moving a v2 world from extended to shapes . The StateHash does not hash the registry, and Registry.Update changes attributes of existing ids: the v2 plants ( flower_* , mushroom_* , tall_grass , dead_bush ) stop being solid cubes (they become walk-through and fragile) and the cactus stops being opaque. The world data and its hash are identical but collision, raycast and rendering are not: the physics of an existing world changes with the level. Registry fingerprint (guard). voxel.Registry.Fingerprint() hashes, in id order, name, Solid, Opaque, Fragile, Liquid and Shape of every block. It is not part of any state hash (existing hashes and goldens are unchanged). The first journal entry carries it ( registry_id ) and sim.ReplayWith refuses a journal recorded with another registry ("replay registry mismatch"); snapshot restore compares every block of the registry and reports both fingerprints. Journals written before the field skip the check. Two-block plants and water. Flowing water destroys the fragile lower half; blockset.InstallShapes (used by the shapes level) adds the shapes.support system, which removes the upper halves left floating. Only overlay chunks (where water wrote) are examined, plus the y=0 layer of the chunk above each of them (halves split across a vertical chunk border; that chunk may be base terrain). A chunk is examined every 32 ticks at a phase that is a pure function of its position, so the work per tick is bounded and the result depends only on the tick and the hashed world (replay and snapshot restore remove the same cells at the same ticks; the system is not journaled). Maximum latency 32 ticks (1.6 s). Measured cost: 13.9 ms per tick in a synthetic pathological case (3750 overlay chunks each holding an upper half, radius 12 x 6 layers), about nothing in a world with no overlay chunk. fluid/ is untouched. Geometry data (package shape ) shape.Model is one stored state: family, decoded props ( Facing , Top , Open , Right , Layers ), a Derive kind and Variants (1, 5 for stairs, 16 for connections). A shape.Variant holds the collision boxes , selection boxes (when different: fences select 1.5 high, flowers a small box, ladders a thin one) and the render quads , in sixteenths of a block. Quads are generated from boxes by shape.BoxQuads (faces and parts of faces hidden inside or behind sibling boxes are removed, so there are no coplanar duplicates: TestNoCoplanarOverlap ) or authored (cross planes, ladders, vines, double sided). Each quad carries the texture slot (which face texture of the block), the lighting face, the UV window (texture coordinates are the block-space position of the quad: a slab side shows the lower half of the image, a torch the middle pixels: no stretching) and Cull , the cell face it lies on. Variant.Cover is a 16x16 bitmap per face of the area covered with opaque material (used for culling). Tables are Go data built at init in a fixed order (no map iteration), the items are JSON. Meshing mesh.Mesh.Fine (set on both meshes of a chunk that contains at least one shaped cell): vertex positions in sixteenths (0..512, int16) and UVs in sixteenths of a texture; merged cube quads are capped at 15 blocks so a UV still fits the byte of the 16-byte vertex. Chunks without shaped blocks are bit-identical to before. Cubes: a shaped neighbour never occludes (AO unchanged), but hides the cube's face when its CoverAll (the part covered by every derived variant) covers the face. Shaped cells: appended in z, y, x order to the transparent mesh (alpha-tested like leaves; glass panes go to the blended range by name). A quad on a cell face is dropped when the neighbour is an opaque cube or a shaped block whose covered bitmap contains the quad. So a slab does not hide the cube above it, a stair hides half of what is behind it, two slabs side by side lose their touching faces. Light: block light of a shaped quad is the light of its cell (and of the open neighbour for boundary quads); shaped cells are non-opaque for the flood fill, so torch light and sky pass. Tint: the biome tint of the cell column applies to grass, ferns, tall grass, vines and foliage plants through the usual tint/biome tables. AO is 3 (none) on shaped quads and shaped blocks do not occlude neighbours' AO: documented limitation.
