Files Ctrl+N / Ctrl+O / Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Shift+S new / open / save / save as scene ( .voxscn ) World menu save / load / clear the .voxworld overlay Project menu new project, open vox.project , rescan, import assets Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y undo / redo the focused document (a drag, a stroke or a paste is one step; 1000 steps / 64 MiB each; see Undo ) Ctrl+D, Delete, H duplicate, delete, hide mesh Ctrl+P command palette: fuzzy search over every action Undo: one history per document Like Blender or Unity, each document has its own undo history, save point and dirty dot. Scene : nodes, voxels, world, and every tool that edits the scene (animation, character, cameras, levels, environment, audio). Its steps are journaled engine commands, so replay and agents work as before. Stop (after Play) restores the scene history. Model, texture, particle effect, game UI : one history each, kept while the editor is open. Their steps are not journaled. Closing the editor panel drops its history; loading another asset into the editor is itself a step of that history. Code, shader, material, prefab and block editors keep their own text or draft undo. Which one Ctrl+Z uses : the full-screen tool, else the panel under the pointer, else the scene. The Undo / Redo buttons of a tool act on that tool's document only; a tool window (own process) has just its document. Dirty and save points : saving marks the document's history as saved; undoing past that point makes it dirty again, redoing back makes it clean. Saving never creates a step in another history. Across documents : an operation touching two documents is a step of the document it changes (a model or texture saved in its editor just rewrites the file, the scene and the characters using it pick it up through hot reload; "create prefab from selection" is one scene step). Undo of one document never replays the other. Agents : editor_undo / editor_redo take doc ( scene by default, model , texture , particles , gameui ); edits made with editor_model / editor_texture are undone with doc=model / doc=texture . Play, Simulate and Stop Play (Ctrl+Shift+P, the toolbar's main button) runs the game as the players will: burrow run on the project, in its own window, with the player, the controller, the HUD, the game UI, the captured mouse, the start level and the saves. The game reads the files on disk, so Play first saves the scene and every asset editor with unsaved changes (an untitled scene asks for a path). Pressing the button again (or Stop) closes the game window; a crash shows its last lines in a toast. From a source checkout ( go run ./cmd/burrowedit ) the game is built from the same sources first, so it always matches the editor. Game panel. Play opens the Game panel (View > Panels): the editor starts the game with -debug-listen 127.0.0.1:0 and a random token in the environment ( BURROW_DEBUG_TOKEN , never logged), reads the one stdout line debuglink: listening <addr> and connects. The panel then shows the game's live scene tree, the components of the selected node as JSON (refreshed twice a second), the game's console (filter by level, Follow, Clear) and a stats line (tick, fps, node count, StateHash ). It is read only. The game only listens on loopback, refuses a wrong token and bounds every message (a tree is cut at 5000 nodes); it never writes to the simulation, so the StateHash is the same with or without the link. Without Play (or once the game exits) the panel shows "Press Play to run the game". A game started by hand can serve the same link: BURROW_DEBUG_TOKEN=<16+ chars> burrowplay -debug-listen 127.0.0.1:0 <project> . Play This Scene (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+P, or the arrow next to Play) starts the game on the scene open in the editor instead of the project's start scene ( burrow run <project> -- -scene scenes/x.voxscn ); the scene must be saved inside the project. Simulate (Ctrl+Alt+P, the lightning button) runs scripts and physics inside the editor's viewport to inspect them: the editor takes a snapshot, runs the simulation and looks through the first active render.camera node. Esc or Stop restores the snapshot: the StateHash after Stop equals the hash before Simulate, and edits made meanwhile are discarded. Pause and Step one tick are in the Play menu. While simulating and the pointer is over the viewport, the keyboard and mouse buttons are routed to the game's input map, so scripts see the same actions as in burrowplay (see scripting.md ); Esc always stops. Agent control The editor exposes editor_* MCP tools so an AI agent and a human edit the same document: burrowedit -headless -agent stdio # JSON-RPC lines on stdin/stdout, CPU screenshots, no GPU burrowedit -headless -agent unix:/tmp/voxed/ed.sock # unix socket (mode 0600, directory 0700) burrowedit -agent unix:/tmp/voxed/ed.sock # windowed: human and agent edit the same document burrow agent --stdio mygame # same as the first line, opening the project File access of the agent is confined to the open project (and -agent-allow directories). See agents.md . Terrain helpers for placing things: editor_ground_at {x,z,ignore_foliage} returns the top solid block of a column (plants and liquids are skipped, stand_y is where feet go); editor_find_view {near:[x,z],radius,height,look_at,apply} finds a high camera position with an unobstructed line of sight to the target and returns position, yaw and pitch ( apply moves the editor camera); editor_place_on_ground {node,offset} snaps a scene node onto the terrain as one undoable step. Asset and node pickers in the Inspector Reference fields use one picker: a field showing the current value that opens a searchable list of the built-in assets and the project's files of the right kind, with icon buttons beside it (open the asset, make a variant). game.mode has a player prefab picker (only prefabs holding a player component; Create variant... makes a variant of the current one and selects it), node pickers for spawn and spawns , an input map picker, dropdowns for the enums and the respawn and kill plane fields in their own groups. game.ui has one picker per slot. Materials, particle effects and sounds ( material_ref , particle_emitter.asset , audio_source.asset ) use the same picker. See prefabs and built-in assets . Assets: thumbnails, drag into the viewport, hot reload The Content browser shows a thumbnail grid (List toggles the table): png (scaled), .vox (isometric render), .obj (lit preview), .voxscn / .prefab (top view of the node positions). Thumbnails are generated lazily by at most 2 background workers (queue bounded at 64), are deterministic, and are cached on disk in <project>/.burrow-cache/thumbs/<sha256 of kind+content>.png (directory 0700 ); an edited file gets a new key. Drag an asset into the viewport: .vox stamps its voxels (nearest palette colour -> solid block) with a ghost preview on the face under the cursor ( R rotates 90 degrees, Esc cancels, one undo step) as a voxel group node (see below); .glb / .gltf adds the whole glTF scene (nodes, rigid skin parts, a .anim file, see assets.md ); .obj creates a MeshInstance node (+ Material from the MTL); .png a billboard Sprite; .voxscn / .prefab instantiate under a node named after the file at the cursor (one undo step). Mesh, sprite and scene assets are referenced by their project path; the editor resolves them through the project's assets.DB ( render/rworld/dbassets ) behind the procedural assets, so the viewport, picking and saved scenes agree. Voxel groups A voxel group is a scene node (component voxel.group ) that owns a set of world voxels: every .vox stamp creates one, and Voxels > Group Region Blocks ( Ctrl+G ) turns the blocks of the box selection into one, which is how structures built before groups existed become objects. Clicking one of its blocks selects the node. Move or turn it with the gizmo or the Transform fields (whole cells; the rotation snaps to quarter turns about the node corner on any axis, also under a turned parent; scale is ignored), or Voxels > Rotate voxel group 90° : the blocks it covered come back and it is written at the new place. Delete it and what it covered comes back; Duplicate stacks a copy on it (move the copy away to see both). Edits made inside it with the voxel tools travel with it; a broken block leaves the group. Bake (Inspector, or Voxels > Bake Voxel Group ) drops the record and leaves the blocks as plain terrain. The blocks always stay in the world ( .voxworld ), so games, collisions, networking and worlds from earlier releases are unchanged: the component is only the editor's record (palette by block name, owned cells and covered cells, run-length encoded). Opening a scene never rewrites the world. A scene that uses voxel.group or layer needs this release or later to open. Layers Edit > Layers Panel opens the Layers tab beside the Outliner. Type a name and press New layer (the selection joins it); each row has an eye (hide in the editor viewport only), a lock (not pickable; the voxels of its voxel groups cannot be changed by the voxel tools), the node count, Select , Move the selection here , Rename and Delete (nodes stay). The Inspector's Layer field moves the selection to a layer. A node joins a layer through the layer component, saved in the scene so a team shares it; a child without one inherits its parent's layer. The layer list, visibility and lock live in the editor sidecar .<scene>.voxscn.editor (which also holds the root order), never in the game. A hidden layer's voxel groups disappear from the viewport too (render-only mask: the world, collisions and the ray-traced lighting still hold the blocks) and the pointer goes through them. MCP: editor_voxel_group (list, info, create from a box, stamp a .vox , bake) and editor_layers (list, create, rename, delete, hide, show, lock, unlock, assign, select). Hot reload: the project is polled about once a second. Changed textures, meshes and voxel models refresh in the viewport (handle versions bump), .wasm scripts are re-registered and bound scripts re-pinned (journaled script_module_changed ), every event is logged to the console, and a change of the open scene file (not our own save) asks "Reload from disk / Keep my version" (the prompt says whether there are unsaved edits). World and project settings Every scene is a world of its own. Save (Ctrl+S) writes the scene and its world next to it: scenes/main.voxscn keeps its seed, generator and voxel edits (blocks, fine water) in scenes/main.voxworld . Opening a scene switches the terrain to its world, and New scene starts on the project terrain without edits. The game ( burrow run ) loads the world of its start scene. Older projects kept every edit in runtime.world ( world.voxworld ): the default scene still loads it until it is saved with a world of its own. Dragging a voxel model ( .bmodel , .vox ) into the viewport places it as a free object (a node drawing it with render.voxmodel ; R turns it a quarter); it writes no blocks. To place blocks, use a prefab holding a voxel group. Double-clicking a compiled script ( .wasm ) opens its Go source ( scripts/<name>/main.go ) in the Script panel, or in the external editor when Preferences > Prefer external editor is on. Project > World settings rebuilds the base terrain with a new seed and generator parameters (heightmap or flat); the voxel edits are kept (re-applied on the new base) or discarded. The whole operation is a journaled command ( editor_world_regen ) and one undo step that restores the previous terrain and overlay. Loading a .voxworld made with another seed is refused unless you choose Adopt seed from file (regenerates the base with the file's seed, then loads its edits, one undo step; the generator parameters must still match). The load radius applies immediately ( Apply radius , or with Regenerate; VoxelWorld.SetRadius : growing streams the new ring, shrinking unloads chunks beyond radius+2); tick the checkbox to also save it to vox.project . Project > Project Settings edits vox.project (name, window title/size, radius, fly/walk, start position, texture pack, plugins, input map) with inline validation errors; nothing is written until the form validates. Scene editing Several nodes can be selected (Ctrl/Shift in the hierarchy or Ctrl+click in the viewport). Editing a transform or a component field in the Inspector applies only that field to every selected node as one undo step; fields whose values differ are listed as "mixed". Reparenting (drag onto a node) keeps the world transform by default (Preferences: keep local); dropping between rows reorders siblings, and Alt+Up / Alt+Down move the selection among its siblings (journaled as scene_reorder ). Undo of a delete restores the EntityRefs from outside the subtree that the delete cleared. The hierarchy rows have an eye (hide the mesh) and a lock (not pickable in the viewport). Roots can be reordered too (drag, Alt+Up / Alt+Down): that order is editor-only and lives in the hidden .<scene>.voxscn.editor sidecar next to the scene, so the .voxscn (sorted by name, hashed and replicated) never changes. A scene without that file lists its roots in creation order. View > Slice view hides everything above a height (slider, Alt+wheel over the viewport, Y<=N badge); it is editor-only state, not in the journal. Shift+F1 lists the shortcuts from the real binding table; keybindings are remapped in Preferences, checked for conflicts as an input.Map and exportable to keymap.json (the same JSON format the game loads). Feature windows (View menu) Weather, Audio, Cameras and Levels are docked panels (Tools menu): they tab with the others and stay open while you work in the viewport, where their effect shows. Particle editor, the Game UI editor and the model and texture editors are windows of their own. Each one works on the open project and needs its plugin (a message says when it is missing): window what it does page Weather (panel) read and set the deterministic weather, day clock and seasons weather.md Audio (panel) mixer buses, mutes, audition of the built-in sounds audio.md Particle editor (panel) edit an effect with a live preview, curves and a gradient particles.md Cameras (panel) list the rigs, switch, shake, live preview cameras.md Game UI editor (panel) design a .ui.json screen visually: outline, canvas, properties, preview values game-ui.md Levels (panel) open, save a region as a level, mark spawns and zones levels-saves.md Model editor..., Texture editor... voxel model and pixel-art texture editing modeling.md The shader level, anti-aliasing and ray tracing of the viewport follow the -shaders , -aa and -rt flags of burrowedit ( render options ); lighting is described in lighting.md . Help F1 (or Help > Documentation ) opens the built-in documentation: guides, tutorials and the reference generated from the code, with search, history and links. With the pointer over a panel it opens that panel's page; every panel header has a ? button, and hovering a component or field in the Inspector shows its description. Shift+F1 is the shortcut cheat sheet. See Reading the docs in the editor . Security notes The in-app file dialog is confined to the project folder; "Browse outside project..." (and the import / open project pickers) ask first in a modal that lists the path. Agent file writes and reads are fd-based ( openat with O_NOFOLLOW from a root fd, temp file + renameat ), so a directory swapped for a symlink between the check and the use cannot make a write land outside the project (tests with a racing goroutine and FuzzConfineRace ). Known gaps Play routes letters, digits, Space, Shift, Ctrl and mouse buttons only. The streaming load radius can be changed live in World settings. Details: editor/README.md .

Game UI gameui is the UI toolkit of games (HUD, menus, inventories, dialogs), distinct from the editor toolkit in ui . A screen is data: a .ui.json document built into a retained widget tree. It is frame domain ; UI input reaches the simulation only through journaled commands, so replays work. Packages: gameui (documents, widgets, layout, focus, themes, localisation, world labels; no engine dependency), gameui/uiplug (the engine plugin) and render/canvas (drawing: the Vulkan overlay and the CPU rasterizer share it). Quick start vox.project : "runtime": { "plugins": { "gameui": true } } . Every *.ui.json of the project is loaded (named after the file), or list them: "gameui": { "screens": [ { "name": "hud", "path": "ui/hud.ui.json" } ], "locale": "en", "scale": 1 } . The inbox that carries UI events to the simulation is simulation state; the plugin is off by default ( runtime.plugins.gameui: true enables it). examples/camera_ui_demo is a complete game (HUD, pause menu, inventory): { "version" : 1 , "theme" : "hud" , "root" : { "type" : "stack" , "layout" : "none" , "children" : [ { "type" : "panel" , "anchor" : "top-left" , "offset" : [ 8 , 8 ], "layout" : "stack_v" , "children" : [ { "type" : "bar" , "bind" : "hp" , "bind_max" : "hp_max" , "size" : [ 150 , 16 ], "format" : "{v}/{max}" } ] }, { "type" : "grid" , "id" : "bag" , "anchor" : "bottom" , "columns" : 9 , "slots" : 9 , "bind" : "hotbar" , "action" : "inv" , "sim" : true } ] } } a.AddPlugin(&uiplug.Plugin{Docs: []uiplug.Doc{{Name: "hud" , Path: "ui/hud.ui.json" }}, Read: readProjectFile}) ui := uiplug.Res(c).UI ui.Values.SetNum( "hp" , 14 ) // frame code binds values directly ui.Show( "pause" ) // modal screens take the focus and the input Documents A .ui.json document: version 1, name , theme , styles , atlases , strings , locale , and for screens modal , layer (draw order), hidden (loaded but not shown), cancel (action of the cancel key) and focus (id focused when a modal screen opens). gameui.Decode rejects unknown fields, trailing data, unknown types, anchors, themes and styles, and every rejection names the valid choices ( unknown theme color "accnt" (valid: text, text_dim, …) , unknown field "colour" (valid: base, colors, font_size, radius) , …); limits: 512 KiB, 2048 widgets, depth 16, 512 children per node, strings 4096 bytes, 4096 items, 32 screens, 4096 localisation strings. widget purpose main fields label text; wraps when size[0] is set text / key , font_size , bold , align , fg , bind image an icon icon : builtin:<lucide or g-heart, g-sword, g-shield, g-coin, g-potion, g-block> , <atlas>:<n or name> , a .png path (the full builtin icon list is in the editor_gameui MCP tool, state ) button click, Enter, gamepad A text / key , icon , action , disabled bar progress bind , bind_max or min / max , format ( {v} , {max} , {pct} ), fg ; eases toward its value panel background, border, title title / title_key , layout , padding list scrolling rows items or bind (item list), row_height , col_widths ; events select . An item with disabled: true is read-only (dimmed, no hover highlight, no select event). col_widths (at most 16 widths, in units) aligns columns: a row's text is split at tab characters and each part starts at its column (the last width repeats for extra parts) grid inventory slots columns , slots , slot_size , bind ; two clicks make a move , a click on the selected slot a use input text field bind , max_len , placeholder ; events change , submit ; caret, Home/End/Delete, UTF-8 safe dialog modal box: title, wrapped text, buttons title , text , buttons [{text, action, sim}] toggle on/off switch (bool) bind , text / key , action ; event change slider float in a range bind , min , max , step (snap, 0 = continuous), value ; left/right or drag; event change choice cycles options with left/right or click options , bind (selected index), action ; event change dropdown popup list of options opened by click or Enter, index bound options , bind (selected index), action ; event change tabs container whose children are the pages, one per options title options (titles), bind (shown index; local state when unbound); event change separator thin line fg (else panel_border ), margin stack , spacer transparent container, flexible gap layout , weight Common fields: id , style (a named partial node from styles ), anchor , offset , size (0 = automatic), margin , padding , weight (share of free main-axis space in a stack), fg / bg / border / radius , hidden , bind_visible , focusable , sim . Extended look (any widget unless noted): hover_bg , press_bg , hover_fg (buttons, toggles, choices, list and grid cells), border_width (0..16), opacity (0..1, widget and children), bg + bg_end + gradient ( vertical default | horizontal ), shadow { offset , spread , blur , color }, text_shadow (a color: 1 unit drop shadow under text), tint and fit ( contain | cover | stretch ) for images, hover_scale (e.g. 1.05 grows the widget while hovered or focused; 0 = off), hover_offset [x,y] (UI units; the widget eases toward that slide while hovered or focused, like hover_scale ) and tooltip . An image with only one of size[0] / size[1] set (or none) derives the other from the image aspect ratio, and contain letterboxes inside the box. Images larger than 2048 px are downscaled on load. A list item's icon (builtin, atlas or .png) is drawn at the row start, scaled to the row height. Load notices (unknown builtin: icon, downscaled or missing image, hot reload) go to UI.Warnings / Loader.Warn ; gameui.IconNames() lists the builtin icons. Put the shared ones in styles and reference them with style : { "version" : 1 , "theme" : { "base" : "dark" , "radius" : 8 , "colors" : { "accent" : [ 255 , 190 , 74 , 255 ] } }, "styles" : { "btn" : { "bg" : [ 52 , 58 , 96 , 255 ], "bg_end" : [ 40 , 45 , 78 , 255 ], "hover_bg" : [ 88 , 98 , 156 , 255 ], "press_bg" : [ 34 , 38 , 66 , 255 ], "border" : [ 120 , 128 , 188 , 255 ], "border_width" : 2 , "hover_scale" : 1.04 , "size" : [ 240 , 44 ], "shadow" : { "offset" : [ 0 , 3 ], "blur" : 6 , "color" : [ 0 , 0 , 0 , 120 ] }, "text_shadow" : [ 0 , 0 , 0 , 140 ] } }, "root" : { "type" : "stack" , "layout" : "none" , "children" : [ { "type" : "panel" , "anchor" : "center" , "layout" : "stack_v" , "gap" : 10 , "padding" : [ 24 , 20 , 24 , 20 ], "children" : [ { "type" : "slider" , "bind" : "vol" , "min" : 0 , "max" : 1 , "step" : 0.05 , "tooltip" : "Master volume" }, { "type" : "toggle" , "bind" : "fullscreen" , "text" : "Fullscreen" }, { "type" : "choice" , "bind" : "quality" , "options" : [ "Low" , "Medium" , "High" ] }, { "type" : "separator" }, { "type" : "button" , "style" : "btn" , "text" : "Apply" , "action" : "apply" } ] } ] } } Background image and nine-slice : bg_image fills the widget with an image (a project path or an atlas icon spec). slice = [left, top, right, bottom] in texels turns it into a nine-slice: the corners and edges keep their size while the middle stretches, so a frame scales without blurred borders. { "type" : "panel" , "bg_image" : "ui/frame.png" , "slice" : [ 12 , 12 , 12 , 12 ], "padding" : [ 20 , 16 , 20 , 16 ], "layout" : "stack_v" , "children" : [] } Animation : anim = { "kind": ..., "duration": seconds, "delay": seconds, "loop": bool } plays on one widget. Looping kinds: pulse (scale breathing), bob (vertical float), wiggle (small rotation). Once-only kinds run when the screen appears: fade_in , slide_up , slide_down , slide_left , slide_right ; loop: true repeats them. duration defaults to 0.6 s (max 30), delay max 30 s, so a staggered menu just raises the delay per button: { "type" : "label" , "style" : "title" , "text" : "GAME TITLE" , "anim" : { "kind" : "bob" } }, { "type" : "button" , "style" : "btn" , "text" : "New game" , "action" : "play" , "anim" : { "kind" : "fade_in" , "delay" : 0.0 } }, { "type" : "button" , "style" : "btn" , "text" : "Settings" , "action" : "settings" , "anim" : { "kind" : "fade_in" , "delay" : 0.12 } }, { "type" : "button" , "style" : "btn" , "text" : "Quit" , "action" : "quit" , "anim" : { "kind" : "slide_up" , "duration" : 0.4 , "delay" : 0.24 } } Tabs and dropdown : tabs shows one child page at a time; options are the tab titles, one per child, in order. dropdown is a compact choice list: { "type" : "tabs" , "id" : "settings_tabs" , "options" : [ "Audio" , "Video" ], "children" : [ { "type" : "stack" , "layout" : "stack_v" , "gap" : 10 , "children" : [ { "type" : "slider" , "bind" : "vol_master" , "min" : 0 , "max" : 1 , "step" : 0.05 , "value" : 0.8 } ] }, { "type" : "stack" , "layout" : "stack_v" , "gap" : 10 , "children" : [ { "type" : "dropdown" , "bind" : "resolution" , "options" : [ "1280x720" , "1920x1080" ], "size" : [ 200 , 32 ] } ] } ] } Transitions : a screen animates with show and hide , each { "kind": ..., "duration": seconds } ; kind is fade , slide_up , slide_down , slide_left , slide_right or scale (empty = none), duration 0..3 (default 0.2). Example: "show": { "kind": "slide_up", "duration": 0.25 }, "hide": { "kind": "fade" } . Layout : containers use layout none (children placed by anchor: top-left ... bottom-right , center , stretch , plus offset and margin ), stack_v , stack_h ( gap , align start/center/end/stretch, weight ) or grid ( columns ). The root fills the safe area ( UI.Safe insets in pixels). DPI scaling : layout is in logical units; the scale is the target height over the theme's RefHeight (720) times UI.Scale , and fonts are rasterized at the exact device size, so text stays crisp. Themes : built-ins dark (default), light , hud — pick one with "theme": "hud" , or override it with an object: "theme": {"base": "dark", "colors": {"accent": [r,g,b,a]}, "font_size": 18, "radius": 4} . The colors keys are the named theme colors ( gameui.ColorNames() , also listed by the editor_gameui MCP tool, state ); an unknown key or base is rejected with the valid names: name paints name paints text label and button text bar_back bar background text_dim dimmed text, placeholder, disabled labels bar_fill bar fill (healthy) accent the source slot of a grid move bar_low bar fill when low panel panel, list and dialog background danger danger text panel_border panel, button, list, bar and slot border backdrop dimming behind a modal screen button button face input_back text field background button_hover hovered / focused button face slot inventory slot button_press pressed button face slot_sel selected inventory slot button_disabled disabled button face focus focus ring around the focused widget For a retro / pixel look, set radius to 0 (square corners) and an earthy palette, e.g.: "theme": {"base": "dark", "radius": 0, "colors": {"panel": [41,34,26,245], "panel_border": [14,11,8,255], "button": [96,83,64,255], "button_hover": [114,99,77,255], "button_press": [70,60,46,255], "text": [240,230,200,255], "text_dim": [170,154,122,255], "accent": [126,196,74,255], "focus": [255,212,92,255], "bar_fill": [155,198,73,255]}} . (The font stays Inter, rasterized crisp at the device size; there is no built-in bitmap font.) Localisation : strings {locale: {key: text}} in the document, or UI.Loc.Set . A node's key wins over text ; lookups fall back to the fallback locale and then to the key itself (a missing translation stays visible). {name} in any text expands a bound value. ui:locale:fr or UI.Loc.Locale = "fr" switches. Hot reload : gameui.Loader re-reads four files every 15 frames and compares content hashes; a changed file replaces the screen, keeping focus, scroll, selection and typed text; a broken save keeps the last good version and the error shows up in editor_gameui state ( errors ). Input and focus One set of navigation keys ( gameui.NavKey ) for the keyboard (arrows, WASD, Enter/Space, Escape, Tab, Backspace/Delete/Home/End), a gamepad (D-pad or left stick, A accept, B/Start cancel, bumpers next/previous; held directions repeat after 0.4 s) and the mouse. Focus moves spatially (the nearest widget in the pressed direction), Tab cycles in tree order, grids and lists navigate inside themselves first, a hover focuses what is under the pointer, and a modal screen or dialog traps the focus. While a modal screen is open the plugin releases the cursor ( engine.UIPointer , menu mode: clicks go to the UI and never recapture the mouse) and removes movement, look and buttons from app.Input , so the game does not walk behind a menu. Set Plugin.NoBlock to keep them. Without a window the controller's keys stand in (W/S/A/D, Space, Esc), so scripted runs can drive menus. Escape and the pause screen. runtime.gameui.pause (a screen name) makes Escape open that screen when no modal screen is open (the mouse is freed with it); inside a modal screen Escape runs the screen's cancel ( ui:back ) as before. With pause set the window never quits on Escape ( Window.SetEscapeQuits(false) ); without it Escape frees the mouse, then quits on the second press. The default input map has a pause action (Escape, gamepad Start) next to quit . A modal screen can carry "music": "menu" ; (*uiplug.GameUI).ModalMusic() returns the top modal's value for the audio layer. Values, actions and events Widgets bind to a Values store (numbers, strings, booleans, item lists; at most 1024 keys, strings 1024 bytes, NaN rejected). Frame code sets values directly; the simulation and scripts push them with uiplug.Emit(fixedCtx, gameui.Request{...}) or the SDK; the requests travel with engine.SendFixed , so a replay shows the same HUD. Interactions produce gameui.Event s ( click , select , move , use , change , submit , cancel ) with the widget id, the action , indexes and a value. Built-in actions run locally: ui:show:<screen> , ui:hide:<screen> , ui:toggle:<screen> , ui:back , ui:set:<key>=<value> , ui:locale:<code> , ui:focus:<id> . An action can hold several actions separated by ; ( "ui:hide:pause; ui:show:settings" ): they run in order, and each part that is not built in is its own event. Events into the simulation : a widget with "sim": true (or an action starting with sim: ) becomes the journaled command gameui_event , applied to a singleton gameui.inbox component (a ring of 32 events, hashed). Fixed systems and scripts read it, so a replay of the journal reproduces the same input: evs, last, ok := uiplug.PollInbox(fixedCtx, since) // events with Seq > since for _, e := range evs { /* e.Widget "bag", e.Kind "move", e.Index -> e.To */ } The demo keeps the inventory in a fixed resource changed only by these events and publishes it back with OpItems requests. App actions (frame domain, never journaled; each also reaches Plugin.Handler ; the host opts in with Plugin.AllowApp / AllowQuit , they ask the appctl.Ctl resource and end the run, the launcher then acts): game:quit / app:quit , app:title , net:join:<link> , net:host , world:play:<slot> , world:create , world:delete:<slot> , net:server_add , net:server_remove:<i> . Arguments may use {value} references ( "world:play:{pick}" ). world:play / world:delete without a slot use the selected row of the worlds list ( select event index, else the value worlds_sel ). world:create reads world_name , world_seed (empty = random; text is hashed), world_type (index or text: flat, normal, empty) and world_mode (index or text: survival, creative); the slot is derived from the name. net:join and net:host use the value player_name when set. Data sources ( Plugin.Worlds , Servers , Settings , implemented by the host): the list value worlds (rows name<TAB>mode<TAB>date , item icon = thumbnail path) refreshed at start and after a delete; the list value servers (rows name<TAB>link ); and the setting values fov , render_distance , vol_master , vol_music , vol_sfx , vol_ambient , vol_ui , fullscreen , locale seeded from SettingsSink.Load and pushed with Apply after each change event. Sounds The game UI plays ui.click (a button, list row or slot is activated), ui.hover (the pointer or keyboard focus enters an interactive widget; once per enter, at most one every 40 ms; disabled widgets are silent), ui.open / ui.close (a modal screen is shown or hidden, once per change and not per frame of its transition), ui.back (Escape / the cancel button runs the screen's cancel action; it replaces the close sound) and ui.error (a disabled widget is activated, or a ui:show / ui:hide action names an unknown screen), ui.slider (a slider value changes, rate limited to one every 60 ms while dragging) and ui.tick (a choice stepper steps). Non-modal screens (the HUD) are silent on show and hide unless they ask for a sound. All come from the local player entity in mode local , through the sound pack, and obey player.sounds overrides and mute . A widget and a screen take an optional sounds object ( click , hover , open , close , back , error , slider , tick ; a widget's open / close / back are ignored). A value is a project sound file ( sounds/x.wav ), a pack event name ( step.stone ), or "" / "none" for silence; absent keeps the default. A widget's value wins over its screen's, which acts as the default of its widgets: { "version" : 1 , "modal" : true , "sounds" :{ "open" : "sounds/menu_open.ogg" , "hover" : "none" }, "root" :{ "type" : "button" , "text" : "Buy" , "sounds" :{ "click" : "sounds/coin.ogg" , "error" : "ui.error" }}} World-space labels UI.Labels : Set a persistent nameplate (id, position, text, color, optional bar (0,1] ) and Pop a floating number (damage) that rises and fades over Life seconds. They are projected with the frame's camera (perspective or orthographic), sorted far to near, culled behind the camera and faded beyond MaxDist (64); at most 128 nameplates and 128 popups. Scripts: UILabel , UIPopup , UIRemoveLabel . Rendering The plugin draws into engine.RenderOverlay (the hybrid frame's canvas) at the renderer's real size ( engine.RenderExtent ); UI.Render(w, h, bg) rasterizes the same canvas on the CPU ( render/canvas/soft ) for headless tests, the editor preview and MCP screenshots. gameui/testdata/golden/*.png are the golden captures ( go test ./gameui -update rewrites them; GAMEUI_SHOTS=dir also writes copies). Scripts and SDK Module vox , ABI additive ( script/ABI.md ): gameui_cmd (JSON requests: set , items , show / hide / toggle , focus , locale , label , pop , remove_label , clear_labels ) and gameui_poll(since, out, cap) : burrowsdk.UISetNum( "hp" , 14 ) burrowsdk.UISetItems( "bag" , []burrowsdk.UIItem{{Icon: "builtin:g-sword" , Count: 1 }}) burrowsdk.UIShow( "pause" ) evs, last := burrowsdk.UIEvents(since) // journaled events; keep `last` with SaveState A menu screen can hand over to the game scene from a script with burrowsdk.SceneLoad("scenes/game.voxscn") (see scripting/04-entities-and-scene.md ): the default_scene of vox.project can be the menu. Editor and agents The designer is a docked full-screen panel (Unreal-style widget editor): Tools > Game UI editor, or a double-click on a .ui.json in the Content browser, opens the Game UI panel with its Game UI settings panel; Save writes the asset directly, Open is the Content browser (content browser). A separate OS window is still available (right-click the asset > "Open in a separate window"; burrowedit -tool gameui -project <dir> -asset <file> ). File > New offers templates ("Start from": Empty, Main menu, Pause, HUD, Dialog, Inventory, Title screen, Settings, Game over, Loading, Shop, Save slots, Credits, Confirm dialog, Lobby; gameui.Template builds them, and they work whatever the screen ends up being named: the close and resume buttons use the built-in ui:back ); the library column's template picker swaps the current screen for one. The header has one tab per screen of the project (a click opens it, + Screen starts a new one); the Screen tab lists every screen with its layer, whether it is modal or pauses the game and how it opens. Library tiles can also be dragged onto the canvas: the widget lands in the container under the pointer, at the drop point in a free layout. Width and height are Auto (fit the content), Fixed (pixels) or Fill (share the free space of the parent row or column, the weight); margin and padding are edited on a nested box diagram. The Style tab shows the main colours as cards (background, text, border, hover: own colour, the style's, or none), sliders for radius, border, opacity, font size and hover grow, and Detach copies a style's look into the widget. Behaviour builds several actions per click ( + Add an action ). The Screen tab also has a Data card (each bound value, where it is used and a slider to try it) and a Translations table (keys x languages, missing ones outlined, a preview language for the canvas). The docked layout: the widget library on the left (tiles grouped as Text and buttons, Layout, Input, with a search; a click adds the widget inside the selected container or after the selected widget) above the layers (the widget tree); the screen in the middle with the selection's size and its path (screen › parent › widget); Game UI settings on the right in four tabs: Layout (a 3 x 3 anchor grid plus Stretch, offset, size, margin, padding, how a container places its children: Free, Column, Row or Grid, then the id, text and data), Style (the shared style and how many widgets use it, then the widget's own look), Behaviour (what a click does, chosen as words: show, hide or toggle a screen, close this screen, set a value, change the language, focus a widget, or send an event to the game, plus visibility and keyboard / gamepad focus) and Screen (the screen settings, preview values, styles, theme, atlases, strings and the file). The Preview button (F5) runs the draft as the game would: the screen takes the pointer and the keys (mouse, arrows, Enter, Tab, typing), keeps focus, scroll and typed text across frames, the last event shows in the status bar and Escape leaves the test. A draft change rebuilds the tested screen (focus and typing survive an unrelated edit only when the tree did not change). The outline of the screen is on the left (the plus button adds the widget picked next to it, inside the selected container or after the selected widget; arrows reorder, copy duplicates, the bin deletes; Widget > Group wraps the selection in one panel). Ctrl+click adds a widget to the selection or removes it from there (the outline and the canvas), a drag on the empty background draws a rubber band that selects what it covers, and a drag of an already-selected widget moves every selected widget of a free layout at once, as one undo step. Delete, duplicate, move and group all work on the whole selection; the inspector edits the last one picked. The screen is in the middle, drawn by the game's own renderer at the device size you pick (1280 x 720, 1920 x 1080, 1024 x 768, 800 x 600, portrait, ultrawide): click a widget to select it, drag it to move it, drag one of the eight handles to resize it (positions snap to 4 pixels, hold Alt for free movement; arrows nudge by 1, Shift 8). Moving works for children of a free ( none ) layout, where it edits offset ; the children of a stack or grid layout are placed by the parent, so change their size, weight or order. The properties of the selected widget are on the right, grouped as placement, layout, content, data, look and behaviour, with the items of a list or grid and the buttons of a dialog; the Screen panel has the document settings (name, modal, layer, pause, cancel action, focus, theme, locale). Preview values fake the numbers, texts and lists that bars, labels and lists are bound to, so a health bar shows something while you design (they are not saved). Every edit is an undo step and an invalid document is refused. Save writes the .ui.json , and a running game reloads it. Styles and atlases are edited in the file. MCP tool editor_gameui : state , list , get , validate {doc} (reason or layout tree), save {path, doc} , show|hide|toggle {screen} , set , items , focus , label , preview {doc?, values?, locale?, plain?, width?, height?} (an image plus the widget tree). Templates gameui.TemplateNames / gameui.Template(name) return complete documents sharing one identity (indigo panels, amber accent, styles btn , btn_danger , card , title , head , muted , row , slider ; a theme override; show / hide transitions). Actions are placeholders to rewire ( play , settings , quit , apply , buy , confirm ...); closing uses ui:back . Bind names ( hp , vol_master , quality , loading , tip , gold , shop ...) are the values your game sets. template content Empty blank stack Main menu card with title and Play / Settings / Quit ( fade_in , staggered) Tabbed menu modal card, tabs (Play / Multiplayer / Help) with fade_in buttons, Back Pause modal, pauses the sim, Resume / Settings / Quit HUD health and stamina bars, crosshair, hotbar Dialog bottom dialog with two buttons Inventory modal 9x3 grid Title screen gradient background, bobbing title ( bob ), staggered fade_in buttons, hover_scale Settings tabs (Audio sliders / Video resolution dropdown , toggles, quality / Controls sensitivity, invert), language choice, Apply / Back Game over dark red gradient, score labels, Try again / Main menu Loading gradient, {pct} bar bound to loading , tip label bound to tip Shop stock grid, detail panel (name, description, price, Buy), gold counter Save slots list of slots with Load / Delete / Back Credits scrolling-free credits block with Back Confirm dialog modal Cancel / Confirm (danger style) Lobby the screen of the multiplayer lobby: scrolling player, spectator and settings lists, ready / team / colour / spectate buttons, host start and cancel, countdown, results with placements; its lobby:* actions become lobby commands (see Lobby screen ) Built-in UI Every engine UI is a built-in .ui.json asset, addressed builtin:<name> and listed read-only in the editor's Engine folder (UI): hud , inventory , main_menu , pause_menu , settings , lobby , title_screen , tabbed_menu , game_over , loading , shop , save_slots , credits , confirm_dialog , dialog , hud_stats and bag (the menus are the Templates below, generated from them and kept equal by a golden test; hud and inventory are the in-game ones). The scene component game.ui chooses which asset implements each slot: "game.ui" : { "hud" : "builtin:hud" , "inventory" : "builtin:inventory" , "pause_menu" : "ui/my_pause.ui.json" , "main_menu" : "none" } Slot Screen name Default (no game.ui ) Role hud game.hud builtin:hud crosshair, use hint, text lines, hotbar; shown unless -nohud / runtime.hud=false / scene.settings hud=false inventory game.inventory builtin:inventory the creative inventory panel, drawn while the inventory is open pause_menu game.pause_menu builtin:pause_menu opened by Escape (modal, pauses the simulation); runtime.gameui.pause wins when set main_menu , settings , lobby game.main_menu , ... none loaded hidden, shown by ui:show:game.main_menu and the like A value of "" or "none" turns a slot off (a component with only some fields set turns the others off; without the component the defaults above apply). With the pause slot off, Escape ends the run as it did before. A project path ( ui/my_hud.ui.json ) replaces the built-in one and hot reloads like any project screen; to start from the engine's version, copy it into the project from the Engine folder and point the slot at the copy. The game UI designer opens a builtin: document read-only (edits and Save are refused; Save as a project path writes an editable copy). In the built-in menus the placeholder actions quit and settings mean: pause menu quit goes back to the title ( app:title ), main menu quit quits, settings shows game.settings when that slot is set. HUD widgets and values (set by the plugin from the player state every frame, read by any screen): Widget Bindings Draws crosshair size (arm length), fg , text_shadow , border_width (thickness) a + at the centre of its rectangle hotbar bind item list (icons block:<id> ), bind_sel selected slot, slots (9), slot_size , gap , bg , border , fg (selection frame) numbered slots with block icons; the selected slot is framed inventory_view bind_visible hud.inventory ; bg , border , fg , hover_bg the creative inventory frame (panel, tabs, grid page, hotbar row, tooltip). The game owns the geometry and the clicks (as before); the widget only draws it Value Meaning hud.text the debug text lines ( FrameState.HUD ) joined by newlines hud.use_text Right click: <prompt> while a usable node is aimed, else empty hud.hotbar 9 items, Icon = block:<id> (empty slot: no icon) hud.selected selected hotbar slot, 0-based hud.inventory true while the creative inventory is open The icon spec block:<id> draws the isometric block icon (any image , grid or list item can use it); hosts without block textures (headless runs) draw nothing for it. The renderer keeps drawing only the frame statistics (FPS) itself when the game UI plugin is on; a build without the plugin ( runtime.plugins.gameui=false ) keeps the renderer's own HUD. Built-in screens in the designer A built-in screen ( builtin:hud , builtin:inventory , builtin:pause_menu ) opens in the designer for viewing only: a banner under the header says so and offers Copy to project and Create variant , which copy the screen into assets/ui and open the copy for editing. The game.ui inspector picks each slot from the built-in and project screens ( (none) turns a slot off), opens a slot in the designer and makes a variant of it. The widget library has a Game HUD family: crosshair , hotbar (slots, slot size, gap, the hud.hotbar / hud.selected values and colours) and inventory_view (the creative inventory frame, shown by hud.inventory ). Budgets and robustness Hostile documents are rejected by Decode (limits above). Per frame the cost is bounded by the widget cap: one layout pass, one hit test, one draw; text wrap is capped at 64 lines, images at 64 per UI (4 MiB, 2048 px), events at 256 per frame, requests at 128 per frame; extra work is dropped and counted. Limits Pointer and text input in a live window need the cgo window ( engine.UIPointer ); headless runs use the controller keys or Plugin.Input . No drag-and-drop (inventory moves are two clicks or keys), no rich text, no right-to-left or complex shaping (Latin, Latin-1 and symbols only), no scrolling containers except list , animations are limited to bar easing, hover scale and screen transitions. Atlases and image icons need project assets; builtin icons are vector (Lucide + g-* ) and need none. Immediate-mode UI from scripts For free-form menus a script can build widgets in code instead of a .ui.json file. The API mirrors Go's gameui/imui . It needs runtime.plugins.gameui ; without it nothing is drawn and widgets return false. burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnFrame: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, f burrowsdk.Frame) { burrowsdk.IMFrame( func (ui *burrowsdk.IMUI) { ui.Window( "Pause" , func () { ui.Button( "Resume" ) ui.Slider( "Volume" , &vol, 0 , 1 ) // vol comes from Props or state, every frame }) }) }, OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { evs, last := burrowsdk.UIEvents(since) if burrowsdk.IMClicked(evs, "Resume" ) { /* simulation reacts here */ } if v, ok := burrowsdk.IMNumber(evs, "Volume" ); ok { /* ... */ } }, }) The tree is built in OnFrame , every frame. IMFrame sends it to the host as one command list (host call imui_frame ). The host draws every node's list in entity order, on top of the game UI. A widget returns the result of the previous frame: Button is true for one frame after a click. Clicks and edited values reach the simulation as journaled UI events with the action im:<key> , read with UIEvents , IMClicked , IMValue and IMNumber . Replays see the same input. Events arrive one frame after the click. The key of a widget is its label (the id for ButtonID and TextInput ). Equal keys in one frame become key , key#1 , ... in call order. The host keeps the value the player edits ( Checkbox , Slider , TextInput ). The value you pass wins only when it differs from the one you passed the frame before, so keep the real value in the simulation and pass it every frame. While a window is open the cursor is free, and the mouse is not passed to the game while it is over the window. Limits: 160 commands, 6 nested levels, 32 KiB per frame and node. OnFrame runs inside a small gas budget ( Config.FrameGas ): keep the tree small. Pause menu Modal is a window that exists only while open. The host keeps the open state (frame domain, not journaled) and flips it when the input-map action toggleAction is pressed. While any modal is open the simulation is paused, the cursor is free and the game input is blocked. OnFrame keeps running ( Frame.Paused is true) so the menu stays alive; OnTick does not. OnFrame: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, f burrowsdk.Frame) { burrowsdk.IMFrame( func (ui *burrowsdk.IMUI) { ui.Modal( "pause" , "pause" , func () { // key, input-map action that toggles it ui.Label( "Paused" ) if ui.Button( "Resume" ) { ui.Close() // closes the innermost modal at the end of the frame } ui.Button( "Quit to menu" ) // im:Quit to menu is read in OnTick once ticks resume }) }) }, Keep the Modal call in every frame, open or not. A modal the script stops describing is dropped. A closed modal costs two commands: fn runs only while it is open, from the very frame its action is pressed. Buttons inside still emit journaled im: events; they are consumed when ticks resume, so call Close for anything the simulation must act on. Only game UI pauses keep OnFrame running. A pause by the editor or a fault stops it.

Getting started New here? The tutorials walk through a first project in the editor; this page covers installation and the command line. Inside the editor, press F1 for the same pages. 1. Install You need macOS on Apple silicon, Go 1.24+ (the repository targets Go 1.27), and Homebrew packages: brew install go molten-vk vulkan-loader glfw shaderc vulkan-validationlayers git clone <this repository> burrow && cd burrow go install ./cmd/burrow ./cmd/burrowplay ./cmd/burrowedit # puts the tools in $(go env GOPATH)/bin burrow doctor burrow doctor checks Go, the Homebrew formulae, the MoltenVK ICD file, a Metal device, the GOOS=wasip1 toolchain (needed to compile scripts), the Burrow binaries and whether the default (restricted-licence) block texture pack is embedded in this build, and prints the exact fix for every problem. Only Go, MoltenVK and Metal are required; the rest is optional ( shaderc only if you rebuild shaders, validation layers only for GPU debugging). Keep burrow , burrowplay and burrowedit in the same directory: burrow looks next to itself first, then on PATH , then builds them from a trusted Burrow source checkout: --burrow-root , $BURROW_ROOT , or the checkout burrow itself was built from (not available in -trimpath builds: set BURROW_ROOT ). The working directory and the project are never searched , so opening somebody else's project cannot make burrow build and run its code as "burrow". Tools are built with -trimpath into a private (0700) cache keyed by the checkout path, a hash of its sources and go.sum , the platform and the build tags; a cached binary that is not yours or is group/world-writable is refused. Set BURROW_ROOT=/path/to/burrow if you moved the checkout. Without any checkout (the Windows creator kit), script projects replace burrow-engine with the kit's minimal sdk/ module (found next to burrow.exe , or $BURROW_SDK ): it holds only sdk/burrowsdk . See security.md for the trust model. You never need to export the MoltenVK variables for burrow commands: burrow run and burrow edit pass DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH and VK_ICD_FILENAMES (and VK_LAYER_PATH with --validate ) to the child explicitly. For manual go run / go test use eval "$(burrow shell-env)" . 2. Create a game burrow new mygame --template sandbox # sandbox | empty | builder | models | scripted | multiplayer cd mygame template what you get sandbox streamed hills with trees, first-person controller, HUD (the voxel_sandbox example as a project) empty a flat world and an empty scene: your starting point builder flat world + one Go script: keys 1-4 stamp a tower, wall, pyramid or house models flat world + an .obj mesh with a textured material, a .vox model and a billboard sprite, all resolved through the asset registry (also from a packed game) scripted flat world + three scripts: a spinning cube, a voxel painter, a wandering AI multiplayer flat world + first-person controller + a base avatars script that moves one avatar per connected player from the server registry ( net_player_info ); overload it for your game (see multiplayer scripting ) A project directory: vox.project manifest (JSON): name, asset directories, default scene, input map, runtime section scenes/main.voxscn the default scene (node tree + components) input.json input actions and bindings assets/ textures, models, worlds, compiled scripts (assets/scripts/*.wasm) scripts/<name>/ Go source of scripts (scripted and builder templates), with go.mod at the root worlds/ optional .voxworld edit overlays The vox.project runtime section Everything is optional; defaults in brackets. { "schema" : 1 , "name" : "mygame" , "engine" : "0.2.1" , "asset_dirs" : [ "assets" , "scenes" ], "default_scene" : "scenes/main.voxscn" , "input_map" : "input.json" , "scripts" : [ "assets/scripts/spin.wasm" ], "runtime" : { "title" : "My Game" , // window title [project name] "width" : 1280 , "height" : 720 , // window size [1280x720] "radius" : 8 , // terrain load radius in chunk columns [8] "mode" : "fly" , // "fly" or "walk" [fly] "start" : [ 0 , 40 , 0 ], // player start (feet) [above the terrain at 0,0] "yaw" : 0 , "pitch" : 0 , // start orientation in degrees "seed" : 1 , // world seed [the .voxworld's seed, else 1] "world" : "worlds/a.voxworld" , // edit overlay loaded at start "tick_rate" : 20 , // fixed; only 20 is accepted "weather" : false , "seasons" : false , // deterministic weather simulation, see docs/weather.md [off] "vsync" : true , "generator" : { "kind" : "heightmap" , "base" : 24 , "amp" : 20 , "scale" : 64 , "octaves" : 4 , "sea_level" : 20 , "caves" : false , "trees" : true }, // or { "kind": "flat", "surface_y": 8, "depth": 8 } "plugins" : { "physics" : true , "scripts" : true , "input" : true , "controller" : true , "render" : true } } } (The JSON above has comments for illustration; real files must not.) Unknown fields are rejected with a spelling hint. plugins.render: false runs the project without a window. Only render , input , controller , character and fine_water are on by default; every plugin that adds simulation state (physics, nav, net, scripts, levels, saves, audio, ...) is off until you set it to true , and scripts is required as soon as vox.project lists scripts (the defaults table is in reference/project-config.md ). burrow new templates enable exactly what they use. Settings come from, in order of priority: command-line flags, BURROW_* environment variables, vox.project , then the defaults of the engine; a scene's scene.settings ( controller , hud ) only applies while that scene runs. 3. Play, edit, test, ship burrow run # = burrowplay . (builds stale scripts first) burrow run -- -shot out.png -frames 60 # flags after -- go to burrowplay: render a PNG and exit burrow edit # = burrowedit -project . (Play button runs the game inside the editor) burrow test # headless check, exits 1 on any problem burrow build -o mygame # single-file game burrowplay (the game runner) burrowplay [flags] [project-dir | game.voxpak] # no argument: the pak appended to the executable, else "." -headless -ticks N -hash no window or GPU; print "tick=N StateHash=<hex>" -shot out.png -frames N render N frames in a hidden window, save a PNG (needs the GPU); the game keeps running while it settles, add -freeze for a reproducible shot (no ticks, sky/water frozen) -ticks N (with a window) warm start: run N REAL fixed ticks first (journaled Step commands, so -journal/-replay reproduce the same StateHash as -headless -ticks N), then show/shoot that state -journal j.json write the session journal on exit -replay j.json -expect <hex> replay a journal with the project's configuration; exit 1 on mismatch -json machine-readable results -scene scenes/x.voxscn start on this scene of the project instead of its default_scene -level id [-spawn name] start in this level of levels/ (at this spawn point) instead of levels.initial -seed N -radius N -w N -h N -novsync -validate -nocapture -check Headless runs are deterministic: the same project, seed and tick count print the same hash on every run and every GOMAXPROCS , and on macOS Apple silicon and Intel (Windows and Linux are checked by CI, which has not run yet); burrow test verifies exactly that (runs with GOMAXPROCS = default, 1 and 8) and also replays the journal. In a window, one fixed tick passes every 50 ms of wall time; the window and renderer are frame-domain and never affect the StateHash . Editing files from the shell No hand-written JSON, no quoting fights (also on Windows): burrow config get runtime.plugins.controller # read vox.project by dotted path burrow config set runtime.plugins.controller false # JSON value, else a string; validated, atomic, formatting kept burrow config set runtime.camera.rigs[ 1 ].fov 70 # array element by index (a.b[2] or a.b.2); a.b[] appends; rm removes burrow config rm runtime.camera.rigs[ 1 ] burrow scene get scenes/main.voxscn # nodes with their ids, paths and components burrow scene set -component scenes/main.voxscn /Sun render.pointlight intensity= 3 range= 20 burrow scene rm-component scenes/main.voxscn /Sun render.pointlight burrow docs search icon names # ranked file:line hits in the embedded docs burrow ui icons # builtin game UI icon names burrow icon from logo.png -out icon.png # square 1024 app icon (pad or -mode crop, -crop x,y,w,h) Every write is checked with the project and scene loaders first; a refused edit leaves the file untouched. burrow test burrow test [dir] [--ticks 200] [--runs 3] [--json] loads the project, builds stale scripts, runs the ticks several times under different GOMAXPROCS , requires identical hashes, no failed commands, no script faults and an exact journal replay, and, with --go-tests only, runs go test ./... of the project when it has its own tests ( that compiles and runs the project's Go code natively and unsandboxed : use it only on projects you trust). Typical CI use: burrow test --json | jq -e .ok burrow build burrow build -o mygame # copy of burrowplay + game archive + trailer ./mygame # runs anywhere on the same OS/arch, no Go, no project folder ./mygame -headless -ticks 200 -hash burrow build -o mygame --app # mygame.app (INSTEAD of the plain executable) + mygame.build.json burrow build --pak game.voxpak # only the archive (burrowplay game.voxpak runs it) The archive ( .voxpak ) holds vox.project , every file under asset_dirs (compiled scripts included), the default scene, input map and world overlay. Paths are sorted, each file is stored or zlib-compressed with its SHA-256, and the whole archive is hashed: building twice gives identical bytes, and ./mygame verifies the hash before unpacking it into a private (0700, random-named) temp directory that is removed on exit (also on SIGINT/SIGTERM). The build result is recorded next to the output as <out>.build.json (with --app : mygame.app and mygame.build.json ). Hash and replay a scripted or builder game with ./mygame -headless -ticks 200 -hash -journal j.json and ./mygame -replay j.json -expect <hash> . Limits: --target accepts only the native target ( darwin-arm64 ): burrowplay needs cgo (GLFW, Cocoa) and MoltenVK, so cross-compiling needs the target SDK. --app bundles libvulkan.1.dylib and libMoltenVK.dylib from Homebrew (with a driver manifest, install_name_tool sets their ids); the game archive ships once, as Contents/Resources/game.voxpak (the executable loads it from its bundle), and the whole bundle is ad-hoc signed once, so codesign --verify --deep --strict mygame.app passes; the app is not notarised. If bundling is not possible the app still runs on Macs that have Homebrew molten-vk installed, and macOS prints the missing library path. Signing and distribution (checked on macOS 15+): the game and the .app carry an ad-hoc signature, which is enough to run on the Mac that built them (the .app passes codesign --verify --deep --strict ; the plain executable has the archive appended after the Mach-O, which strict validation reports, so for strict validation, Gatekeeper and notarisation distribute the .app ). A copy that is downloaded, AirDropped or unzipped gets the com.apple.quarantine flag and Gatekeeper rejects it ( spctl --assess says "rejected"; double-click shows "cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified"). The recipient can clear the flag with xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine mygame.app . To distribute without that step, sign with a Developer ID certificate and notarise ( codesign --force --deep --options runtime -s "Developer ID Application: NAME" mygame.app , zip it, xcrun notarytool submit mygame.zip --wait , xcrun stapler staple mygame.app ); Burrow does not do this for you. The default block textures are restricted-licence: see texture-packs.md before you distribute. 4. Scripts burrow script new spin # scripts/spin/main.go (+ go.mod if missing) burrow script build # scripts/*/ -> assets/scripts/*.wasm burrow script check # ABI check of every module Attach a script to a node with the script component: {"module": "assets/scripts/spin.wasm", "props": {"speed": 90}} . See scripting.md . 5. Next concepts.md explains the two domains and the determinism rules; editor.md the editor; troubleshooting.md the usual macOS problems. Naming and compatibility The engine was called "vox" before it became Burrow. The product, the Go module and the programs are renamed; the file formats and the wire-level identifiers are not, so existing projects, worlds, packs, scripts and agent integrations keep working. Renamed: Go module vox -> burrow-engine (import "burrow-engine" , package name burrow ; burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk for scripts). Programs: vox -> burrow , voxedit -> burrowedit , voxd -> burrowd , voxctl -> burrowctl , voxplay -> burrowplay , voxasset -> burrowasset , voxscript -> burrowscript , voxshot -> burrowshot , voxgen -> burrowgen , voxlive -> burrowlive , voxshader -> burrowshader , voxpacktool -> burrowpacktool ( vkprobe and lookmeasure are unchanged). The --vox-root flag of burrow new / burrow script new is now --burrow-root (the old spelling still works), and burrowctl keeps its session in .burrow/ by default (pass -dir .vox to continue an old session). Environment variables are BURROW_* ( BURROW_ROOT , BURROW_GPU , BURROW_LIVE , ...). The old VOX_* names are still read as a fallback when the BURROW_* one is not set (an explicitly empty BURROW_X wins). All reads go through internal/envx . Kept on purpose: File names and formats: vox.project , .voxscn , .voxworld , .voxpak (trailer VOXGAME1 ), .vmeta , and the MagicaVoxel .vox format. MCP tool names ( vox_* , editor_* ) and the agent/JSON-RPC schemas. The WASM ABI: its version, the vox host import module and the export names, so compiled scripts keep loading. The voxel_* host functions, shader names and the word "voxel" everywhere.

Go game (package gogame) A project's game logic can be a plain Go main package that imports burrow-engine/gogame . The project folder still holds the scenes, prefabs, input map and assets ( vox.project ); only the logic moves from WebAssembly scripts to your own Go code, with full access to the engine. Go game or WASM scripts? Go game ( gogame ) WASM scripts ( script ) Trust trusted, native code sandboxed, gas-metered Delivery one Go binary next to the project .wasm modules inside the project / pak Engine access everything ( Ctx.App() , any Go package) host functions only, JSON features State package variables persist memory reset on every call; state lives in components Editor burrow edit shows scenes, but the logic is not hot reloaded hot reload, debugger, script panel Mods / untrusted content no yes Pick the Go game for your own game with an AI agent or a Go programmer at the keyboard. Pick WASM scripts for mods, user-made content and anything that must run in the editor with hot reload. Quick start burrow new mygame --template gogame cd mygame go run . # window go run . -headless 100 # 100 ticks, one JSON line {"ok":true,"ticks":100,"hash":"...","error":""} vox.project keeps "scripts": [] . No scripting plugin is needed: the journaled input snapshot behind Ctx.Action comes from input/inputsnap (older projects that still enable plugins.scripts keep working; the script plugin then produces the same snapshot). Flags of gogame.Main : -dir , -scene , -headless N , -saves . func main() { gogame.Main(gogame.Game{ OnStart: func (c *gogame.Ctx) error { return nil }, OnTick: func (c *gogame.Ctx) { if c.ActionPressed( "stamp" ) { c.SetVoxel( 1 , 9 , 1 , "wood" ) } }, OnFrame: func (f *gogame.Frame) {}, UI: func (ui *imui.UI) { ui.Label( "hello" ) }, }) } examples/gogame_demo scaffolds the template and runs it. gogame.RunHeadless(game, gogame.Options{Headless: n}) returns the Result (with StateHash and the finished App ) for tests. Determinism OnStart and OnTick run inside the fixed step (20 Hz) after the engine's own fixed systems. Their changes are part of the simulation state, so a run replays to the same StateHash when your code is deterministic: use Ctx.Rand (never math/rand globals), no wall clock, no map-order dependence, no reads of data outside the simulation. Package variables persist but are not saved or rolled back. OnFrame and UI are per rendered frame and cosmetic. A failing call (unknown block, bad component JSON) is returned as the tick's error and stops the run. Ctx reference Writes take effect at once inside the tick. Method Meaning App() *engine.App , Fixed() *engine.FixedContext escape hatches to the engine Tick() uint64 , Dt() float32 tick index, tick length (1/20 s) Rand() *rand.Rand deterministic random source Log(format, args...) line on stderr tagged with the tick Action(name) bool , ActionPressed(name) bool button held / went down this tick (input map action) Axis(name) float32 , Axis2(name) (x, y) axis value (sticks, composites, mouse delta, wheel) Find(name) (Entity, bool) , FindByTag(tag) []Entity , Player() node lookup (name, or slash path with "/") Pos/SetPos , Transform/SetTransform local transform of a node Spawn(prefabPath, pos) (Entity, error) , Despawn(e) prefab instances Get(e, component, &out) bool , Set(e, component, v) error component JSON access Voxel(x,y,z) string , SetVoxel(x,y,z, block) error blocks by name ("air" clears) SetVoxels([]VoxelEdit{X,Y,Z,Block}) error , FillVoxels(lo, hi [3]int, block) error batches: up to 65536 edits, or a box of up to 1 048 576 cells; Spawn(path, pos) keeps the root's rotation and scale Tolerate(func()) run calls whose failure must not end the run (a missing prefab, a node already gone); they still return their error SpawnNode(SpawnOpts{Name, Parent, Transform, Components}) a bare node (no prefab) with components; an empty name gets a free generated one Patch(e, component, patch) , RemoveComponent(e, component) merge patch (RFC 7386) into a component, remove a component PlaySound(emitter, sound, SoundOpts) (SoundHandle, error) , StopSound(h, fade) , SetSound(h, volume, pitch) , SetBusVolume(bus, v) , StopAllSounds(bus) , SetListener(node) sounds come from a node placed in the scene;
