h: Reads and writes inside a call
x: Execution model How and when the engine calls a script, what a call can see and change, and the rules that keep a script deterministic. The rules in short Guest memory is not persistent (unless you opt in to keep_memory ). Before every call the instance is reset to the image taken right after init() . Globals, heap and stack do not survive. Persistent data lives in components ( Props and State ). Calls happen only inside the fixed tick (20 per second), one transaction per script node per tick. Effects are buffered and applied only if every call of the transaction finished. A fault drops them all. Time is the tick. dt is always 50 ms; there is no wall clock. Reads see your own writes inside a call (with the exceptions listed below). One tick flowchart TB T["FixedUpdate tick"] --> E["Next script entity, ascending id"] E --> R["Reset the instance to the image taken after init()"] R --> S["OnStart (first tick only)"] S --> V["Pending OnEvent calls"] V --> K["OnTick"] K --> Q{"Every call finished?"} Q -- yes --> A["Apply the buffered effects"] Q -- no --> D["Fault: drop all of them"] Details the chart leaves out: The system is script.run . With the physics plugin it runs before physics.character . Order between nodes : ascending entity index (the low 32 bits of the id), recomputed every tick. A node that reuses the slot of a deleted node runs early. Nodes that are disabled , have no module bound yet, or were spawned during this tick are not in the list (a node spawned by a script first runs on the next tick). Order inside a transaction : OnStart (if not started), then the inbox events in emission order, then due timers (as events, ordered by due tick then id), then OnTick . Each hook is a separate guest call with its own gas budget and a memory reset between calls; the budgets of host calls and effects are shared by the whole transaction. Commit : effects are applied in the order the script requested them, then State, subscriptions and timers are saved, then the next node runs. Node B therefore sees the committed voxels, components and spawns of node A in the same tick; A never sees B's. Events and messages sent during tick N reach OnEvent at tick N+1 or later, never in the same tick, even for a later node. Input is a journaled snapshot taken before the tick; every script sees the same values ( input, events and time ). A paused game or editor runs no ticks. Several ticks can run in one frame; the frame rate does not change what scripts see. 20 Hz scripts and smooth visuals A script runs 20 times a second on purpose: the same ticks give the same result on every machine, in a replay and in multiplayer. It cannot run per frame. What the player sees is still smooth: Moved nodes are interpolated. Meshes, sprites, voxel models and point lights are drawn between their previous and current tick by the frame's phase ( App.TickAlpha ), so a node a script moves 20 times a second glides at the screen rate. A teleport (more than 8 blocks), a new node and a gap of ticks are drawn as they are. Frame domain only: scripts, physics and the hash see the real 20 Hz value. engine.NodeInterp.Off turns it off. Per-frame behaviour is data, not script. Use the frame-domain components: visual.spring , visual.sway and visual.bind ( frame visuals ), render.viewattach (held items), character ( fp_* , held_model ), camera_rig (follow, smooth, shake), animation clips and tracks, particles, audio_source . A script starts them ( CameraSwitch , AnimPlay , Emit ...); the engine plays them every frame. Do not read frame-rate values in a script (mouse look, camera pose between ticks): input is a snapshot per tick, so a script that must feel instant (an aim reticle, a cursor) belongs to the game UI ( game.ui ), which runs per frame. Reads and writes inside a call Operation Takes effect Visible to the same call Visible to other scripts Set , SetRaw , field setters, Patch , Remove at commit yes ( Get , Has , field getters) after commit SetTransform at commit yes ( GetTransform , Get(...,"transform") ) after commit SetVoxel at commit yes ( Voxel , Raycast ) after commit Spawn node appears at commit the handle works for Set , SetTransform , Despawn , Get after commit Despawn at commit; runs OnDestroy of the subtree Exists , FindByName report it gone after commit SaveState persisted at commit yes ( LoadState returns it, also in later hooks of the transaction) never (State is private to the node) Emit , Publish delivered at commit into the inboxes, handled on a later tick next tick After , Every , Subscribe , CancelTimer saved at commit yes ( TimerRemaining ) audio, particles, camera, game UI, level and save requests queued at commit as frame-domain requests SaveSet , SaveDelete at commit SaveGet sees them after commit Reads that do not reflect the call's own writes: LightAt , PhysicsRaycast , PhysicsOverlap , and the scene queries ( Parent , Children , ScenePath , FindWith , FindTag , which read the committed scene only; nodes spawned by this call are absent). FindByName and FindByPath also read the committed scene. Voxel and SetVoxel accept coordinates in [-16777216, 16777216] on each axis ( ERR_INVALID outside) and block ids below BlockCount() ( ERR_INVALID otherwise). A call that exceeds a budget returns ERR_BUDGET instead of trapping; once the per-transaction call budget is used up, almost every host call (including Log and Voxel ) fails that way, see budgets . Persistent memory ( keep_memory ) Opt in for single-player games when ordinary Go code (package variables, maps, slices that live between ticks) must work. Project-wide: "runtime": {"script_limits": {"keep_memory": true}} in vox.project ; or per node: "keep_memory": true in its script component. Each such node gets its own instance, never pooled or shared with other nodes. Its globals and heap are not reset between calls (OnStart, events, timers, OnTick, OnDestroy). OnFrame (the visual domain) keeps using a reset instance; it does not see these globals. Gas, host budgets and the memory cap are unchanged. Memory growth persists, so the 32 MiB cap ( memory_pages ) bounds the heap for good. Fault : the instance is discarded and recreated from the init image on the next call; the memory is lost (the fault is reported as usual). Determinism : same inputs give the same results, so replaying from tick 0 and StateHash runs still match. Save and load , snapshot restore and the editor hot reload drop every memory: scripts restart from the init image. Whatever must survive goes in State /components ( SaveState ). Networked games refuse it ( runtime.plugins.net , net_model: "replicated" , dedicated server): guest memory can be neither restored nor sent to a late joiner. The project fails to load with an error. Native builds: globals already persist; BURROW_NATIVE_DEBUG skips the package-variable check for a module with a keep_memory script. Time API Value Tick() Index of the current fixed tick. The first scripted tick of a new game is 1. Identical on every machine and in a replay. dt of OnTick 1 / rate seconds: 0.05 at the default 20 Hz (the host passes 50 ms), 0.033 , 0.025 or 0.017 with runtime.tick_rate 30, 40 or 60. burrowsdk.TickRate() and TickDt() give it. Duration in seconds ticks * TickDt() . Keep durations as tick counts in State ( Tween , Cooldown , After , Every do this for you). WASI clock ( time.Now in a Go script) tick * 50 ms + 1 us per query. Monotonic and deterministic, but it measures ticks, not time. Do not use it. time.Sleep , timers of the standard library Nothing waits. Use After and Every . Randomness API Result Rand() Next uint64 of the script's stream. RandFloat() [0, 1) from the top 53 bits of Rand() . RandN(n) [0, n) ; 0 when n <= 0 . The stream is a hash of (project seed, entity, tick, draw index). The draw index counts every Rand* call of the transaction, across OnStart , events, timers and OnTick , so an extra draw in one hook shifts only the later draws of the same node in the same tick. Adding or removing other scripts never shifts it, and it never consumes the shared simulation RNG. The seed is runtime.seed in vox.project (override: burrowplay -seed N ). rand_u64 is not a free call: it counts against the call budget. math/rand and crypto/rand read the WASI random_get , a fixed stream seeded by the module hash: deterministic, but the same sequence every call (memory is reset) and unrelated to the project seed. Do not use them. Faults A trap, a Go panic , os.Exit , gas exhaustion or out-of-memory fails the whole transaction: all buffered effects of the node's transaction are dropped; the node's State, inbox, timers and started flag stay as they were (the same events are delivered again next tick); Log lines the script wrote before the fault are still delivered; a ScriptFault event is sent, the node's fault counter goes up, and at 3 faults the node is disabled until its module changes; other nodes are unaffected, the engine never crashes. Reasons, counters and how to read one: errors and limits . What is deterministic The same project, seed, inputs and module bytes give the same StateHash ( determinism ). The sandbox enforces most of it: no clock, entropy, files, network, threads or floating-point fusion (the WebAssembly spec forbids fused multiply-add, so Go's math is portable inside a guest), and gas is counted per instruction. What remains is your responsibility. Do Do not Keep time as ticks: Tick() , After , Every , Tween , Cooldown Use time.Now , time.Since , time.Sleep Draw randomness from Rand , RandFloat , RandN Use math/rand , crypto/rand , a hand-seeded generator that is not part of State Keep everything that must persist in State, Props or components Keep it in package variables, closures, maps or slices that outlive a call Iterate maps through sorted keys, or use slices Rely on range order over a map Keep floats finite; clamp before converting to an integer; let SetTransform reject NaN and Inf Store NaN or Inf in State or components; use CanonF32 when a value may be NaN Run every effect through the SDK so it is buffered and journaled Start goroutines, wait on channels, read files, environment variables or the network (they do not exist) Store entity ids as burrowsdk.Entity or uint64 Round-trip entity ids through float64 or any (they are 64-bit: slot index plus generation) Re-read the world each tick, check Exists before using a saved entity Assume a saved entity still exists (a stale id is not alive: its generation differs) Pass the same Config limits when replaying Change gas, memory, budgets or MaxFaults between recording and replay Do not print for debugging with fmt.Println : stdout and stderr are captured only for fault messages. Use Log / Logf ( debugging ). Where scripts run Context Behaviour Editor, edit mode Scripts do not run. A rebuilt .wasm is picked up about once a second: the module is re-registered and bound nodes are re-pinned (journaled script_module_changed ), faults reset. Editor, Play (Ctrl+Shift+P) Scripts run in the editor's simulation. Keyboard and mouse go to the game's input map while the pointer is over the viewport. Esc or Stop restores the snapshot taken at Play: State, timers, faults and every edit made during play are discarded, and the StateHash after Stop equals the one before Play. The editor installs neither the level plugin nor the save plugin, so LevelLoad , SaveSet and SaveSlot fail with ERR_UNAVAILABLE there; run the project with burrow run to test them. Hot reload works. burrow run / burrowplay / exported game Same simulation. Modules are fixed at start: no hot reload. runtime.plugins.scripts: true (default off, required when scripts are listed) installs the plugin. Headless ( burrow test , burrowplay -headless -ticks N ) No window and no device input: Action returns ok == false unless the host queues an input snapshot. burrow test runs the project several times and requires an identical StateHash ( testing ). Replay and journal The journal names each node's module by hash; replay re-executes the scripts with exactly those bytes. A runtime that lacks a module, runs under another Config fingerprint, or finds a data file ( ReadAsset ) whose content changed since recording fails the tick with an error (never a silent skip). Snapshot, undo, rollback, save games Every piece of script state is a component, so these are exact. A fixed tick that fails for any reason is rolled back by the engine, script effects and random draws included. Multiplayer ( networking ) Scripts run on every peer from the same commands ( multiplayer ). The local script_set_input snapshot is dropped: read the player registry instead ( NetPlayerCount , NetPlayerAt , NetPlayerInfo ). Binding is done from simulation state before every session tick, so a late joiner binds at the same tick; modules are pinned by the project content hash; hot reload is refused. See also Getting started : hooks and registration. State and props : what survives between calls. Native scripts : the shipped game links scripts natively (no wasm reset, no gas): the same rules, enforced by a parity test. Errors and limits : gas, budgets, faults. Debugging and testing : logs, profiling, burrow test . Input, events and time , multiplayer , embedding and the ABI . Determinism , networking , script/ABI.md .

State and props Guest memory is wiped before every call, so a script keeps data in components: Props for read-only designer settings, State for its own memory, and other components or the save data for everything shared. Where to keep what Need Use Writable by the script Size limit Saved with the game, snapshotted, hashed Designer settings (speed, block name, radius) Props no 16 KiB yes The script's own memory between calls State yes, own node only 64 KiB yes Data other scripts or the editor should see an existing component ( Get / Set , field setters, tags ) yes (except protected ones) schema yes Game-wide values (score, flags, unlocked items) SaveSet / SaveGet (plugin runtime.plugins.saves ) yes 1024 keys, 64 KiB per value, 1 MiB total yes Timers and subscriptions After , Every , OnMessage (stored in the script component) through the API 64 timers, 32 topics yes Static game tables (items, recipes) project data files read with ReadAsset no 256 KiB per file pinned by content hash Cache that can be recomputed nothing: recompute it, or keep it in State Globals, closures and heap values live for one call only. Even OnStart and OnTick of the same tick do not share them; they share State, because SaveState is visible to later calls of the same transaction. With the opt-in keep_memory ( execution model ) Go globals persist between ticks in single-player games, but are lost on fault, hot reload and save load: keep what must survive in State . Props Props is the props field of the script component: one JSON object per node, edited in the inspector or in the scene file. "script" : { "module" : "assets/scripts/painter.wasm" , "props" : { "block" : "wood" , "every" : 3 , "len" : 18 } } Rule Detail Limit 16,384 bytes of JSON after canonicalisation. A larger value is refused when the component is set or the scene loads: script props are 17008 bytes, limit 16384 . Shape Any JSON value is accepted by the component, but Props[T] decodes into your type, so use an object. null or absent means "no props". Canonical form Keys are sorted and whitespace removed; numbers keep their written text ( 90 stays 90 , 1e2 stays 1e2 ). Equal settings hash equally. Read Props[T]() decodes into T ; empty props give the zero T and a nil error; a shape mismatch returns the JSON error and a partly filled value. PropsRaw() returns the bytes. props_get does not use up the call budget. Write Never. A script that sets the script component gets ERR_DENIED (6), as for script.input . Change Edit in the inspector or the scene file. Edits made during Play are discarded by Stop, like every other change. Use pointer-free structs with JSON tags and give every field a sane zero value, because a missing key leaves the field at zero: package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" type props struct { Block string `json:"block"` Every int `json:"every"` Speed float32 `json:"speed"` } func (p props) withDefaults() props { if p.Every <= 0 { p.Every = 3 } if p.Speed == 0 { p.Speed = 1 } return p } func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { p, err := burrowsdk.Props[props]() if err != nil { burrowsdk.Logf( "bad props: %v" , err) return } p = p.withDefaults() if burrowsdk.Tick()% uint64 (p.Every) == 0 { burrowsdk.Logf( "block %q speed %v" , p.Block, p.Speed) } }, }) } func main() {} Decoding costs: Props[T] runs encoding/json inside the guest on every call that asks. The spin script (decode one field, read and write the transform) uses about 480,000 gas per tick, roughly 1% of the default 50,000,000; heavier JSON costs more, and script/ABI.md measures about 1.4 ms of wall time per JSON-using call on an Apple M2 Max. If the props are large, decode them once in OnStart and keep what you need in State (props edited later are then ignored), or parse with PropsRaw() yourself. State State is an opaque byte string ( state in the component, base64 in scene files). The SDK stores JSON by default; a binary codec is also available. API Does LoadState[T]() Decodes the JSON state into T . Empty state (first call) returns the zero T and a nil error. SaveState(v) json.Marshal(v) then SetStateRaw . Pass a pointer when you defer it (see below). A marshal error (NaN, unsupported type) is returned and the state is left unchanged. StateRaw() / SetStateRaw(b) The bytes. SetStateRaw fails with ERR_LIMIT (9, burrow state_set: limit exceeded (9) ) above 65,536 bytes; the old state stays. Writer / Reader Compact little-endian codec, no reflection (below). Semantics: A write is visible at once to LoadState / StateRaw in later hooks of the same transaction, and persisted at commit. If the transaction faults, the old state stays and the OnStart /events are retried next tick. Persisted only when the bytes changed. The raw bytes are hashed into StateHash , so a byte difference is a determinism difference. It is snapshotted, restored by undo and Stop, written into save games and rolled back with the tick, with no work from the script. Hot reload keeps it. The new module sees the old bytes ( migration ). state_get and state_set are free calls (they do not use the host-call budget) but their bytes count against the 1 MiB per transaction copy budget. package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" type state struct { Version int `json:"v"` WasDown bool `json:"was_down"` Presses int `json:"presses"` } func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { st, err := burrowsdk.LoadState[state]() if err != nil { st = state{} // unreadable state: start over } st.Version = 1 defer burrowsdk.SaveState(&st) // pointer: saves the value as it is when OnTick returns x, _, ok := burrowsdk.Action( "jump" ) down := ok && x > 0.5 if down && !st.WasDown { // derive edges from your own State st.Presses++ burrowsdk.Logf( "jump pressed %d times" , st.Presses) } st.WasDown = down }, }) } func main() {} defer burrowsdk.SaveState(st) with a value saves the copy taken when defer ran, before your changes. Use &st , or call SaveState explicitly at each exit. JSON rules and gotchas Topic Rule Types that work Structs (exported fields only), maps with string or integer keys (written in sorted key order, so the bytes are deterministic), slices, arrays, strings, bools, all integer and float types, pointers, json.RawMessage , burrowsdk.Entity , burrowsdk.Tween , burrowsdk.Cooldown . Types that fail chan , func , complex , cyclic pointers: SaveState returns the error. time.Time marshals but is meaningless here. Field tags json:"name" sets the key; omitempty drops zero values; json:"-" skips a field. Unexported fields are silently not saved. Missing and unknown keys A missing key leaves the field at its zero value; an unknown key is ignored. This makes adding fields safe. Renaming or retyping a field loses data or returns a decode error. Floats float32 and float64 round-trip exactly. NaN and Inf cannot be encoded ( json: unsupported value ): the save fails and the old state stays. Clamp or CanonF32 values that may be NaN. Integers int is 64-bit in the guest. Typed integer fields keep all 64 bits. Through any or map[string]any numbers decode as float64 and lose precision above 2^53 (entity ids are 64-bit): use typed fields. []byte Encoded as base64 (33% larger). Maps range order is unspecified: copy the keys to a slice and sort before you act on them. (Marshalling sorts keys for you.) Cost Marshal plus unmarshal of a small struct is millions of gas. A full 64 KiB state costs much more. Keep State small, or use Writer / Reader . Size JSON is verbose. Check len(burrowsdk.StateRaw()) while developing; 64 KiB is a hard limit. Binary state Writer and Reader skip reflection and JSON, so they avoid the roughly 1.4 ms a JSON decode costs inside the guest, and allocate one buffer. Supported: U8 , Bool , U32 , I32 , U64 , F32 (NaN canonicalised), String (u32 length prefix). There is no F64 ; store math.Float64bits with U64 . Reader returns zeros and sets Err on short input, so an empty first-call state decodes to all zeros. package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { r := burrowsdk.NewReader(burrowsdk.StateRaw()) count := r.U32() lastTick := r.U64() first := r.Err // true on the very first call: nothing was stored yet count++ var w burrowsdk.Writer w.U32(count).U64(burrowsdk.Tick()) if err := burrowsdk.SetStateRaw(w.Bytes()); err != nil { burrowsdk.Logf( "save: %v" , err) } if !first && count% 100 == 0 { burrowsdk.Logf( "100 more ticks, last was %d" , lastTick) } }, }) } func main() {} Do not mix codecs on the same node: LoadState on binary bytes returns a JSON error. Changing the state format The module can change while State stays (hot reload, a new game version loading old saves). The new code must read the old bytes. Add a version field first ( Version int in JSON; a leading U8 in binary), starting at 1. Only add fields (they decode as zero in old data) and handle old versions explicitly: st, err := burrowsdk.LoadState[state]() if err != nil { st = state{} // unreadable: reset } switch st.Version { case 0 , 1 : // 0 = first run or written before versioning st.Name = "default" // field added in version 2 st.Version = 2 } Binary: append new fields at the end and read them after the old ones; an old, shorter blob sets Err and yields zeros for the new fields. To drop State altogether, SetStateRaw(nil) . Hot reload clears the fault counter and the disabled flag but does not reset State or started , so OnStart does not run again after a rebuild. Other components as storage Get[T] , Set[T] , GetRaw , SetRaw , Has , Remove and the field accessors ( GetFloat , SetString , Patch , ...) work on any node and any registered component; Registry("components") lists them. Writes are validated against the component schema and applied at commit. There is no free-form "data" component: you cannot invent component names. Store private data in State, shared data in an existing component that fits ( tags for labels, physics.velocity , nav.target , ...), or in the save data. Protected components that a script can read but never write, remove or spawn with: script , script.input ( ERR_DENIED ). Also protected against removal: transform , scene.name , scene.parent , scene.children . Another node's State is not reachable: it lives in its script component. Exchange data with Emit (to one node or all) or Publish on a topic instead. Save data ( SaveSet(key, val string) , SaveGet , SaveDelete ) is global to the game, shared by all scripts, hashed and rolled back with the world. Keys match [A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]{1,128} ( ERR_INVALID otherwise); a value over 64 KiB is ERR_MEMORY (the per-argument cap); it is ERR_UNAVAILABLE without runtime.plugins.saves and in the editor's Play mode. Writes are visible to your own SaveGet at once and to others after commit. Encode structured values as JSON strings. Module pinning A node records the content hash of the module it runs in hash ( sha256:<hex> ), part of StateHash . The first time a node is seen without a hash , the engine resolves module and queues a journaled bind command that stores the hash and a fingerprint of the runtime configuration. Do not write hash by hand in scenes. A replay re-executes every script with the module whose hash the journal names. The runtime keeps module versions by content (at most 256; versions the journal needs are pinned and never evicted). When a .wasm file changes under the editor, a journaled script_module_changed command re-pins every node with that module to the new hash on a tick boundary, re-enables them and clears their fault count. A file that fails to load keeps the old module. Restoring a snapshot or a save into a runtime that does not have the module named by a node's hash fails the next tick with an error naming the hash. Rebuilding a script therefore changes the game's identity: version your saves ( Plugin.GameVersion and Migrate in levels and saves ) and keep State changes backward compatible. A game build registers the modules at start and has no hot reload, so a running game never changes a node's module. Script.Cfg fingerprints gas, memory, budgets, MaxFaults , WASI strictness and module size cap; a replay under another configuration fails instead of diverging ( host tuning ). See also Execution model : reset, transactions, what survives a fault. Errors and limits : ERR_LIMIT , budgets, byte counts. Debugging and testing : "my global variable resets", "Props decode is slow". Entities and scene : component access, field accessors, tags. Cookbook : state patterns. Components reference: script , script API: codec and data .

Entities and scene How a script reaches nodes of the scene: entity handles, components, transforms, spawning, searching and tags. Every function here is a host call: it costs one call of the budget ( limits ) and returns an *burrowsdk.Error on failure, never a trap. The generated signature list is reference/script-api.md ; this page gives the semantics. Error codes: 1 INVALID , 2 MEMORY , 3 NOT_FOUND , 4 TOO_SMALL (handled by the SDK), 5 BUDGET , 6 DENIED , 7 UNAVAILABLE , 8 REJECTED , 9 LIMIT . burrowsdk.IsNotFound(err) tests code 3. Entities An Entity is a uint64 handle to a scene node. The low 32 bits are the slot, the high 32 bits a generation, so a handle to a despawned node never matches a later node that reuses the slot. 0 means "no entity" (root parent, "everything" as an event target, "whole scene" as a search root). function what it does errors Self() the node that carries this script none Exists(e) true for a live node, a handle returned by Spawn in this call, and not for a node despawned in this call none ( false on any failure) Rules: A handle is only meaningful inside the run that obtained it. Keeping an Entity in State between ticks is fine for ordinary nodes (it is a plain number), but check Exists before use: the node may be gone. A call on a dead or unknown handle fails with NOT_FOUND . 0 is never alive. Spawn returns a pending handle , valid only until the end of the call that created it. Never store it. See Spawn and Despawn . Node names are unique among siblings only, so a name does not identify a node globally; use a handle, a path or a tag. Components Components are addressed by their schema name ( "transform" , "physics.body" , "tags" , ...). The list with every field, range and default is reference/components.md . Registry("components") lists the names a running game knows ( world ). function what it does errors GetRaw(e, name) canonical JSON of the component NOT_FOUND (dead entity, unknown name, component absent) Get[T](e, name) GetRaw + json.Unmarshal into T as GetRaw ; a decoding failure is a plain error SetRaw(e, name, json) attach or replace the whole component REJECTED , DENIED , NOT_FOUND , INVALID Set[T](e, name, v) json.Marshal + SetRaw as SetRaw ; a marshal failure is a plain error Has(e, name) true when attached none ( false on any failure) Remove(e, name) detach the component DENIED , NOT_FOUND Behaviour: Immediate checks, deferred effect. SetRaw validates the JSON against the schema at once and returns REJECTED on failure; the write itself is queued and applied when the script call commits. A fault drops it. Remove is queued the same way. The failure text of a rejection is shown in the console. Reads see your own writes. After Set , Get and Has in the same call return the new value, and after Remove , Has is false and Get is NOT_FOUND . Other scripts see the change from the next script run (the commit happens before the next script of the tick starts). Set replaces the whole component. Fields you leave out take the zero value of their type (only transform fills identity defaults: scale 1). For a partial change use field access . Strict validation. Unknown fields, a wrong JSON type, an out-of-range value and the component's own consistency rules (for example physics.body needs non-zero half for a dynamic body) all give REJECTED . The value must be a single JSON object. Canonical output. GetRaw returns the schema's own field order, with every field present. Absent is not an error for Remove . Removing a component the node does not have succeeds and does nothing. Sizes. A component name is 1..128 bytes ( INVALID otherwise); one argument is at most 64 KiB ( MEMORY ). Bytes moved count against the per-call byte budget. Components a script cannot write (in SpawnOpts.Components the same three names are refused with REJECTED ): component Set and field writes Remove Get / Has script DENIED (use SaveState ) DENIED allowed script.input DENIED DENIED allowed transform allowed (see Transforms ) DENIED allowed scene.name , scene.parent , scene.children REJECTED (structural, not writable) DENIED Get returns the value, Has is false Names, parents and children cannot be changed after creation: there is no rename or reparent call. Spawn under the right parent and despawn to remove. A component that exists in the schema only when a plugin is on ( physics3d.* , nav.* , ai.* , anim.player , ...) is NOT_FOUND on Get and REJECTED on Set when the project does not enable that plugin. package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" type body struct { Kind string `json:"kind"` Half struct { X, Y, Z float32 } `json:"half"` Mass float32 `json:"mass"` } func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnStart: func (self burrowsdk.Entity) { if !burrowsdk.Has(self, "physics.body" ) { return } b, err := burrowsdk.Get[body](self, "physics.body" ) if err != nil { burrowsdk.Logf( "get: %v" , err) return } b.Mass *= 2 if err := burrowsdk.Set(self, "physics.body" , b); err != nil { burrowsdk.Logf( "set: %v" , err) // REJECTED: schema refused the value } }, }) } func main() {} Field access Field calls read or write one value by path. A read costs a few microseconds against about a millisecond for a whole-component JSON round trip in Go-in-wasm, and a write sends only the change. Writes follow the same rules as Set : the whole resulting component is validated ( REJECTED if invalid), queued, applied at commit, dropped on a fault. Reads see this call's writes. script and graph_script are DENIED for writes and readable. function what it does errors FieldRaw(e, comp, path) JSON text of the value NOT_FOUND , INVALID (bad path) GetFloat / GetInt / GetBool number (bool as 0/1); GetInt truncates as above, INVALID for a non-number GetString string value as above, INVALID for a non-string GetFloats(e, comp, paths...) several numbers in one call, in order; NaN for a missing or non-numeric path INVALID , LIMIT (more than 32 paths) GetFields(e, comp, paths...) several raw JSON values; nil for a missing path INVALID , LIMIT (more than 32 paths) SetFieldRaw(e, comp, path, json) set one value from JSON text NOT_FOUND , REJECTED , DENIED , INVALID SetFloat / SetInt / SetBool / SetString typed setters; SetFloat writes an integer when the value is integral as above; INVALID for NaN or Inf Patch(e, comp, json) RFC 7386 merge patch of the component NOT_FOUND , REJECTED (not a JSON object, or invalid result), DENIED Path syntax: dot separated keys with optional [n] indexes, pos[1] , bodies[2].mass , at most 256 bytes and 16 segments. An empty segment, a negative or non-numeric index is INVALID . Intermediate keys and indexes must exist, otherwise NOT_FOUND ; the last key of a write may be new (the schema then accepts or rejects it). The component must be present on the node ( NOT_FOUND ); field writes never attach a component. Merge patch: objects merge recursively, null deletes a key, anything else (including arrays) replaces the value. Vector fields have two JSON shapes, and the path must match the shape: shape where path example array [x,y,z] transform , camera_rig ( offset , bounds , ...) pos[1] object {"X":..,"Y":..,"Z":..} fields typed vec3 in physics.body , physics.character , physics.velocity , nav.* , ai.perception half.Y Check with GetRaw when unsure. The typed vec3 accessors (see below) use the right form for each field; with GetFloat / SetFloat you choose the path yourself. Typed accessors. components_gen.go holds one getter and one setter per scalar field of every built-in component, generated from the schema ( make sdk-gen ): AiBrainInterval(e) , SetAiBrainInterval(e, v) , CameraRigFov(e) , ... plus a Comp<Name> constant per component ( CompNavAgent ). Types: string , int64 , float64 , bool , [3]float64 for vec3. They are thin wrappers over the calls above and obey the same errors. The full list is in reference/script-api.md . The vec3 accessors of object-shaped fields ( PhysicsBodyHalf , NavAgentVel , ...) read the .X , .Y , .Z paths and write an object. Before this was fixed (0.2.2 and earlier) they used array paths and failed: reads gave NaN and writes were REJECTED . package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { // one value, not the whole body m, err := burrowsdk.GetFloat(self, "physics.body" , "mass" ) if err != nil { return } _ = burrowsdk.SetFloat(self, "physics.body" , "mass" , m+ 0.01 ) _ = burrowsdk.SetFloat(self, "physics.body" , "half.Y" , 0.5 ) // object-shaped vec3 _ = burrowsdk.Patch(self, "physics.body" , [] byte ( `{"trigger":true}` )) xs, _ := burrowsdk.GetFloats(self, "transform" , "pos[0]" , "pos[1]" , "pos[2]" ) _ = xs }, }) } func main() {} Transforms function what it does errors GetTransform(e) local Transform{Pos, Rot, Scale} NOT_FOUND SetTransform(e, t) replace the local transform (queued, applied at commit) NOT_FOUND , INVALID (any NaN or Inf), BUDGET Transform holds three [3]float32 : field unit meaning Pos blocks (1 voxel = 1 block) position relative to the parent Rot degrees, [pitch, yaw, roll] = rotation about X, Y, Z Euler angles Scale factor, 1 = unscaled per axis Rotation order. The matrix is R = Ry(yaw) * Rx(pitch) * Rz(roll) and the local matrix T(Pos) * R * S(Scale) : roll is applied first, then pitch, then yaw. Local only. The SDK has no world transform. A child's Pos is relative to its parent and rotates and scales with it. To get world coordinates, walk Parent and compose the transforms yourself, or keep such nodes at the root. Physics and voxel APIs use world coordinates. Replace, not merge. SetTransform writes all nine floats. A Scale of exactly {0, 0, 0} , which a literal Transform{Pos: p} holds, is written as {1, 1, 1} (older SDKs wrote scale 0 and made the node invisible). Any other scale, even one with a single 0 axis, is written as given. To hide a node use its render component. Same data as the component. Get(e, "transform") / Set(e, "transform", ...) and the field paths pos[0] , rot[1] , scale[2] read and write the same value, with the same read-your-writes view. The component JSON form is {"pos":[x,y,z],"rot":[p,y,r],"scale":[x,y,z]} ; omitted fields default to 0, 0, 1 . Bodies overwrite it. A rigid body ( physics3d ) and a physics.character write the node's transform every tick they move, so a script that also sets it fights the simulation. Move bodies with velocity, intent or impulse ( world ). Pending handles. On a node spawned in this call, GetTransform returns the identity until you call SetTransform on it; the Transform option passed to Spawn is applied at commit and is not visible to reads. package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { t, err := burrowsdk.GetTransform(self) if err != nil { return } t.Rot[ 1 ] += 90 * float32 (dt) // 90 degrees per second of yaw t.Pos[ 1 ] += 0.5 * float32 (dt) _ = burrowsdk.SetTransform(self, t) }, }) } func main() {} Spawn and Despawn function what it does errors Spawn(prefab, opts) queue a new node, return a pending handle NOT_FOUND (unknown prefab or parent), REJECTED , BUDGET Despawn(e) queue removal of e and its whole subtree NOT_FOUND , BUDGET SceneLoad(path) queue a .voxscn project file, instantiated under the root at commit DENIED (unsafe path or not .voxscn ), NOT_FOUND (unknown file), REJECTED (invalid document), LIMIT (> 8 MiB), BUDGET SpawnOpts (all optional, zero value = default): field default meaning Name <prefab or "node">_<tick>_<your entity>_<n> node name; 1..128 bytes, valid UTF-8 in NFC form, no / , not . or .. , no control characters Parent 0 = scene root a live node or a pending handle from this call Transform identity ( pos 0, rot 0, scale 1 ) local transform; a non-nil value replaces all nine floats, so set Scale Components none name -> JSON , validated like Set ; script and script.input are refused Behaviour: The node appears at commit , after the call finishes without a fault. Until then no search sees it; scripts that run later in the same tick do see it. The handle is call-local. It lets you Set , Remove , SetTransform , Despawn or use the node as Parent of another Spawn or as an Emit target within the same call. Reads ( Get , Has , GetTransform ) of a pending node see only writes made through the handle in this call, not the options given to Spawn . The real entity is not returned: find it later by name, path or tag (give it a unique Name or a tag via Components: {"tags": {"tags":["x"]}} ). Validation split. The call checks name syntax, the component JSON and the parent now. A sibling name clash, a parent that is gone, or a tree deeper than 4096 is only found at commit: it is reported as a non-fatal fault in the console, the node is not created, and later queued operations on its handle fail the same way. The rest of the call's queued effects still apply (commit is not rolled back by such failures). Use unique names (the default name is unique per script, tick and call). Prefabs. prefab names a scene document saved as <name>.prefab or prefabs/<name>.prefab in the project (so Spawn("crate", ...) loads prefabs/crate.prefab ). The name may use letters, digits, _ - . / and no .. ; anything else, or a missing file, is NOT_FOUND . A prefab is read once and cached. The standard runners ( burrow run , burrowplay , exported games, the editor Play mode) all load them; an embedding program can also fill script.Plugin.Prefabs or PrefabSource ( embedding ). Before 0.2.2 the standard runners had no prefabs and only "" (a bare node) worked. The prefab root takes Name and Transform ; its child nodes keep the prefab's names. Prefabs. A spawned prefab keeps its root's scale: the spawn transform places it and its scale multiplies the root's. Without a Name , the node is named after the prefab file ( wolf_<tick>_<entity>_<n> for assets/prefabs/wolf.prefab ). A prefab counts as one spawn whatever its size, so an articulated model of many nodes is spawned as a prefab. Limits. 32 spawns per script call and 1024 per tick ( BUDGET ); at most 4096 queued operations per call ( BUDGET ). SceneLoad(path) loads a whole scene document at once — the same journaled scene_load start-up command a default_scene uses, so a menu can hand over to the game ( burrowsdk.SceneLoad("scenes/game.voxscn") ). The path follows the ReadAsset rules (project relative, no .. /absolute/backslash/hidden segment) and must end in .voxscn . The file is read pinned by content hash like asset_read — a replay loads the same document — and validated against the scene schema at call time, so a broken file is an error and nothing is committed. It instantiates under the root at commit (later scripts of the same tick see the nodes); its bytes, spawned nodes and one event count against the transaction budgets, and the gas is 200 + 1 per 64 bytes read. SceneSwitch(path) replaces the whole running scene by another scene of the project, world included : every root is despawned, the base terrain is rebuilt from the target scene's world file (the .voxworld next to the scene: its seed, generator and voxel edits; the project's terrain when the scene has none), and the document is instantiated. The path rules, the pinned read and the schema validation are SceneLoad 's (an unsafe, missing, non- .voxscn or invalid path is an error and nothing happens). The scripts of the running scene get on_destroy when the request is accepted (like a despawn). The switch is one journaled command applied right after the tick (it carries the document and the world file, so a replay never reads the project); later scripts of the same tick still see the old scene, only the first request of a tick is served, and a second call in one invocation fails with a budget error. The player is put back at runtime.start (or above the terrain at the origin). Limits: the generators the game can rebuild are heightmap , flat , biomes and empty , and a scene keeps the project's generator when its world file records a "custom" one (it can then only have its own seed); a world file made with another generator or seed than the one the scene runs is refused (logged, nothing changes). A save made after a switch reloads into that scene (see levels and saves ). The camera history is cut ( FrameState.CameraCut ), so temporal anti-aliasing does not smear the old world into the new one. Despawn removes the node and all descendants at commit. If the node or any descendant carries a script with an OnDestroy handler, that handler runs first (in the same commit, before removal, in tree order) and its own effects are committed; despawns requested from inside an OnDestroy do not run further OnDestroy hooks. Nodes removed by the engine, the editor or a level switch do not call OnDestroy . Despawning a handle spawned in the same call cancels the spawn. After Despawn(e) , Exists(e) is false and every search in the same call skips e and its subtree. package main import ( "encoding/json" "fmt" "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" ) func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { if burrowsdk.Tick()% 20 != 0 { return } at, _ := burrowsdk.GetTransform(self) t := burrowsdk.Transform{Pos: at.Pos, Scale: [ 3 ] float32 { 1 , 1 , 1 }} h, err := burrowsdk.Spawn( "" , burrowsdk.SpawnOpts{ Name: fmt.Sprintf( "marker_%d" , burrowsdk.Tick()), Transform: &t, Components: map [ string ]json.RawMessage{ "tags" : json.RawMessage( `{"tags":["marker"]}` ), }, }) if err != nil { burrowsdk.Logf( "spawn: %v" , err) return } _ = burrowsdk.SetTransform(h, t) // the handle works within this call if old, ok := oldest(); ok { _ = burrowsdk.Despawn(old) } }, }) } func oldest() (burrowsdk.Entity, bool ) { list, _, err := burrowsdk.FindTag( "marker" , 0 ) if err != nil || len(list) < 8 { return 0 , false } return list[ 0 ], true } func main() {} Finding things Queries read the committed scene : what earlier scripts of this tick left, minus nodes this call has despawned. Nodes spawned by this very call, and tags or components you set in this call, are not visible to them. Results are deterministic: children in child order; searches depth-first in child order from the roots in ascending entity-index order. function what it does errors FindByName(name) first node with that name, depth-first from the roots NOT_FOUND , INVALID (empty or over 1024 bytes) FindByPath(path) node at a slash path such as world/tower/top ; a leading / is ignored NOT_FOUND , INVALID ScenePath(e) slash path of e (a root is just its name) NOT_FOUND Parent(e) parent of a committed node, 0 for a root NOT_FOUND (dead or pending handle) Children(e) children in child order, at most 4096 NOT_FOUND FindWith(component, root) nodes under root carrying the component NOT_FOUND (unknown component or dead root), INVALID (empty or over 128 bytes) FindTag(tag, root) nodes under root carrying the tag INVALID (bad tag syntax), NOT_FOUND (dead root) root = 0 searches the whole scene; a non-zero root is included in the search and its subtree walked. FindWith("transform", 0) returns every node. Bounds and truncation. MaxQueryResults = 4096 . FindWith and FindTag return truncated = true when more than 4096 nodes match, or when the scan hit its cap of 100,000 nodes before finishing; the matches found so far (at most 4096, in search order) are returned. Children also stops at 4096 but does not report truncation. A search stops after 100,000 nodes scanned and returns what it found so far; this limit is not reported in truncated . Scenes that large need narrower roots. FindByName and FindByPath do not see nodes spawned in this call and skip nodes despawned in it. Cost. Every query is charged deterministic gas on top of its call: call gas Parent 4 Children 8 + 1 per child ScenePath 8 + 1 per 8 bytes of path FindWith , FindTag 16 + 1 per node scanned The SDK starts with room for 64 results and retries with 256, 1024, then 4096 when more matched, so a search with many results scans up to four times. Run a search once, keep the result in State or a local, and avoid scanning the whole scene every tick. package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnStart: func (self burrowsdk.Entity) { coins, truncated, err := burrowsdk.FindTag( "coin" , 0 ) if err != nil { burrowsdk.Logf( "find: %v" , err) return } kids, _ := burrowsdk.Children(self) path, _ := burrowsdk.ScenePath(self) parent, _ := burrowsdk.Parent(self) burrowsdk.Logf( "%s (parent %d): %d children, %d coins, truncated %v" , path, parent, len(kids), len(coins), truncated) if door, err := burrowsdk.FindByPath( "world/door" ); err == nil { _ = burrowsdk.AddTag(door, "interactive" ) } }, }) } func main() {} Tags Tags label nodes so scripts find groups without knowing names. They live in the scene component tags , which is an ordinary component: saved with the scene, editable in the inspector, hashed. function what it does errors TagsOf(e) sorted tags of e ; nil when the component is absent or on any error none HasTag(e, tag) whether e carries the tag none AddTag(e, tag) add a tag (no-op if present) REJECTED (invalid tag or more than 16), NOT_FOUND RemoveTag(e, tag) remove a tag (no-op if absent) NOT_FOUND A tag is [A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]{1,32} (letters, digits and _ . : / - ), at most 16 per node . The stored list is sorted and unique. AddTag and RemoveTag read and rewrite the whole tags component, so they follow Set : validated now, applied at commit, readable by TagsOf in the same call, and visible to FindTag only after the commit. FindTag with an invalid tag string fails with INVALID ; AddTag with one fails with REJECTED . Tags can also be set in SpawnOpts.Components and in the scene file ( "tags": {"tags": ["coin"]} ). World How a script reads and edits voxels, casts rays, queries and drives physics bodies, steers navigation agents, talks to levels and saves, and reads project data. Signatures are in reference/script-api.md ; this page gives units, limits, timing and edge cases. Error codes: 1 INVALID , 2 MEMORY , 3 NOT_FOUND , 4 TOO_SMALL (handled by the SDK), 5 BUDGET , 6 DENIED , 7 UNAVAILABLE , 8 REJECTED , 9 LIMIT ( errors and limits ). Coordinates and units One voxel is one block, one unit of length. Voxel cells are integers (x, y, z) ; the cell (x, y, z) covers the float range [x, x+1) on each axis, so floor maps a position to its cell. +Y is up. World coordinates, shared by voxels, rays, physics and navigation. Only Transform.Pos of a child node is relative to its parent ( entities ). Voxel cells must satisfy |x|, |y|, |z| <= 16,777,216 (2^24), otherwise INVALID . Chunks are 32 blocks wide. Space that is not loaded or not generated reads as air (id 0). There is no error for it. A write there creates the chunk in the world's edit overlay. Rays and boxes take float32 ; non-finite values are INVALID . Voxels function what it does errors Voxel(x, y, z) block id at the cell, including this call's earlier writes INVALID (out of range) SetVoxel(x, y, z, id) write a block id INVALID (out of range or unregistered id), BUDGET BlockByName(name) id of a registered block; "air" and "" give 0 NOT_FOUND LightAt(x, y, z) light of the cell INVALID Raycast(origin, dir, max) first solid voxel along a ray INVALID BlockID is an int32 ( 0 = air); ids are defined by the project's block registry ( below ). When a write is visible. SetVoxel is validated at once and buffered; the chunk changes when the script call commits (and not at all if it faults). Until then Voxel and Raycast of the same call see it; LightAt , PhysicsRaycast and the other physics queries do not. After the commit, scripts that run later in the same tick see it, then the physics step, then meshing and rendering. Writing the block already there still costs one edit of the budget. Budget. 4096 voxel edits per script call and 262,144 per tick; the next one returns BUDGET and nothing is written for it. Physics3DRemoveVoxel counts as one edit too. Light. Light{R, G, B, Sky} holds block light per colour channel and skylight, each 0..15 . Block() is the brightest block channel; Level(skyDim) is max(Block(), Sky - skyDim) , with skyDim 0 at noon up to 15 at night (the "mobs spawn in the dark" rule). LightAt is deterministic and a function of the committed blocks only, so it ignores writes made in this call. Details: lighting . Voxel raycast. Raycast(origin, dir, max) returns a Hit{X, Y, Z, NX, NY, NZ, Dist, Block} and ok . input rule dir any non-zero vector; it is normalised, so Dist is in blocks along the ray max must be > 0 ; clamped to 4096 hits blocks whose registry entry is solid; air, water and non-solid plants are passed through origin inside a solid voxel hit on that voxel with Dist = 0 and a zero normal NX, NY, NZ normal of the entered face (points back toward the origin), one component is +-1 miss ok = false , no error It reads the world as this call sees it (earlier SetVoxel included) and respects block shapes when the project uses shaped blocks. package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { t, err := burrowsdk.GetTransform(self) if err != nil { return } stone, err := burrowsdk.BlockByName( "stone" ) if err != nil { return // not in this registry } // look straight down and fill the cell above the first solid block hit, ok, err := burrowsdk.Raycast(t.Pos, [ 3 ] float32 { 0 , - 1 , 0 }, 32 ) if err != nil || !ok { return } x, y, z := int (hit.X+hit.NX), int (hit.Y+hit.NY), int (hit.Z+hit.NZ) if id, _ := burrowsdk.Voxel(x, y, z); id == 0 { _ = burrowsdk.SetVoxel(x, y, z, stone) } }, }) } func main() {} Block registry The registry is the list of block types of the running project: the shaped set ( runtime.blocks: "shapes" , the only supported value; "classic" and "extended" are deprecated and resolve to it), plus plugin blocks such as water levels. Ids follow registration order and differ between those sets, so always resolve blocks by name ( BlockByName ), never hard-code ids. See blocks and block shapes ; a shaped block keeps its bare item name for the default state ( oak_stairs ) and name[prop=value,...] for the others. function what it does errors BlockCount() number of registered blocks, air included (ids are 0..count-1 ); returns the negative error code instead when the host is unavailable none BlockName(id) name of a block id NOT_FOUND BlockInfo(id) BlockProps of a block id NOT_FOUND Registry("blocks") all block names, index = id INVALID (unknown kind) BlockProps : ID , Name , Solid (blocks movement and rays), Opaque (stops light, hides faces), Color (RGB 0..255), Emit (light level 0..15; 0 also for blocks that emit by well-known name, such as torches), Liquid (0 not a liquid, 1..7 flowing level, 8 source), Fragile (flowing liquid destroys it), LightLoss (extra light levels lost per RGB channel), Shape (0 = cube, otherwise a shape model id). Item registry The project's items come from runtime.items (package itemset ; items ). The engine has no built-in item list and no inventory: the registry gives scripts identity, ids and stack limits, and the mod keeps counts in block data, Script.State or the save store. Ids are 1..ItemCount() , item 0 is the empty stack, and a project without the file has none. Resolve items by name, never hard-code ids. function what it does errors ItemCount() number of registered items none ItemName(id) registry name of an item id NOT_FOUND ItemIDByName(name) id of an item name (case and the burrow: prefix are ignored) NOT_FOUND ItemInfo(id) ItemProps{ID, Name, Display, MaxStack, Block} NOT_FOUND A stack is 6 bytes, little endian: u16 item id then u32 count. burrowsdk.ItemStack has Encode , DecodeItemStack , Split(n) and Merge(src, maxStack) ; the engine counterparts are in itemset . ItemProps.Block is the registry name the item stands for or places, and is only reported: the engine never places or drops it. Physics queries Two independent physics plugins exist, and the functions are separate: plugin project setting script functions when absent physics (AABB bodies, characters, triggers: character ) runtime.plugins.physics PhysicsRaycast , PhysicsOverlap UNAVAILABLE physics3d (rigid bodies, voxel bodies, joints: physics ) runtime.plugins.physics3d (off by default) Physics3DRaycast , Physics3DOverlap , Physics3DApplyImpulse , Physics3DBody , Physics3DRemoveVoxel UNAVAILABLE Layers: a body has a layer bitmask and a mask of the layers it collides with. A query mask selects which layers it sees. LayerDefault is bit 0 ( 1 ), terrain (voxels) is bit 31 ( 0x80000000 ), all bits is 0xFFFFFFFF . Terrain is only tested when the mask has bit 31. PhysicsRaycast / PhysicsOverlap Physics3DRaycast / Physics3DOverlap mask 0 sees nothing sees every layer triggers ignored by the ray, included by the overlap ignored by the ray, included by the overlap body state read committed state of this tick, before this tick's physics step same, shapes as of the end of the previous step this call's voxel writes not seen not seen Both read the simulation as it stands when your script runs (scripts run before the physics step of the same tick). Rays. origin and dir as for Raycast ( dir non-zero, max > 0 , finite), else INVALID . PhysicsRaycast(origin, dir, max, mask) (PhysicsHit, ok, err) : PhysicsHit{Entity, Voxel, Point, Normal, Dist} . Entity == 0 means terrain, and Voxel is then the cell; for a body, Voxel is zero. On equal distance terrain wins, then the lower entity id. The terrain part looks at most 4096 blocks. Physics3DRaycast(...) (RayHit3D, ok, err) : RayHit3D{Entity, Terrain, Cell, Point, Normal, Dist} . Terrain is true for a voxel hit ( Entity == 0 ); Cell is the terrain voxel, or the grid cell of a voxel body. Overlaps. PhysicsOverlap(min, maxp, mask, max) and Physics3DOverlap(...) test the axis-aligned box [min, maxp] and return bodies []Entity (ascending entity id, at most max ), terrain bool (a solid voxel overlaps, only when the mask has bit 31) and total (all bodies found, may exceed max ). min <= maxp on every axis and finite, else INVALID . max <= 0 is treated as 1; max > 4096 is INVALID . PhysicsOverlap needs a strict overlap (touching faces do not count). Physics3DOverlap inflates a flat axis by 0.001 and rejects a box wider than 2048 on any axis ( INVALID ). package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { t, err := burrowsdk.GetTransform(self) if err != nil { return } const bit31 = uint32 ( 1 ) << 31 hit, ok, err := burrowsdk.PhysicsRaycast(t.Pos, [ 3 ] float32 { 0 , - 1 , 0 }, 2 , bit31| 1 ) if err != nil { return // UNAVAILABLE: the physics plugin is off } grounded := ok bodies, terrain, total, _ := burrowsdk.PhysicsOverlap( [ 3 ] float32 {t.Pos[ 0 ] - 1 , t.Pos[ 1 ] - 1 , t.Pos[ 2 ] - 1 }, [ 3 ] float32 {t.Pos[ 0 ] + 1 , t.Pos[ 1 ] + 1 , t.Pos[ 2 ] + 1 }, bit31| 1 , 16 ) burrowsdk.Logf( "grounded %v on %d, %d bodies near (listed %d), terrain %v" , grounded, hit.Entity, total, len(bodies), terrain) }, }) } func main() {} Physics components and bodies Physics bodies are ordinary components, so scripts configure them with Get / Set , field access and the typed accessors ( entities ): physics.body , physics.velocity , physics.character (set its move and jump intent fields before the physics step), physics3d.rigidbody , physics3d.collider , physics3d.voxelbody , physics3d.joint . Fields, ranges and defaults: reference/components.md . Writes follow the usual rule: validated now, applied at commit. physics3d adds direct calls: function what it does errors Physics3DApplyImpulse(e, impulse) adds a momentum impulse (mass x blocks per second) to a dynamic body, applied at the next physics step, wakes it UNAVAILABLE , NOT_FOUND (not a dynamic body), INVALID (non-finite) Physics3DBody(e) Body3D state: Pos (centre of mass, world), Rot (quaternion x, y, z, w), Vel (blocks per second), AngVel (radians per second, world frame), Sleeping , Dynamic , Kinematic , InvMass UNAVAILABLE , NOT_FOUND (no rigid body) Physics3DRemoveVoxel(e, x, y, z) clears one cell of a voxel body (grid coordinates inside the body, not world cells); returns whether the cell held a voxel; disconnected islands split off at the next step UNAVAILABLE , NOT_FOUND (no voxel body), BUDGET These three act on the physics state immediately , not through the buffered effect list: a later fault of the same call does not undo them. Body3D values are float32 views of the float64 simulation. A body writes its node transform every tick it moves, so drive bodies with impulses, velocity or intent and not with SetTransform . Navigation and AI Needs runtime.plugins.nav and a node with the matching component; otherwise every call is NOT_FOUND (the component does not exist). All calls edit the nav components like Set : validated now, applied at commit, reads see this call's writes. Concepts and budgets: navigation and AI . function needs what it does errors NavSetGoal(e, goal, slack) nav.agent send the agent to the feet voxel goal ( NavNode{X, Y, Z} ); slack blocks away counts as arrived (0 = the node) INVALID (slack negative or NaN, coordinate beyond +-1,048,575), NOT_FOUND NavStop(e) nav.agent clear goal and path, state becomes idle NOT_FOUND NavGetState(e) nav.agent NavIdle 0, NavPending 1, NavQueued 2, NavMoving 3, NavArrived 4, NavFailed 5 NOT_FOUND NavPath(e) nav.agent waypoints still to visit ( []NavNode , at most 128) NOT_FOUND NavSetBB(e, key, v) ai.brain number on the behaviour tree blackboard INVALID (NaN or Inf, key over 128 bytes), LIMIT (key over 32 bytes or 64 keys already), NOT_FOUND NavGetBB(e, key) ai.brain read a blackboard number NOT_FOUND (unset key too) NavPutBB(e, key, v) ai.brain typed blackboard value BBValue ( BBNum , BBVec , BBEnt , BBStr up to 64 bytes) INVALID (bad kind, NaN or Inf), LIMIT , NOT_FOUND NavReadBB(e, key) ai.brain read a typed blackboard value NOT_FOUND (unset key too) NavDelBB(e, key) ai.brain remove a blackboard key NOT_FOUND NavSetGoalPos(e, pos, slack) nav.agent like NavSetGoal with a world position ( NavVec3 , floored to its voxel) as NavSetGoal NavSensed(e) ai.perception nearest remembered target, 0 for none NOT_FOUND Timing: NavSetGoal does not compute a path in the call. The state goes Pending (goal set), Queued (request in the deterministic queue), then Moving or Failed a few ticks later within the plugin's per-tick budget; a Failed agent retries after a delay. Calling NavSetGoal again within 2 blocks of the current goal while the agent is pending, queued or moving only updates slack and keeps the path. Poll NavGetState for NavArrived . package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { st, err := burrowsdk.NavGetState(self) if err != nil { return // no nav.agent } switch st { case burrowsdk.NavIdle, burrowsdk.NavArrived, burrowsdk.NavFailed: if target, _ := burrowsdk.NavSensed(self); target != 0 { if p, err := burrowsdk.GetTransform(target); err == nil { _ = burrowsdk.NavSetGoal(self, burrowsdk.NavNode{X: int32 (p.Pos[ 0 ]), Y: int32 (p.Pos[ 1 ]), Z: int32 (p.Pos[ 2 ])}, 1.5 ) _ = burrowsdk.NavSetBB(self, "alert" , 1 ) } } } }, }) } func main() {} Levels and saves Needs the level plugin ( runtime.plugins.levels ) and the save plugin ( runtime.plugins.saves ); without them the calls are UNAVAILABLE (the editor's Play mode has no level plugin). Concepts and file formats: levels and saves . Requests. LevelLoad , SaveSlot , LoadSlot and DeleteSlot only queue a request, served by the host between frames (a level switch becomes a journaled command). They return success whatever the host does later, so a script behaves the same live and in a replay; a missing level or slot is not reported to the script. The cost is one event of the budget ( BUDGET ). function what it does errors LevelLoad(id, spawn) switch to level id at spawn point spawn ( "" = default); id and spawn match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63} INVALID , UNAVAILABLE , BUDGET SaveSlot(slot, label) save the game to a slot, served at the start of the next frame, between ticks (with several ticks per frame the snapshot is taken after all of them) INVALID , UNAVAILABLE LoadSlot(slot) restore a slot at the same point INVALID , UNAVAILABLE DeleteSlot(slot) delete a slot INVALID , UNAVAILABLE A slot name is [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47} ; a label is at most 128 bytes. Queries of the loaded level (read-only, no budget beyond the call): function what it does errors LevelCurrent() id of the loaded level, "" when none UNAVAILABLE LevelSpawnCount() number of spawn points NOT_FOUND (no level loaded), UNAVAILABLE LevelSpawnAt(i) LevelSpawn{Name, Pos, Yaw, Tags} ; Pos in world blocks NOT_FOUND (bad index or no level) LevelZoneAt(x, y, z) first zone (in file order) containing the world point; ok = false when none NOT_FOUND (no level) LevelSettings() JSON of the level settings NOT_FOUND (no level) LevelZone{Name, Kind, Min, Max, Target, TargetSpawn, Props} : Kind is "zone" or "trigger" ; Min (inclusive) and Max (exclusive) are level-local blocks, relative to the level's minimum corner, while the query point is in world blocks. A trigger zone switches level by itself when an actor stands in it; scripts only read zones. LevelSettings keys (each present only when set): sky , weather , weather_intensity , fog ( density , color ), gravity , kill_y (level-local Y), bounds ( min , max , level-local). The engine itself enforces kill_y and bounds ; the rest is data for your game. Dynamic zones. ZoneSet(name, min, max, props) creates or replaces a zone at run time and ZoneDel(name) removes it (no error when absent); both apply at commit and return INVALID or UNAVAILABLE (no level plugin). min and max are world blocks (unlike the level-local zones of the file). Dynamic zones are simulation state: rolled back, hashed and saved with the game, and cleared on a level switch . LevelZoneAt checks the zones of the loaded level first (file order), then the zones made by scripts. burrowsdk.ZoneSet( "arena" , [ 3 ] float32 { 0 , 10 , 0 }, [ 3 ] float32 { 8 , 14 , 8 }, map [ string ] string { "team" : "red" }) z, ok, _ := burrowsdk.LevelZoneAt( 2 , 11 , 2 ) // ok, z.Name == "arena" Game data (save keys). SaveSet , SaveGet , SaveDelete read and write a key/value store that is part of the simulation state: it is hashed, rolled back and saved with the game. function what it does errors SaveSet(key, val) store a string, applied at commit INVALID , UNAVAILABLE , BUDGET SaveGet(key) (val, ok, err) ; ok = false when the key is not set; sees this call's own writes UNAVAILABLE SaveDelete(key) remove a key INVALID , UNAVAILABLE , BUDGET Key [A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]{1,128} , value at most 64 KiB (bytes, so store JSON or text), at most 1024 keys and 1 MiB of keys and values together. Going over the totals is not an error at the call: the write fails at commit and shows as a non-fatal fault in the console. package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { p, err := burrowsdk.GetTransform(self) if err != nil { return } zone, ok, err := burrowsdk.LevelZoneAt(p.Pos[ 0 ], p.Pos[ 1 ], p.Pos[ 2 ]) if err != nil || !ok || zone.Name != "checkpoint" { return } if _, seen, _ := burrowsdk.SaveGet( "checkpoint.reached" ); !seen { _ = burrowsdk.SaveSet( "checkpoint.reached" , "1" ) _ = burrowsdk.SaveSlot( "auto" , "checkpoint" ) } }, }) } func main() {} Block data and block events With runtime.plugins.blocks a script can attach data to a cell that holds a block (the block entity of a machine) and receive the changes of the world. Full guide, scaling figures and an example furnace: blocks . The block calls are binary where they are hot (a few instructions per cell), because decoding JSON in a guest costs tens of thousands of instructions per cell. function what it does errors BlockData(x, y, z) data of the cell, ok = false when it has none; sees this call's writes UNAVAILABLE (plugin off) SetBlockData(x, y, z, data) / SetBlockDataJSON store up to 16 KiB; the cell must hold a block (a pending SetVoxel counts) INVALID (air), LIMIT , BUDGET , UNAVAILABLE DeleteBlockData(x, y, z) remove it BUDGET , UNAVAILABLE BlockDataIn(min, max, limit) cells with data in a box, sorted by x, y, z (committed state) INVALID , UNAVAILABLE BlockDataMany(cells) the data of up to 4,096 cells in one host call (binary) INVALID , LIMIT , UNAVAILABLE BlockDataApply(ops) up to 4,096 set or delete operations in one host call (binary), each counted as a voxel edit INVALID , LIMIT , BUDGET BlockSchedule(x, y, z, delay, every) / BlockUnschedule make a cell a ticking machine delivered to OnBlockTick when due INVALID (air), BUDGET , UNAVAILABLE BlockFlood(x, y, z, through, ends, max) the cable, pipe or belt network connected to a cell, walked natively (up to 60,000 cells) INVALID , UNAVAILABLE OnBlockChange , OnBlockSet(name) , OnBlockBreak(name) , OnBlockUse(name) , OnBlockTick(name) , OnBlockRandomTick(name) handlers for the block events, delivered in batches; random ticks need "random_tick": true on the block and runtime.random_tick_rate (default 24 per chunk), see blocks OnContact(fn) contacts and trigger overlaps of the script's own physics3d rigid body, both sides of the pair ( Contact{Kind, Other, Point, Normal} , kinds ContactBegin , ContactEnd , TriggerEnter , TriggerExit ); handled the tick after the physics step, in step order, counted in the per-tick event budget. The physics.character controller does not produce them FluidAmount , FluidPour , FluidDrain read, add and remove water of a cell, in units of FluidFull (64) per full cell; they act at once INVALID , REJECTED (outside the world), BUDGET , UNAVAILABLE On a micro-voxel brick the events name the micro voxel: BlockEvent.MicroN (the brick resolution, 0 for a whole-cell event), Micro ( [x, y, z] ) and MicroBlock . A use event reports the micro voxel's block in Block / ID (so OnBlockUse("mymod:lamp") fires for a lamp chiselled into a brick) and a micro change goes through OnBlockBreak(old) / OnBlockSet(new) with the micro blocks (see docs/blocks.md "Micro block events"). The data is bound to the block of the cell: another block there deletes it, and the OnBlockBreak / OnBlockChange event carries what was lost. Writes follow the same commit rules as SetVoxel (at commit, in order, dropped by a fault); a block write budget of 4096 edits per call counts data writes too. Project data and registries ReadAsset(path) returns the bytes of a project data file; ReadAssetJSON (generic over the target type T , same path rules) decodes JSON into T (a decoding failure is a plain error ). Items, recipes and balance tables belong here: the engine has no item registry. Rules: path is project-relative with / separators, at most 512 bytes: no .. , no absolute path, no backslash, no segment starting with . , not vox.project . A violation is DENIED . Extension one of .json .txt .csv .tsv .md .toml .yaml .yml .dat , else DENIED . The file must be known to the project's asset database ( NOT_FOUND otherwise, also when the host has no database) and at most 256 KiB ( LIMIT ). At most 16 files are read from disk per script call ( BUDGET ). Gas: 200 + 1 per 64 bytes. Frozen and pinned. Data files are not simulation state, so replays stay exact like this: the first content a session sees for a path is frozen, and every script remembers the hash of each file it read (up to 64 files, LIMIT after that; part of its hashed state). Re-reading a file you already read is served from that frozen copy and does not use one of the 16 disk reads. Editing a data file while the game runs does not change what scripts see; restoring or replaying against a different file fails the tick with an error that names the file. Read in OnStart and keep what you need in State , since a Go script parses JSON slowly. function what it does errors Registry("components") scene schema component names UNAVAILABLE Registry("assets") readable data files (extension rule above), sorted, at most 4096, frozen per session NOT_FOUND (no database) Registry("blocks") block names, index = id see block registry package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" type item struct { Name string `json:"name"` Weight float64 `json:"weight"` } func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnStart: func (self burrowsdk.Entity) { items, err := burrowsdk.ReadAssetJSON[ map [ string ]item]( "data/items.json" ) if err != nil { burrowsdk.Logf( "items: %v" , err) return } if id, err := burrowsdk.BlockByName( "stone" ); err == nil { info, _ := burrowsdk.BlockInfo(id) burrowsdk.Logf( "%d items, stone is block %d (solid %v)" , len(items), id, info.Solid) } files, _ := burrowsdk.Registry( "assets" ) burrowsdk.Logf( "%d readable data files" , len(files)) }, }) } func main() {} See also Entities and scene : components and transforms that bodies and agents use.
