Input, events and time How a script reads player input, talks to other scripts through events and the message bus, schedules work with timers, and animates values with tweens, all in deterministic simulation time. Signatures are in reference/script-api.md . Error codes: 1 INVALID , 3 NOT_FOUND , 5 BUDGET , 7 UNAVAILABLE , 9 LIMIT ( errors and limits ). Time The simulation runs at a fixed rate: 20 ticks per second unless runtime.tick_rate says 30, 40 or 60 (see determinism ). OnTick receives dt = 1 / rate (0.05 s at 20 Hz) every time; burrowsdk.Tick() is the index of the current tick and the only clock a script has. Everything below counts ticks (20 ticks = 1 second at the default rate); the ...Seconds forms and burrowsdk.TickRate() keep a script right if the rate changes. There is no wall clock and no randomness outside Rand , so timers, tweens and cooldowns stop when the simulation pauses and replay exactly. Order inside one script run: OnStart (first tick only), then queued events and fired timers (see delivery order ), then OnTick . One script's run is committed before the next script starts ( execution model ). Input Action(name) (x, y float32, ok bool) reads one input action as of the current tick. action kind x y button 0 or 1 0 axis1d the axis value 0 axis2d x of the value y of the value ok is false when no action has that name, when the project has no input plugin, or before any input has been sampled. No error value is returned. Precision is three decimals: the host passes thousandths ( float32(milli)/1000 ), clamped to +-1000 . Axes from sticks and composites are in -1..1 after dead zone and sensitivity. Relative actions (mouse delta, scroll and mouse-axis bindings) are not levels but amounts: they are the sum of all motion since the previous tick, in pixels (or wheel steps) times the action's sensitivity , so they can exceed 1. The first tick after a frame consumes them: if the game runs several ticks to catch up, the later ticks read 0 and the motion is applied once. A script gets levels, not edges . Derive "pressed" and "released" from your own State , as below. The value is the latest snapshot taken before the tick; a press that starts and ends between two ticks (under 50 ms) is not seen, so do not rely on one-frame taps for critical actions. A paused game journals no input, and motion made while paused is dropped, so resuming does not replay it as one big camera turn. package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" type jumpState struct { WasDown bool `json:"was_down"` Presses int `json:"presses"` } func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { st, _ := burrowsdk.LoadState[jumpState]() down := false if x, _, ok := burrowsdk.Action( "jump" ); ok { down = x > 0.5 } if down && !st.WasDown { // rising edge st.Presses++ burrowsdk.Logf( "jump pressed %d times" , st.Presses) } st.WasDown = down _ = burrowsdk.SaveState(st) mx, my, _ := burrowsdk.Action( "move" ) // axis2d: x strafe, y forward lx, ly, _ := burrowsdk.Action( "look" ) // mouse movement since the last tick _, _, _, _ = mx, my, lx, ly }, }) } func main() {} Input map ( input.json ) Scripts read actions , never keys. The project file named by input_map in vox.project (conventionally input.json ) defines them; without it the engine's default map is used ( reference/input-actions.md lists its actions: move , look , jump , sprint , break , place , hotbar1 .. hotbar9 , ...). A map that fails to load is logged and the default stays. { "version" : 1 , "contexts" : [ { "name" : "gameplay" , "priority" : 0 , "enabled" : true , "actions" : [ { "name" : "move" , "kind" : "axis2d" , "bindings" : [ { "type" : "composite2d" , "up" : "W" , "down" : "S" , "left" : "A" , "right" : "D" }, { "type" : "pad_stick" , "scale" : 1 , "deadzone" : 0.15 } ] }, { "name" : "look" , "kind" : "axis2d" , "sensitivity" : 0.12 , "bindings" : [ { "type" : "mouse_delta" } ] }, { "name" : "jump" , "kind" : "button" , "bindings" : [ { "type" : "key" , "key" : "Space" }, { "type" : "pad_button" , "button" : 0 } ] } ] } ] } element fields file version (must be 1 ), contexts context name , priority (higher wins), enabled (default true), modal (lower contexts are ignored while it is active), actions action name , kind ( button , axis1d , axis2d ), deadzone (0..1, radial for 2D), sensitivity (multiplier after the dead zone, 0 = 1), consume (its bindings are hidden from lower-priority contexts) binding type key , mouse_button , mouse_axis , scroll , pad_button , pad_axis , composite1d ( neg , pos ), composite2d ( up , down , left , right ), mouse_delta , mouse_pos (pointer position -1..1 , needs a free cursor), pad_stick ( axis , scale , deadzone ) binding extras mods ( ctrl , shift , alt ), exclusive , scale Which binding types suit which kind, key names and the parse errors (the loader names the JSON path and suggests the intended spelling) are in the input package ( input actions reference lists them). Rules at runtime: A button is 1 while any of its bindings is active (an analog binding needs a value of at least 0.5). An axis takes the strongest of its bindings. The context with the highest priority that has the action active owns it; actions of a context with enabled: false read 0 . Scripts cannot enable or disable a context. The template projects ( burrow new ) ship an input.json ready to edit. What the window reports runner keys and buttons that reach the map game window ( burrow run , burrowplay , exported games) every physical key by US-layout position (layout independent), all mouse buttons, mouse movement, scroll, modifiers, and the first connected gamepad editor Play mode only while the pointer is over the viewport: letters a - z , digits 0 - 9 , Space, Tab, Enter, the arrow keys, left Shift, left Ctrl, the left, right and middle mouse buttons, mouse movement (pointer travel between two frames, none on the first frame over the viewport), the wheel, and the first connected gamepad. Not routed: Esc (it stops Play), function keys and the other modifiers. Before 0.2.2 movement, wheel, arrows and gamepad were missing. The pointer is not captured, so a mouse-look game turns only while you drag across the viewport. Typed text is for UI fields only; scripts do not receive it. In a multiplayer session the local device snapshot is replaced by per-player input ( multiplayer ). Frame look Mouse look read from Action("look") arrives once per tick (20 Hz). To make the view turn at frame rate without changing the simulation, set frame_look on the camera_rig component of a first or third person rig to the degrees per mouse pixel your script applies (range 0..10, 0 = off). The rig then adds the mouse motion no tick has consumed yet to the target's look angles and drops it when a tick completes. The script still receives the summed motion once per tick, so no double rotation happens. The value must equal the script's own sensitivity; other rig kinds ignore it. There is no script call for it: it is a field of the component ( cameras ). "camera_rig" : { "name" : "fp" , "kind" : "first_person" , "frame_look" : 0.12 } Events between scripts Emit(target, kind, payload) queues an event for another script (or for all). The receiver gets it in OnEvent(self, ev Event) with Event{From, Kind, Payload} . function what it does errors Emit(target, kind, payload) queue an event; target 0 = every script (the sender included) NOT_FOUND (dead target), LIMIT (payload over 1024 bytes), BUDGET , MEMORY Commit, then next tick. The event is queued with the call and appended to the receivers' inboxes when the sender's run commits. It is delivered in the next tick or later, never in the tick that sent it, even to a receiver that runs after the sender. kind is an application number (any int32 ). Use values below 0x40000000 : 0x40000000..0x7fff0000 are bus topics and 0x7fff0001 is the timer kind ( below ), and the SDK routes them to bus and timer handlers before OnEvent . From is the emitting entity. Payload is at most 1 KiB of opaque bytes; copy it if you keep it, because it is only valid during the handler. A target that has no script component, or is despawned before the commit, is skipped silently. A target that is a pending handle from this call (a node you just spawned) is resolved at commit. Budgets: 64 events per call and 4096 per tick ( BUDGET ). A broadcast counts as one. Inbox. Each script holds at most 64 undelivered events. A further event to a full inbox is dropped and reported as a non-fatal fault in the console naming the receiver; the sender gets no error. The inbox is emptied each time the script runs, so overflow needs more than 64 events aimed at one script between two of its runs. A script without OnEvent still consumes its events (they are dropped). package main import ( "encoding/binary" "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" ) const kindDamage = 1 func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { if target, err := burrowsdk.FindByName( "boss" ); err == nil && burrowsdk.Tick()% 40 == 0 { var p [ 4 ] byte binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(p[:], 7 ) if err := burrowsdk.Emit(target, kindDamage, p[:]); err != nil { burrowsdk.Logf( "emit: %v" , err) } } }, OnEvent: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, ev burrowsdk.Event) { if ev.Kind == kindDamage && len(ev.Payload) == 4 { burrowsdk.Logf( "%d took %d damage from %d" , self, binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(ev.Payload), ev.From) } }, }) } func main() {} Engine events (trigger enter/exit, collisions) are frame-domain and are not delivered to scripts. Poll instead: PhysicsOverlap diffed against the previous tick's result kept in State , game UI events , or LevelCurrent . Delivery order Everything a script receives comes from one queue, in a fixed order: OnStart (first tick of the script only). Inbox events in arrival order. Arrival order is the commit order: scripts run in ascending entity id, and one run's emits and publishes keep their call order. Direct events and bus messages share the queue. Fired timers, ordered by (due tick, timer id). OnTick . A script that faults keeps its inbox and gets the same events again next tick ( errors ). Message bus The bus is publish/subscribe by topic name. Subscriptions are stored in the script component, so they survive the guest memory reset, snapshots and replays. function what it does errors OnMessage(topic, fn) register a handler from init() ; the SDK subscribes for you before OnStart and OnTick panics at load on two topics whose kinds collide Publish(topic, payload) send to every script subscribed to topic INVALID (bad topic), LIMIT (payload over 1024 bytes), BUDGET Subscribe(topic) subscribe without a handler; read it in OnEvent with BusKind(topic) INVALID , LIMIT (more than 32 topics) Unsubscribe(topic) drop a subscription (no error if not subscribed) INVALID BusKind(topic) the Event.Kind a topic arrives with: 0x40000000 + FNV-1a32(topic) % 0x3fff0000 none A topic is [A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]{1,64} . At most 32 subscriptions per script (idempotent: subscribing twice counts once). Publish takes effect at commit. The message goes to every subscribed script in ascending entity order, the publisher included if it subscribed, and arrives in a later tick with from = the publisher. A subscription made in a run counts for publishes committed after that run commits; a message published earlier in the same tick is not delivered to it. Each delivery uses one unit of the per-tick event budget (4096), plus a small charge for scanning the scripts. When the tick budget runs out the remaining deliveries are dropped with a non-fatal fault, and a full inbox drops a message the same way. Publish costs gas: 48 + 1 per 64 payload bytes + 1 per 8 scripts in the scene, even with no subscriber. A handler registered with OnMessage is re-subscribed by the SDK whenever the host holds fewer subscriptions than there are handlers. Unsubscribe on such a topic is therefore undone on the next call; remove the handler instead. package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" func init() { burrowsdk.OnMessage( "door.open" , func (self, from burrowsdk.Entity, payload [] byte ) { burrowsdk.Logf( "door opened by %d: %q" , from, payload) _ = burrowsdk.After( 1 , 60 ) // close again in 3 s }) burrowsdk.OnTimer( 1 , func (self burrowsdk.Entity) { _ = burrowsdk.Publish( "door.close" , nil ) }) burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnStart: func (self burrowsdk.Entity) { _ = burrowsdk.Every( 2 , 20 ) }, }) } func main() {} Timers Timers are kept by the host in the script component, in ticks. function what it does errors After(id, n) fire timer id once, n ticks from now ( n < 1 is 1) INVALID (negative id), LIMIT Every(id, n) fire every n ticks, the first time n ticks from now ( n < 1 is 1) as above AfterSeconds(id, sec) / EverySeconds(id, sec) After / Every in seconds, rounded up to whole ticks; they stay correct when runtime.tick_rate changes as above TimerStart(id, delay, every) raw form: first firing delay ticks after the next tick, then every every ticks (0 = once) INVALID (negative, or over 2^30), LIMIT CancelTimer(id) disarm NOT_FOUND if not armed TimerRemaining(id) ticks before it fires ( 0 = at the start of the next tick) NOT_FOUND if not armed OnTimer(id, fn) handler for a timer id, registered in init() none Ids are your own non-negative int32 numbers, per script. At most 64 armed timers per script; arming an id that exists replaces it (no LIMIT ). After(id, n) armed in tick T fires at the start of tick T + n : After(id, 1) is the next tick. A timer never fires in the tick that armed it. The effect of arming is stored when your run commits. Every keeps its phase: a period is never shifted by the time spent in handlers. If a script missed periods (it was disabled), the timer fires once and continues on its original phase. A one-shot timer is removed before its handler runs, so the handler can re-arm it. A firing is delivered as an event of kind KindTimer ( 0x7fff0001 ) with a 4-byte little-endian id payload; OnTimer handles it for you. A timer with no OnTimer handler arrives in OnEvent with that kind. All timers count simulation ticks: they stop with a paused game and replay exactly. Use Cooldown below for state kept by hand. Tweens and easing A Tween is plain data evaluated at a tick. It runs no goroutine and holds no hidden state, so it can live in State as JSON and replays exactly. item meaning Tween{From, To, Start, Dur, Ease} Start and Dur in ticks; JSON keys from , to , start , dur , ease NewTween(from, to, dur, ease) start now ( Start = Tick() ); dur < 1 becomes 1 t.At(tick) value at tick : From at or before Start , To from Start+Dur on (progress is clamped), and From always if Dur is 0 t.Now() At(Tick()) t.Done(tick) tick >= Start + Dur Lerp(a, b, t) a + (b-a)*t , no clamping EaseKind.Apply(t) the curve at progress t ; t is clamped to [0,1] , NaN counts as 0 A tween advances only because you evaluate it: call Now() in OnTick , store the tween once. Progress at tick k is (k - Start) / Dur , so a tween started at tick S with Dur = 30 shows From at tick S , and reaches To at tick S + 30 . Easing curves ( t in 0..1 ; the result is in 0..1 except where noted): EaseKind formula Linear t InQuad / OutQuad / InOutQuad t^2 / 1-(1-t)^2 / 2t^2 then 1-(2-2t)^2/2 InCubic / OutCubic / InOutCubic t^3 / 1-(1-t)^3 / 4t^3 then 1-(2-2t)^3/2 InSine / OutSine / InOutSine 1-cos(t*pi/2) / sin(t*pi/2) / -(cos(pi*t)-1)/2 OutBack 1 + 2.70158(t-1)^3 + 1.70158(t-1)^2 ; overshoots 1 (to about 1.1) before settling OutBounce the standard four-bounce curve ( 7.5625 t^2 pieces, ends at exactly 1) SmoothStep t^2 (3-2t) Cooldown{Until} is a tick deadline for "can act again in N ticks": c.Start(n) sets Until = Tick()+n ( n < 0 is 0), c.Ready() is Tick() >= Until ; the zero value is ready. Keep it in State (JSON key until ). Determinism: curves and Lerp are float64 code compiled into the guest, so they give the same bits on every machine; a stored tween round-trips exactly through JSON. package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" type doorState struct { Anim burrowsdk.Tween `json:"anim"` Cool burrowsdk.Cooldown `json:"cool"` } func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnStart: func (self burrowsdk.Entity) { st, _ := burrowsdk.LoadState[doorState]() st.Anim = burrowsdk.NewTween( 0 , 90 , 30 , burrowsdk.OutBounce) // 1.5 s st.Cool.Start( 100 ) _ = burrowsdk.SaveState(st) }, OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { st, _ := burrowsdk.LoadState[doorState]() if !st.Anim.Done(burrowsdk.Tick()) { _ = burrowsdk.SetFloat(self, "transform" , "rot[1]" , st.Anim.Now()) } if st.Cool.Ready() { // can act again } }, }) } func main() {} See also Execution model : tick order, commit, faults. x: Effects: audio, particles, animation, cameras, UI, models What a script can trigger outside the simulation core, and which of it is replayed, hashed or only presented. Two domains domain functions when applied in the StateHash replay frame (presentation) Audio* , Particle* , Camera* , UI* setters queued at commit, delivered after the tick, in call order no the same requests are re-emitted when ticks are re-executed simulation Anim* , SpawnModel , UIEvents (read) Anim* and SpawnModel : at commit, like Set / Spawn ; UIEvents : reads the journaled inbox now yes exact Rules for every frame-domain call: Queued with the buffered effects of the transaction: if the script faults, its sounds, bursts, camera and UI requests are dropped with everything else. Deterministic and never read back. There is no return value that depends on the presentation (a handle is derived from the tick, never from the mixer). A script cannot learn whether a sound loaded, a voice was stolen, a rig exists or a screen exists. Ignored, with nil error, when the plugin is off: runtime.plugins.audio: false , particles: false , camera: false , gameui: false in vox.project (all on by default, see project-config ). App.VerifyReplay and rolled-back ticks drop the requests; headless runs with the plugin installed process them (audio on the silent null backend). The StateHash is identical with or without them. Each request costs one host call and one event of the budget (64 per script per tick, 4096 per tick overall, shared with Emit and Publish ; see errors and limits ). Over budget the call returns BUDGET (code 5). A HUD that sets 70 keys every tick exhausts it: set a key only when it changes. A NaN or Inf in SoundOpts / ParticleOpts makes the SDK's JSON encoding fail silently and the call goes out with no options (defaults). In the camera and UI setters it returns the Go encoding error instead of a *burrowsdk.Error . Argument errors come back at call time: INVALID (1) for NaN or out-of-range numbers, REJECTED (8) for malformed option JSON, LIMIT (9) for oversized options, UNAVAILABLE (7) outside a tick. Validation of the engine side (unknown rig, unknown screen, missing file) happens later, in the frame, and is silent for the script. Per frame the plugins consume a bounded number of requests and drop the rest: camera 64, game UI 128, particles 256. Audio has no such cap, but the mixer has 32 voices by default. See the generated signatures in Script API . Audio Plugin: runtime.plugins.audio . Subsystem: audio . function what it does errors PlayOn(entity, name, SoundOpts) (SoundHandle, error) start a sound emitted by an entity (self or another node), return its handle INVALID : no entity (0), a pending entity, unknown Mode , empty name, name over 256 bytes, unknown bus, NaN, volume or pitch outside 0..8 or negative, fade NaN. NOT_FOUND : no such entity. REJECTED : bad options JSON AudioStop(h, fade) fade the sound out over fade seconds (0..60, clamped) INVALID : handle 0 AudioSet(h, volume, pitch) change a playing sound; a negative value keeps the parameter INVALID : handle 0, NaN, a value over 8 AudioBus(bus, volume) volume of sfx , music , ambient , ui or master , 0..4 INVALID : unknown bus, NaN, outside 0..4 AudioListener(e) use entity e as the ears; 0 returns to the default listener NOT_FOUND : no such entity SoundOpts (zero value = all defaults): field default range Bus sfx sfx , music , ambient , ui Volume 1 0..8 (0 means 1, not silence) Pitch 1 0.05..8 after clamping (0 means 1) Loop false Priority 0 -100..100; a higher priority survives voice stealing Fade 0 fade-in seconds Mode localized global (every player, no position), local (one player, no position) or localized (3D at the entity: distance attenuation, panning, occlusion through voxels) Player 0 local only: the player that hears it; 0 = the player owning the entity, else the local player Offset none localized only: position relative to the entity Breaking change. Every sound comes from an entity placed in the scene. AudioPlay , AudioPlayAt and AudioMusic are gone; the music is the audio.music component of an entity (write its sound / context fields with the component functions). The raw audio_music host function always returns DENIED . Names. A sound name is a project-relative path to a .wav or .ogg file ( assets/sfx/coin.ogg ), read through the project source (files in a packed game included, 64 MiB per file). Files are decoded on first use, at most 8 new loads per frame; a sound requested while the budget is spent is skipped. builtin:<name> is documented in the SDK comment and used by some templates, but the engine has no builtin sounds any more (the synthesised set was removed), so such a call returns a handle and plays nothing. Sound pack. The pack (default and user packs, sounds.json ) belongs to the engine's ambience hook: it maps engine events ( step.stone , ui.click , music scheduling) to files and plays them itself. Scripts cannot trigger pack events and the pack cannot see script sounds. They share the same mixer: buses, the 32-voice limit and ducking (a sound on ui lowers music and ambient ) apply to both. The audio.music component picks between the pack's scheduler and a looped sound asset, so a game that drives its music from a script writes that component instead of fighting the pack. Handles. SoundHandle is positive and derived from (entity, entry point, tick, request index): a replay produces the same values, and it is valid for the voice that call started. A handle may be kept in State and used in later ticks as long as the voice exists. AudioStop / AudioSet on a finished, stolen or never-started voice succeed and do nothing. A one-shot ends by itself; only loops need a stop. Other details. AudioSet clamps: volume 0..8, pitch 0.05..8. Here 0 really sets 0 (silent) and 0.05 for pitch; only negative means "keep". It cannot move a 3D sound (position is fixed at play time). AudioListener beats an audio_listener component and the camera. If the entity is despawned the default listener comes back. Without a sound device or in headless runs the null backend runs the mixer silently. package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" type state struct { Engine burrowsdk.SoundHandle `json:"engine"` } func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnStart: func (self burrowsdk.Entity) { h, err := burrowsdk.PlayOn(self, "assets/sfx/engine.ogg" , burrowsdk.SoundOpts{Bus: "ambient" , Loop: true , Volume: 0.6 , Fade: 1 }) if err == nil { _ = burrowsdk.SaveState(state{Engine: h}) } }, OnDestroy: func (self burrowsdk.Entity) { st, _ := burrowsdk.LoadState[state]() _ = burrowsdk.AudioStop(st.Engine, 0.5 ) }, }) } func main() {} Particles Plugin: runtime.plugins.particles . Subsystem: particles . function what it does errors ParticleBurstOn(entity, effect, ParticleOpts) one-shot effect emitted by an entity (self or another node), at Offset from it; lives on its own INVALID : no entity (0), empty or over-long (256) effect, huge offset, count outside 0..4096, scale outside 0..16. NOT_FOUND : no such entity. REJECTED : bad options JSON ParticleBlockBreakOn(entity, block, ox, oy, oz) debris of a broken block, centred on the offset from the entity as above ParticleEmit(e, count) emit count extra particles from the particle_emitter component of e INVALID : entity 0, count outside 1..4096. NOT_FOUND : no such entity ParticleStop(e) stop the emitter of e and clear its particles; entity 0 clears every particle NOT_FOUND : no such entity Shockwave(entity, ox, oy, oz, radius, strength, duration) expanding ring of distorted air emitted by an entity, centred on its position plus the offset (heat-haze style lens ripple, see rendering.md "Air distortion"): grows to radius blocks over duration seconds and fades; needs shader level medium and up INVALID : no entity (0), NaN or huge offset, radius outside 0..256, strength outside 0..8 (0 means 1), duration outside 0..30 s effect is builtin:smoke , sparks , dust , splash , fire , debris or a .particles.json project path. ParticleOpts : Offset (from the emitter, default at it; Entity is filled by ParticleBurstOn ), Dir (emission axis override, world space), Count (default the asset's burst, else 16), Scale (size, spawn volume and speed multiplier, 0 means 1), Block (block name whose texture replaces the sprite, for debris). Randomness is seeded from the tick and the request index, so a replay shows the same burst. An unknown effect or block draws nothing and raises no error. ParticleEmit / ParticleStop need the entity only to exist: an entity without particle_emitter is accepted and ignored. An emitter is switched on and off with its enabled field ( Set / SetBool , simulation domain). _ = burrowsdk.ParticleBurstOn(self, "builtin:sparks" , burrowsdk.ParticleOpts{Offset: &[ 3 ] float32 { 4 , 20 , - 3 }, Count: 24 , Scale: 0.5 }) _ = burrowsdk.ParticleBlockBreakOn(self, "stone" , 4.5 , 20.5 , - 2.5 ) _ = burrowsdk.ParticleEmit(self, 50 ) Animation Not a frame-domain effect. Anim* edit the anim.player component of the entity: the change is applied at commit, journaled, hashed and replayed exactly, and the anim.step system advances the player with the fixed tick. Use it for animation that matters to gameplay (moving platforms, doors, hazards); purely visual animation runs in the frame domain on the host. Subsystem: animation . function what it does errors AnimPlay(e, clip, AnimPlayOpts) play clip now (or queued) NOT_FOUND : entity or its anim.player missing. LIMIT : queue already holds 64. INVALID : empty or over-long (128) clip name. NOT_FOUND also for entity 0 AnimStop(e) halt the player, the pose stays NOT_FOUND AnimSetSpeed(e, speed) speed multiplier, 0..100 (0 means 1) INVALID : NaN or outside the range AnimSetParam(e, name, v) set a state machine parameter (bool = 0/1) INVALID : NaN or Inf. LIMIT : 64 parameters already set AnimTrigger(e, name) raise a trigger parameter; the next transition that tests it consumes it NOT_FOUND AnimTime(e) (int64, error) playhead in microseconds NOT_FOUND AnimPlayOpts : Mode ( AnimMode : AnimDefault = the clip's flag, AnimOnce , AnimLoop , AnimPingPong ), Queue (play after the current clip ends; if nothing is playing it starts now), FadeMillis (crossfade, 0..65535 ms). The clip name is not checked: an unknown clip plays nothing and is not an error. Clips and machines come from .anim files of the project. AnimPlay detaches the player from its state machine ( machine and state are cleared); to drive a machine, set machine on the component and use AnimSetParam / AnimTrigger only. Reads see your own writes in the same call. Events crossed by the last advance are in anim.player.fired (read with FieldRaw(e, "anim.player", "fired") ), at most 256 per tick. The component must already be on the entity (scene or prefab); these calls never add it. _ = burrowsdk.AnimPlay(door, "open" , burrowsdk.AnimPlayOpts{Mode: burrowsdk.AnimOnce, FadeMillis: 150 }) _ = burrowsdk.AnimSetParam(door, "locked" , 0 ) _ = burrowsdk.AnimTrigger(door, "slam" ) Cameras Plugin: runtime.plugins.camera (also enabled by a scene that uses camera_rig ). Subsystem: cameras . Rig names are the name of a camera_rig component or of a rig in runtime.camera.rigs . function what it does errors CameraSwitch(rig, blend) activate a rig, blending over blend seconds INVALID : empty rig name, name over 64, blend NaN or outside 0..1000 CameraShake(amount) add trauma 0..1 (the total is capped at 1; amplitude grows with its square) INVALID : NaN or outside 0..1000 CameraCut() mark a discontinuity (teleport, respawn): temporal history is dropped none blend 0 is a cut that resets TAA/FSR2 history; blends longer than 30 s are clamped; switching between perspective and orthographic rigs always cuts; switching to the active rig is a no-op. An unknown rig is dropped in the frame without a trace in the script. Shake values above 1 are accepted and clamped by the controller. _ = burrowsdk.CameraSwitch( "iso" , 0.6 ) _ = burrowsdk.CameraShake( 0.4 ) Game UI Plugin: runtime.plugins.gameui . Subsystem: game UI . Screens are *.ui.json files named after the file (or listed in runtime.gameui.screens ). function what it does errors UISetNum(key, v) / UISetStr(key, v) / UISetBool(key, v) bind a value to key (bars, {key} in labels, bind_visible ) INVALID : NaN, over 1e15, string over 4096 bytes, key over 128 UISetItems(key, []UIItem) bind an item list (grid, list); UIItem{Icon, Text, Count} , empty Icon = empty slot INVALID : more than 4096 items, text or icon over 4096 UIShow(screen) / UIHide(screen) / UIToggle(screen) screen visibility INVALID : name over 128 UILocale(code) switch locale ( "" or over 16 bytes is dropped in the frame) UILabel(id, x, y, z, text, bar) persistent world-space nameplate; bar 0 = none, else (0,1] INVALID : NaN UIPopup(x, y, z, text, life) floating number that rises and fades over life seconds INVALID : NaN UIRemoveLabel(id) remove a nameplate UIEvents(since) ([]UIEvent, uint32) journaled UI events newer than since , and the latest sequence number no error: returns nothing without the plugin Details: Setters are frame domain and last-write-wins per key. An unknown screen, a full value store (1024 keys) or a pool of 128 labels / 128 popups drops the request in the frame. UIShow of a modal screen takes input focus. The host also accepts focus ( ui:focus ) and clear_labels and a label color / size ; the Go SDK has no wrapper for them (use a UI action in the .ui.json instead). Events back. A widget with "sim": true , or an action starting with sim: , becomes the journaled command gameui_event stored in a 32-event ring (simulation state, hashed). UIEvents returns events with Seq > since and the new last sequence; keep it in State : field meaning Seq increasing event number Screen , Widget screen name and widget id Kind click , select , move , use , change , submit , cancel Action the widget's action string Value text (input fields, up to 1 KiB) Index , To slot index; To is the destination of a move Poll every tick: the reply buffer is 4096 bytes. If the JSON of the pending events is larger (a full ring of long names can be), the call returns nothing and since does not advance. Events a widget does not mark sim never reach scripts. package main import "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" type state struct { Seen uint32 `json:"seen"` Coins int `json:"coins"` } func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { st, _ := burrowsdk.LoadState[state]() evs, last := burrowsdk.UIEvents(st.Seen) for _, e := range evs { if e.Kind == "click" && e.Action == "sim:buy" { st.Coins-- _ = burrowsdk.UISetNum( "coins" , float64 (st.Coins)) _ = burrowsdk.UIPopup( 0 , 12 , 0 , "-1" , 1 ) _ = burrowsdk.CameraShake( 0.2 ) } } if last != st.Seen { st.Seen = last _ = burrowsdk.SaveState(st) } }, }) } func main() {} Models SpawnModel(asset, voxelScale, SpawnOpts) (Entity, error) is Spawn with a render.voxmodel component ( cast_shadow on). It adds no host call: the spawn is an ordinary journaled command with the same rules and budgets as Spawn (32 per script per tick), and errors are Spawn 's. asset is a project path to a .bmodel or .vox ; voxelScale is the world size of one voxel (0 means 1/16). An unknown asset spawns the node and draws nothing (a warning is logged by the host). Model editing and character models: modeling , character . crate, err := burrowsdk.SpawnModel( "assets/models/crate.bmodel" , 0.0625 , burrowsdk.SpawnOpts{ Name: "crate" , Transform: &burrowsdk.Transform{Pos: [ 3 ] float32 { 4 , 10 , 4 }, Scale: [ 3 ] float32 { 1 , 1 , 1 }}, }) Editor overlay and editor commands DrawBox(min, max, opts) , DrawLine(a, b, opts) , DrawSphere(center, r, opts) and DrawLabel(pos, text, opts) ( DrawOpts{Color, Layer, Life} ) draw debug shapes in the editor viewport. EditorZoneAdd , EditorZoneRemove , EditorSpawnAdd and EditorSpawnRemove queue authoring edits for the level. All take world blocks. They are frame domain , like particles: queued at commit, never part of the simulation state (the state hash and replays are unchanged), and ignored when the game runs outside the editor. Life is a number of frames (0 = this frame only, at most 600); a label is at most 128 bytes and a layer name at most 32. The editor applies the queued Editor* commands to the level draft as one undo step when Play stops , so the edit survives the snapshot restore of Stop. Errors: INVALID for a bad shape or command. burrowsdk.DrawBox([ 3 ] float32 { 0 , 10 , 0 }, [ 3 ] float32 { 8 , 14 , 8 }, burrowsdk.DrawOpts{Color: burrowsdk.RGBA{ 255 , 80 , 0 , 255 }, Life: 60 }) burrowsdk.EditorZoneAdd( "arena" , [ 3 ] float32 { 0 , 10 , 0 }, [ 3 ] float32 { 8 , 14 , 8 }, map [ string ] string { "team" : "red" }) See also Execution model : transactions, commit, what a fault drops. Errors and limits : error codes, event and call budgets. Entities and scene : Spawn , components, tags. Multiplayer : effects run on every peer. Cookbook : sound on event, burst on hit, HUD counter. Script API reference , ABI . Subsystems: audio , particles , animation , cameras , game UI . Application control Plugin: none (the launcher, burrowplay , serves it). A script can quit the game, join or host a multiplayer game, play or create a world and go back to the title screen, the same things the game UI actions app:* , net:* and world:* do: burrowsdk.AppQuit() burrowsdk.NetJoin( "burrow://host:7777?fp=...&key=..." , "Ada" ) // name "" = the user name burrowsdk.NetHost( "Ada" ) // embedded server, you play on it; the join link is printed burrowsdk.WorldPlay( "w1" ) // a world is a save slot (docs/levels-saves.md) burrowsdk.WorldCreate( "w2" , "My world" , 0 , "flat" , "creative" ) // seed 0 = random, generator "" = the project's burrowsdk.Title() // back to the start scene burrowsdk.SetShaders( "high" ) // shader level, no restart (docs/rendering.md) burrowsdk.SetGraphics( "god_rays" , 32 ) // one graphics setting on top of the level burrowsdk.SetGraphicsOn( "bloom" , false ) burrowsdk.ResetGraphics() // back to the level's preset These are frame domain ( app_cmd ): they only queue a request that ends the windowed run when the invocation commits, then the launcher builds what was asked. The window stays open across the change, like in Minecraft: the old game shows the loading screen, the new one keeps it up while the world around the player streams in (the simulation is held meanwhile, so nobody falls through missing terrain; 15 s at most), then the game starts. To move between scenes of the same game without rebuilding it, use SceneSwitch . They never change the StateHash ; headless runs, replays and -shot runs ignore them, and only the first request of a run is served. A bad slot name or link returns INVALID .

h: Local input does not exist in a session
Ready-made base script: the multiplayer template
x: Multiplayer How scripts behave in a multiplayer session, which functions read the players, and what a script must never do. The protocol, hosting and joining are in networking . Who runs what Burrow multiplayer is server-authoritative ( replication ): the server runs the whole simulation, scripts included, and streams to each client what it needs. So: Only the server runs scripts. Clients run frame stages (rendering, UI, audio) on a replicated copy and never call a script. A script cannot tell which player is "local"; no SDK function returns a local player id. Keep per-player data under the player id and let the game's presentation code pick the local one. Script State never reaches a client. Anything a client must show or read (an inventory, a furnace, skills, a health bar) belongs in a component written by the script, with a visibility rule: everyone, the owner only, or nearby clients ( component visibility ). Rule of thumb: keep client-visible state in components, not in script State . A script may keep its working data in State and copy what clients show into the component when it changes. Frame-domain effects ( audio, particles, cameras, UI ) are requested by the scripts on the server, which has no plugins for them and ignores them; a client's own presentation code produces them from the replicated components. A script cannot play a sound "only for player 3". Opting in Add "net": true to runtime.plugins in vox.project . The plugin installs the hashed player registry ( net/netsim ), so a project without it keeps its old StateHash . Without it the three functions below return UNAVAILABLE (code 7), as they do outside a tick. Host with burrow serve , join with burrowplay -connect ; see networking . Player functions Reads of simulation state: free of side effects. function result errors NetPlayerCount() (int, error) number of connected players UNAVAILABLE without the plugin NetPlayerAt(i) (uint32, error) id of the i-th connected player, ascending ids UNAVAILABLE ; NOT_FOUND : i negative or past the end NetPlayerInfo(id) (NetPlayer, error) the player's record UNAVAILABLE ; NOT_FOUND : unknown id type NetPlayer struct { ID uint32 Name string Connected bool Input NetInput } Ids are assigned by the server and are stable across a reconnect (the token gives the slot back within the 60 s grace). A player who leaves stays in the registry with Connected false and an empty Input , so NetPlayerInfo still answers for that id; NetPlayerCount and NetPlayerAt list connected players only. After the grace period the record is removed and NetPlayerInfo gives NOT_FOUND . Join and leave are commands applied at a tick of the server. The registry also stores a join tick, a spawn point and a spawned flag; scripts cannot read them ( NetPlayer has only the four fields above). Input NetInput is quantized to integers so it hashes and travels exactly: field unit and range MoveX , MoveY thousandths, -1000..1000 (strafe, forward) Yaw millidegrees, 0..359999 Pitch millidegrees, -90000..90000 Buttons bit field, one bit per game action The game window fills it from the input map every frame: action move gives the axes, action look (mouse delta) accumulates into yaw (0.1 degree per unit) and pitch (clamped to +-89), and every other action, in name order, is a button bit (bit 0 is the first name, at most 32, pressed above 0.5). Rename or add an action and the bits shift; derive them from the sorted action names of input.json . Input is the player's last applied input: a client sends its input and the server applies it at a tick. It stays until the next input replaces it, and is cleared when the player leaves. Edges (pressed this tick) are derived by the script from its own State , as in input . Local input does not exist in a session The command that feeds Action(name) ( script_set_input ) is dropped by the command router on server and clients: in a session read NetPlayerInfo instead of Action . The local player's input reaches the simulation only through the server, so a script behaves the same for the local and for remote players. Rules for script authors A script that follows the determinism rules of the single-player engine is multiplayer-ready; these are the ones that bite: Only the simulation decides. Use Tick() , Rand() / RandN (a per-script stream from seed, entity and tick), NetPlayer* and components. Never use anything that differs per machine: wall-clock time, the machine's locale, os calls, Go map iteration order (iterate sorted keys or slices), goroutines. The sandbox already blocks most of these (see errors and limits ); the rest is your discipline. Iterate players in a fixed order. NetPlayerAt(0..n-1) is ascending by id; keep that order when you spawn, score or tie-break. Never branch on frame-domain facts. Do not use a sound, camera, UI or particle outcome as a condition (you cannot read them anyway), and do not store presentation state in components. UI input comes back only as UIEvents of sim widgets. No hidden state. Guest memory resets before every call; anything that must outlive a tick lives in State , Props or components, which saves and snapshots carry. Only components reach clients. No hot reload. Replacing a script module during a session is refused; modules are pinned by the project hash. Respect command whitelists for clients. A client may submit only net_player_input , set_block , fill_box (4096 voxels), fill_sphere (radius 8) and gameui_event (when the project uses game UI). Script effects are not client commands: they run inside the server's simulation, so budgets and limits ( errors and limits ) apply to the server. Level changes ( LevelLoad ) are served by the server's frame; clients load the same level files (they are part of the project hash). Calling it from several scripts in the same tick is a request race: designate one script. Test with two runs. Run the project headless twice and compare StateHash ( debugging and testing ). Example An avatar per connected player, created on join and moved by that player's input. It runs unchanged on the host and on every client. package main import ( "fmt" "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" ) const speed = 6.0 // blocks per second at full stick func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { n, err := burrowsdk.NetPlayerCount() if err != nil { return // plugin off: nothing to do } for i := 0 ; i < n; i++ { // ascending ids: a fixed order id, err := burrowsdk.NetPlayerAt(i) if err != nil { continue } p, err := burrowsdk.NetPlayerInfo(id) if err != nil { continue } name := fmt.Sprintf( "avatar_%d" , id) avatar, err := burrowsdk.FindByName(name) if err != nil { _, _ = burrowsdk.Spawn( "" , burrowsdk.SpawnOpts{ Name: name, Transform: &burrowsdk.Transform{Pos: [ 3 ] float32 { float32 (id) * 3 , 10 , 0 }, Scale: [ 3 ] float32 { 1 , 1 , 1 }}, }) continue // it exists from the next tick } t, err := burrowsdk.GetTransform(avatar) if err != nil { continue } t.Pos[ 0 ] += float32 (p.Input.MoveX) / 1000 * speed * float32 (dt) t.Pos[ 2 ] -= float32 (p.Input.MoveY) / 1000 * speed * float32 (dt) t.Rot[ 1 ] = float32 (p.Input.Yaw) / 1000 _ = burrowsdk.SetTransform(avatar, t) } }, }) } func main() {} Leaving players keep their avatar here; despawn it when p.Connected is false to clean up. Ready-made base script: the multiplayer template The multiplayer template ( burrow new -t multiplayer ) ships exactly this pattern as an overloadable base script, scripts/avatars/main.go : one avatar per connected player, driven by NetPlayerInfo(id).Input into a physics.character component (walk intents + facing), and in solo (no connected players) the same script falls back to Action() on its own player node. Tweak the props of the script component in scenes/main.voxscn ( speed , sprint_mul , jump_bit , sprint_bit , auto_test — the last one walks forward regardless of input, so movement is verifiable headlessly), or edit and rebuild the script ( burrow script build ). Remember the rule above: in a session Action() is empty by design, so a player script must read NetPlayerInfo , not Action . Lobby functions With runtime.lobby ( lobby ) three more functions exist, all UNAVAILABLE without it: LobbyPhase() (int, error) (0 lobby, 1 countdown, 2 playing, 3 results), ReadLobby() (LobbyInfo, error) (phase, host, match counter, countdown, slots with team and colour, the chosen settings, the last results, the configuration) and LobbyEndMatch(results []byte) error (ends the running match with a JSON verdict of at most 4096 bytes; REJECTED when no match is running). The end takes effect when the script call commits; clients see the new phase through the replicated lobby state. See also Networking : the model, hosting, pins, limits. Lobby : teams, colours, ready, settings, match results. Replication : what clients receive, and component visibility. Determinism : the rules the server relies on. Execution model , input, events, time . Effects : what runs per peer on the screen. Embedding and ABI : net_player_* in the ABI table.

h: Tuning the limits on the host side
x: Errors and limits Every error code a host call can return, every limit with its default and what happens when a script exceeds it, and how faults, rollback and disabling work. Two kinds of failure Error value Fault What A host call refused the request and returned a code The call stopped: trap, panic, gas, memory Script sees *burrowsdk.Error (or ok == false ) and keeps running Nothing: the call ends Effects of the transaction kept all dropped Counted against the script no yes, 3 faults disable it Bad input, missing things and exhausted budgets are error values, never traps. Error values Host calls return a negated code; the SDK turns it into *burrowsdk.Error{Op, Code} . Op is the host function ( voxel_set ), Code is the positive number. Error() reads burrow voxel_set: invalid argument (1) . Code Constant ( abi.Err... ) Meaning Typical causes 1 ErrInvalid bad value NaN or Inf, coordinate beyond +-16,777,216, unknown block id, empty or over-long name, invalid tag or topic, negative slack, bad log level, field path too long 2 ErrMemory pointer or length outside guest memory, or one argument over 64 KiB a value or payload larger than 64 KiB 3 ErrNotFound no such entity, component, block name, action, field, timer, file stale entity id, missing component, unknown block name, missing key 4 ErrTooSmall output buffer too small handled for you: the SDK retries up to 3 times with the size from last_required ; seen only when a result keeps growing 5 ErrBudget a per-transaction or per-tick budget is exhausted too many host calls, voxel edits, spawns, events, asset reads, bytes, or 4,096 buffered operations 6 ErrDenied not allowed for scripts writing or removing script and script.input ; removing transform , scene.name , scene.parent , scene.children ; ReadAsset of a hidden path, .. , an absolute path or a disallowed extension 7 ErrUnavailable the subsystem is not installed, or the call was made outside a tick no physics, physics3d , levels, saves, net or game UI plugin; any world call from init() ; the editor's Play mode for levels and saves 8 ErrRejected schema or JSON validation failed invalid component JSON, a field value the schema refuses, a spawn that clashes with a sibling name, too many tags, a pinned data file that changed 9 ErrLimit a size cap was hit State over 64 KiB, event payload over 1 KiB, 33rd subscription, 65th timer, data file over 256 KiB, 65th data pin ErrRejected carries no reason for the script; test the same JSON in the editor inspector to see the message. Test a code: package main import ( "errors" "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk" "burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk/abi" ) func init() { burrowsdk.Register(burrowsdk.Script{ OnTick: func (self burrowsdk.Entity, dt float64 ) { err := burrowsdk.SetVoxel( 0 , 0 , 0 , burrowsdk.BlockID( 9999 )) var e *burrowsdk.Error switch { case err == nil : case burrowsdk.IsNotFound(err): burrowsdk.Log(burrowsdk.LevelWarn, "not found" ) case errors.As(err, &e) && e.Code == abi.ErrBudget: // out of budget this tick: try again on the next one default : burrowsdk.Logf( "set voxel: %v" , err) } }, }) } func main() {} Functions without an error result swallow failures by design: Exists and Has report false , Action reports ok == false , PropsRaw and StateRaw return empty bytes, Log returns nothing, Rand returns an undefined value from init() . Limits Defaults of script.Config{} . A project raises or lowers them with runtime.script_limits in vox.project (gas per call, guest memory, max_faults , per_script and per_tick budgets: blocks ); burrow run , burrowplay , the editor and burrow test all build their host from it. An embedding program tunes them in Go ( tuning ). Execution Limit Default Scope When exceeded Gas 50,000,000 each guest call ( OnStart , every event, OnTick , OnDestroy ) fault gas exhausted (deterministic instruction budget) at the same instruction on every machine. About 10-20 ms of pure arithmetic on an M2 Max; real scripts with host calls last longer. Module init() gets 4 times as much. Host-call gas per function (base + units, e.g. scene_find_tag 16 + 1 per node scanned, field_set 64 + 1 per 64 bytes, asset_read 200 + 1 per 64 bytes) drawn from the same gas same fault; shown as HostGas in the profile Guest memory 512 pages = 32 MiB per instance growth refused; a Go guest aborts: fault. A Go guest starts near 180 pages because the SDK pre-grows an 8 MiB heap. Wall-clock watchdog off per guest call off by default; when on, a trip disables the script at once and is journaled (not deterministic) MaxFaults 3 per node since its module last changed node disabled Budgets A host call that would exceed a budget returns ErrBudget (5) and counts in Stats.BudgetDenied ; nothing traps. A refused call still counts as a call; its bytes, spawns, edits and events are refunded. One transaction = all hooks of one node in one tick. Budget Per transaction Per tick (all scripts) Host calls 1,000 200,000 Bytes copied between host and guest 1 MiB 64 MiB Spawns 32 1,024 Voxel edits 4,096 262,144 Events ( Emit , Publish , plus bus deliveries) 64 4,096 Every call except tick , entity_self , event_from , last_required , entry_get , props_get , state_get , state_set and abi_version costs one host call, Log , Rand and Voxel included. Once 1,000 are used the rest fail with ErrBudget , even Log . With the default, a transaction can place at most about 1,000 blocks (each SetVoxel is also a call) although the edit budget says 4,096. The per-tick budgets are shared by all scripts in entity order: early nodes can use up what later nodes need. Also per transaction: 4,096 buffered operations ( Set , Remove , SetTransform , Despawn , Emit , Spawn ) before ErrBudget ; 16 ReadAsset reads; 64 data pins; 64 Log lines (the rest are dropped without an error). A bus delivery beyond the per-tick event budget and an event for a full inbox are dropped, with a non-fatal fault in the console, not an error to the sender. Sizes and counts Limit Value When exceeded Module file 8 MiB (a Go module is about 4 MiB) load refused: module is N bytes, limit is 8388608 Loaded module versions 256 (pinned ones never evicted) load refused with a hint to Unpin Module structure block depth 512, 100,000 functions, 3,000,000 instructions in total, 512 KiB per function, 1,048,576 table entries load refused before compilation. The caps are the engine's own gas.Limits checks (run before wazero compiles anything), not wazero limits. A block-depth refusal names the workaround: rebuild with -gcflags=all=-l (inlining off); burrow script build and burrowscript build retry that way automatically State 64 KiB (65,536 bytes) ErrLimit ; old state kept Props 16 KiB (16,384 bytes) component refused when set or loaded One host call argument 64 KiB ErrMemory Component name 128 bytes ErrInvalid Log message 1 KiB, cut cut, no error Event payload 1 KiB ErrLimit Inbox 64 pending events the new event is dropped (non-fatal fault) Bus topic [A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]{1,64} , 32 subscriptions ErrInvalid , ErrLimit Timers 64 per script, id >= 0, delay and period up to 2^30 ticks ErrLimit , ErrInvalid Tags 16 per node, [A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]{1,32} ErrRejected Query results 4,096 entities per call; a search stops after 100,000 nodes scanned truncated flag Field path 256 bytes, 16 segments ErrInvalid World coordinates -16,777,216 to 16,777,216 per axis ErrInvalid ReadAsset 256 KiB per file, extensions .json .txt .csv .tsv .md .toml .yaml .yml .dat ErrLimit , ErrDenied Save data key [A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]{1,128} , value 64 KiB, 1,024 keys, 1 MiB total ErrInvalid , ErrMemory ; total: non-fatal fault at commit PhysicsOverlap buffer 4,096 bodies ErrInvalid Smaller caps (animation, navigation, audio, camera and UI JSON) are listed per function in script/ABI.md and the API reference . What the sandbox forbids Checked when a module loads ( burrow script check shows the reason): Imports other than the vox host module and the WASI preview1 startup stubs ( env , gojs : built with GOOS=js by mistake). The WASI stubs for files and sockets exist but always fail; with StrictWASI they are rejected. _start (a command build; use -buildmode=c-shared ), a missing vox_abi_version (the module does not import the SDK), an ABI version other than 1, no memory export, no on_* export, on_event without vox_alloc . Table or segment mutation ( table.set/grow/fill/copy/init , data.drop , elem.drop ), SIMD, threads, tail calls. A vox.* function or signature this engine does not know (a script built with a newer SDK). Faults In a natively linked game ( burrow build --native , Native scripts ) there is no gas and no memory cap: an infinite loop or runaway allocation is not a fault but a hang. The debug watchdog ( BURROW_NATIVE_DEBUG=1 ) turns a stuck call that still makes host calls into a watchdog fault. Everything else on this page (budgets, transactions, faults, MaxFaults ) is identical. A fault is a trap, a Go panic (including a failed type assertion, a nil dereference, an index out of range), os.Exit , gas exhaustion, running out of memory, or a host-side panic. What happens, in order: The transaction's buffered effects are dropped. Nothing of it reached the world. State, inbox events, due timers and the started flag stay as they were, so the same events and timers arrive again next tick. Log lines written before the fault are still delivered. A script.ScriptFault{Entity, Module, Tick, Reason, Trace, Fatal, Disabled} event is sent; the editor console and the script.Console ring buffer (512 rows) show it; Stats.Faults and the node's faults counter rise. At MaxFaults (3) the node is disabled : it no longer runs. Its other components stay. The node is re-enabled, with its counter cleared, when its module changes: a rebuild whose bytes differ, hot reload in the editor, or restoring a snapshot (Stop in the editor). Rebuilding to identical bytes does nothing. Faults of a node never affect other nodes or the engine. An effect that fails at commit time (a spawn whose name clashes with a sibling, a despawn of an entity already gone, a full inbox) is a non-fatal fault: shown in the console, effects before it stay applied, no counter change, the node keeps running. Failures that are not script faults and stop the whole tick (the engine rolls the tick back and reports an error naming the cause): a node bound to a module hash the runtime does not have (a replay or a restored save without the module bytes); a node bound under a different script.Config fingerprint than the runtime's; a data file read by ReadAsset whose content differs from the recorded one. Reading a fault Editor console line (also ConsoleEntry.Msg and .Trace ): [script /bad tick 3] wasm error: unreachable; guest stderr: hello from println panic: runtime error: index out of range [8] with length 0 goroutine 1 [running]: main.init.0.func1(0x100000001, 0x3fa999999999999a) t1/scripts/idx/main.go:9 +0x6 burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk.dispatchTick(...) (script disabled) in on_tick .$1333(i32) i32 .$697(i32) i32 Part Meaning [script <path> tick <n>] node and tick of the fault gas exhausted (deterministic instruction budget) the loop or the work is too long: profile it , reduce work per tick, spread it over ticks wasm error: unreachable; guest stderr: ... a Go panic or os.Exit : the panic message, goroutine and file:line come from the guest's captured stderr (first 700 characters in the reason, 4,096 captured). Also contains what fmt.Println printed in that call wasm error: out of bounds memory access , integer divide by zero , indirect call type mismatch trap from the module itself host panic: ... an engine bug while serving a call: report it wall-clock watchdog fired only when the host enabled the watchdog event has a payload but the module does not export vox_alloc the module was not built with the SDK (script disabled) this was the third fault in on_tick + $N frames the wasm stack, up to 2,048 bytes. Frames are function indexes ( $1333 ) in a stripped build; function names need a debug build ( burrowscript build -debug ). There are no wasm line numbers because gas instrumentation rewrites the module, but a Go panic prints its own file:line burrow test and burrowplay -headless -json report the count ( script_faults , script_invocations ) and burrow test exits 1 when it is not zero. PauseOnFault ( host side ) is not used by the editor or the game. Tuning the limits on the host side The limits above are fields of script.Config , set when a Go program creates the runtime. The editor, burrowplay and burrow build theirs from the defaults and the project's runtime.script_limits ; to change anything else, embed the engine and pass your own runtime to script.Plugin : rt, err := script.NewRuntime(script.Config{ GasPerInvocation: 200 _000_000, MemoryPages: 1024 , // 64 MiB MaxFaults: 5 , PerScript: script.Budget{Calls: 10 _000, VoxelEdits: 8192 }, PerTick: script.Budget{Calls: 1 _000_000}, }) app.AddPlugins(&script.Plugin{Runtime: rt, PauseOnFault: true }) script.Config field Default Effect GasPerInvocation 50,000,000 gas per guest call MemoryPages 512 64 KiB pages per instance MaxModuleBytes 8 MiB module size MaxModules 256 loaded module versions MaxFaults 3 faults before a node is disabled PerScript , PerTick ( script.Budget : Calls , Bytes , Spawns , VoxelEdits , Events ; zero = default) tables above host-call budgets StrictWASI false reject every WASI import beyond the startup set Watchdog 0 (off) wall-clock limit per call; not deterministic, costs about 10 us per call Limits ( gas.Limits ) see Sizes module structure caps LoadTimeout 120 s validation plus compilation of one module PoolSize 8 idle instances kept per module NoWriteTracking , Interpreter false reset strategy and engine; same results Rules: Gas, memory, budgets, MaxFaults , StrictWASI and MaxModuleBytes are part of the configuration fingerprint stored in each node ( cfg ). A replay or restore under another configuration fails the tick instead of diverging, so record and replay with the same Config . Plugin.PauseOnFault pauses the simulation (reason script.fault ) on a fatal fault; resume with SetPausedBy("script.fault", false) . Raising a limit raises the worst-case cost of every tick; the per-tick budgets exist to keep one script from starving the frame. The standalone checker accepts -max-bytes and -strict-wasi only for the check; they do not change what the game accepts. See also Execution model : transactions and what a fault drops. State and props : size limits in practice. Debugging and testing : logs, profiling, FAQ. script/ABI.md : gas cost model, structural caps, WASI stubs. Embedding and the ABI : script.Config , the plugin, the host side. Script API reference , security .

h: A headless test of a script
x:
Debugging and testing How to see what a script does (logs, faults, profile), how to check it ( burrow script check , burrow test , replay, your own headless test), and the problems people hit most, each with cause and fix. Logging burrowsdk.Log(burrowsdk.LevelWarn, "low ammo" ) burrowsdk.Logf( "tick %d: %d enemies" , burrowsdk.Tick(), n) // LevelInfo Level Constant Shown in the editor console as 0 LevelDebug info 1 LevelInfo ( Logf ) info 2 LevelWarn warning 3 LevelError error A line is cut at 1 KiB, invalid UTF-8 becomes ? , a level outside 0..3 is ignored, and only the first 64 lines of a transaction are kept. Log is a host call: it counts against the call budget and is refused (silently) once the budget is used up ( limits ). Lines are delivered even when the transaction later faults; the effects are not. Log in moderation ( if burrowsdk.Tick()%20 == 0 ): every line costs a host call, and the ring buffer keeps only the last 512 entries. Where the output goes: Host Output Editor Console panel, [script <node path> tick <n>] message , with the level filter. Faults appear as errors with the wasm stack under the message. burrow run , burrowplay , exported game Nowhere. Entries go to the in-memory script.Console ring and nothing prints it. Debug in the editor, or in a headless host that reads the ring (below). burrowplay -headless -json and burrow test only report counts ( script_invocations , script_faults ). Your own Go host The *script.Console resource of the app ( engine.Res ), Entries() oldest first; or the script.ScriptLog and script.ScriptFault events. fmt.Println and println write to stdout/stderr, which the sandbox captures only to enrich a fault message (first 4 KiB); on a successful call the text is discarded. Use Logf . Reading a fault Faults appear in the console with the reason and a stack. The errors page explains each part. In short: a Go panic shows its message and file:line in guest stderr ; gas exhausted means too much work in one call; (script disabled) means three faults. For function names in the wasm stack, build the module with burrowscript build -debug -o assets/scripts/x.wasm scripts/x (bigger file, different hash). To stop on the tick of a fault, run in your own host with script.Plugin{PauseOnFault: true} : the simulation pauses with reason script.fault and the node can be inspected. The editor and the game do not set it. The debugger A script is an all-or-nothing transaction: its call cannot be frozen half way, so the debugger stops the simulation at the end of the tick in which a script asked for it. The stop gives you the script's State and Props , the host functions it called (at most 64, in order), the label and variables it passed, and the world as it is at the tick boundary. Then you continue, or step one tick at a time. The debugger only observes: StateHash , journal and replay are the same with it on or off. In the editor it is on while the scene plays. A stop switches the editor to Pause, writes [debugger] stopped: ... in the console, and Pause resumes, Step runs one tick (the batch of a step ends early at a stop). The MCP tool editor_script_debug does the same from an agent: state , breakpoint_add , breakpoint_remove , breakpoints_clear , resume , step . In your script , a breakpoint written in code: if burrowsdk.Debugging() { // true only with the debugger on; Break alone costs one host call when it is off _ = burrowsdk.Break( "low ammo" , map [ string ] any { "ammo" : st.Ammo, "target" : target}) } _ = burrowsdk.BreakIf(st.Hp < 0 , "negative hp" , st) // a conditional breakpoint From the host , without touching the script: breakpoints match every script run that fits all the fields you set. field stops when module the script's module path contains this text entity the node has this entity id from_tick the tick is at or after this one on_fault the script faults (the stop carries the fault text and the host calls made before it) once (modifier) the breakpoint removes itself after the first stop A breakpoint stops before the call: the snapshot is the State the script is about to receive ( before: true ). A Break call snapshots after the call, with the State it just saved. d := rt.Debug() // *script.Runtime d.SetEnabled( true ) id, _ := d.AddBreakpoint(script.Breakpoint{Module: "enemy" , FromTick: 200 , Once: true }) // the engine App pauses itself (reason "script_debugger") at the end of the tick; read d.Last() / d.Hits(), then: d.Step( 1 ) // run one tick and stop again d.Resume() A game that runs on engine.App pauses the App for you; a host that drives ticks itself (the editor) calls SetManaged(true) and reads TakePending() after each tick. Limits: 64 breakpoints, 32 stops kept, Break variables 4096 bytes, label 256 bytes, one stop per script transaction. Break and Debugging exist in module vox as debug_break and debug_enabled ( ABI ). What it does not do: no stepping through source lines or inspecting local variables of a running call (wasm without debug info and the all-or-nothing transaction rule that keeps scripts deterministic). Put the variables you want to see in Break . Profiling Cost is measured in gas, which is deterministic (the same on every machine and in a replay), plus wall time as a hint. Source What you get Runtime.Profile() One row per script node, most expensive first: Entity , Module , Entry , Ticks (transactions), GasTotal , GasMax , GasLast , HostGas (the part charged by host calls: queries, field access), LastTick , WallNanos , Faults . ResetProfile() clears it. Runtime.Stats() Cumulative counters: Invocations , Faults , GasFaults , HostCalls , BudgetDenied , GasUsed , Spawns , VoxelEdits , Instantiations , Resets , ResetBytes , ModulesLoaded , Evicted . burrowplay -headless -ticks N -json report.script_invocations , report.script_faults . Editor Profiler panel Frame, render, GPU and simulation times; no per-script rows . For a script profile, use a host that calls Profile() (the program below). Reading the numbers: compare GasMax with the 50,000,000 limit; a high HostGas share means queries and field access dominate (see scene queries charges: per node scanned); a GasMax far above GasTotal/Ticks means rare expensive ticks (spread the work). Typical cost: about 1.5 us per call for a trivial script without JSON, much more with encoding/json ( script/ABI.md performance table). Checking a module burrow script check [dir|file.wasm] runs the same loader the game uses, without running any code of the script beyond init() . Failing reasons and fixes: Message contains Cause Fix module is N bytes, limit is 8388608 module over 8 MiB build stripped (the default), drop heavy imports ( net/http , big parsers) exports _start (command build) built without -buildmode=c-shared use burrow script build , or the flags in getting started does not export vox_abi_version the package does not import burrowsdk import it and call burrowsdk.Register forbidden import env... / gojs... built with GOOS=js GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm imports unknown host function vox.X built against a newer SDK than the engine rebuild with the SDK of this engine guest ABI version N, host speaks 1 SDK of another ABI same forbidden import wasi_snapshot_preview1... StrictWASI check drop the package that uses files or sockets initialisation failed init() does heavy work or panics move work into hooks; init() gets 4x the gas malformed or unsupported module truncated file, SIMD, tail calls, table mutation, structure over the caps rebuild; check Go version burrow script build prints the same check after compiling. --json gives entries , size and hash per module. burrow test Headless health check of a project; run it in CI. burrow test # 200 ticks, 3 runs burrow test --ticks 2000 --runs 5 --json burrow test --go-tests # also `go test ./...` in the project (unsandboxed) burrow test --parity # also link the scripts natively and require the same StateHash as wasm --parity links the project's scripts into a headless runner (the same linking as burrow build --native ), runs it for the same ticks, once more with BURROW_NATIVE_DEBUG=1 (faults any script that keeps state in package-level variables), and fails unless the StateHash equals the wasm one. See Native scripts . It (1) loads the project, default scene, world overlay and input map; (2) builds stale scripts and checks every module listed in vox.project scripts ; (3) runs --ticks ticks --runs times (defaults 200 and 3; at most 1,000,000 and 20) under GOMAXPROCS default, 1 and 8, requiring the same StateHash each time; (4) fails on failed commands and any script fault, and replays the journal and compares; (5) with --go-tests runs the project's own Go tests. Output: PASS name ticks=200 StateHash=... (3 runs identical, replay verified) or FAIL and the problems, exit 1. Limits of the check: no device input (scripts reading Action see nothing unless the project queues input), only the default scene, and a scene node whose module ends in .wasm is checked for existence. A different hash between runs means something outside the simulation leaked in: map iteration order, math/rand , time , goroutines, or a float-to-int conversion of NaN ( rules ). Replay and journal A run is a journal of commands; replay re-executes it and must reach the same hash. burrow run -- -headless -ticks 400 -hash -journal run.json # prints tick=400 StateHash=... burrow run -- -replay run.json -expect <hash> # fails unless the hash matches burrow run -- -headless -ticks 400 -hash-every 20 # hash every 20 ticks: diff two machines to find the first bad tick StateHash covers every script component (State, props, hash, inbox, timers), so a script that is not deterministic, or a module that changed, shows up as a different hash. Replay needs the exact modules (they are named by content hash) and the same script.Config ; the engine fails the tick with an error naming the hash otherwise. A headless test of a script Create the runtime, register the module, spawn a node, run ticks, and assert on hash, replay, faults and cost. This program runs assets/scripts/spin.wasm twice and compares: package main import ( "encoding/json" "fmt" "os" "burrow-engine/engine" "burrow-engine/scene" "burrow-engine/script" ) // play runs the module on one node for the given number of ticks. func play(wasm [] byte , ticks int ) (*engine.App, *script.Runtime, error ) { rt, err := script.NewRuntime(script.Config{}) if err != nil { return nil , nil , err } if _, err := rt.Register( "spin" , wasm); err != nil { // scenes may now say "module": "spin" return nil , nil , err } app := engine.New(engine.Options{Seed: 1 , Blocks: engine.DefaultBlocks(), StrictCommands: true }) app.AddPlugin(&engine.ScenePlugin{}) app.AddPlugin(&script.Plugin{Runtime: rt}) if err := app.Build(); err != nil { return nil , nil , err } if err := app.Do(scene.SpawnNode{Name: "cube" }); err != nil { return nil , nil , err } data := json.RawMessage( `{"module":"spin","props":{"speed":90}}` ) if err := app.Do(scene.SetComponent{Path: "cube" , Name: script.CompScript, Data: data}); err != nil { return nil , nil , err } return app, rt, app.RunHeadless(ticks) } func main() { wasm, err := os.ReadFile(os.Args[ 1 ]) if err != nil { fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err) os.Exit( 1 ) } a1, rt, err := play(wasm, 100 ) if err != nil { fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err) os.Exit( 1 ) } defer rt.Close() a2, rt2, err := play(wasm, 100 ) if err != nil { fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err) os.Exit( 1 ) } defer rt2.Close() problems := 0 if a1.StateHash() != a2.StateHash() { fmt.Println( "FAIL: two runs differ" ) problems++ } for _, p := range rt.Profile() { // most expensive script first (read before the replay runs the scripts again) fmt.Printf( "entity %#x: %d ticks, gas total %d max %d (host %d)
" , p.Entity, p.Ticks, p.GasTotal, p.GasMax, p.HostGas) } if st := rt.Stats(); st.Faults > 0 { fmt.Println( "FAIL: script faults:" , st.Faults) for _, e := range engine.Res[*script.Console](a1).Entries() { fmt.Printf( " tick %d fault=%v %s
" , e.Tick, e.Fault, e.Msg) } problems++ } if err := a1.VerifyReplay(); err != nil { // re-executes the journal and compares the hash fmt.Println( "FAIL: replay:" , err) problems++ } fmt.Printf( "tick=%d StateHash=%016x
" , a1.Tick(), a1.StateHash()) if problems > 0 { os.Exit( 1 ) } } Notes: It needs a Burrow checkout ( replace burrow-engine => checkout ); the Windows kit's sdk/ module holds only burrowsdk , so host-side tests are not possible there. Save it as scripttest/main.go in your project and run go run ./scripttest assets/scripts/spin.wasm , or put the body in a _test.go file and let burrow test --go-tests run it. To assert behaviour, read components back after the run: engine.Res and the scene API give you the node (see script/harness_test.go and examples/scripting_demo/main.go for complete examples, including voxel setup with sim.FillBox ). Pure logic of a script (math, parsing, state transitions) can be tested natively with go test : move it into plain functions. On a native build every host call returns ERR_UNAVAILABLE , so code that calls the SDK needs the harness above. Scenarios with input: app.Do(script.ScriptSetInput{Names: []string{"jump"}, X: []int32{1000}, Y: []int32{0}}) makes Action("jump") return 1.0 from the next tick (values in thousandths, names sorted). FAQ Problem Cause Fix My global variable resets every tick Guest memory is restored before every call, even between OnStart and OnTick of one tick Keep it in State or a component ( state ); registrations go in init() My State seems to save the old value defer burrowsdk.SaveState(st) copies st when defer runs defer burrowsdk.SaveState(&st) or save explicitly LoadState returns an error after I rebuilt The struct changed incompatibly (retyped or renamed field), or the codec changed Version the state and migrate ( state ); on error, start from a zero value Props decode is slow Props[T] runs encoding/json in the guest on every call Decode once in OnStart into State, shrink the props, or parse PropsRaw() by hand My voxel edit is not visible Edits apply at commit, not at the call; LightAt and physics queries read the committed world; or SetVoxel returned an error you ignored (bad block id, coordinate range, ErrBudget ) Check the error. Voxel and Raycast do see your own pending edits; other scripts see them after commit Only about 1,000 blocks get placed per tick Each SetVoxel is a host call and the call budget is 1,000 per transaction Spread the work over ticks, or raise PerScript.Calls in your own host ( tuning ) Log stops printing in the middle of a hook The host-call budget is used up; Log is refused when it is Reduce calls; log less Script disabled / "script disabled" in the console Three faults since its module last changed Fix the cause, rebuild (the bytes must change) or press Stop in the editor; see faults gas exhausted More than 50,000,000 instructions in one call: an unbounded loop, a large scan, or JSON on big data Profile, bound the loop, scan once and cache the result in State, spread work over ticks Nothing happens, no error module does not resolve (typo, .wasm not built, GUID of a deleted asset), the script plugin is off ( runtime.plugins.scripts: false ), or no hook does anything The editor shows the module on the component; run burrow script build ; check runtime.plugins ; add a Logf in OnStart Works in the editor but not in the game The game has no hot reload and registers modules at start: the .wasm must exist in the project ( burrow run rebuilds it, a copied folder may not have it). Also: the editor lacks the level and save plugins, but the game needs runtime.plugins.levels / saves for them; in the game window only the controller's keys reach the input map (W A S D, E, Q, Shift, Space, F, Z, F2, Esc, 1-9, mouse buttons per the previous documentation, not re-verified here) Run burrow test and burrow run before shipping; bind scripts to keys the window reports; enable the plugins in vox.project Works in the game but not in the editor Level and save calls return ERR_UNAVAILABLE in Play; input only reaches scripts while the pointer is over the viewport Test those paths with burrow run ; hover the viewport Action returns ok == false The action is not in the input map, no input snapshot exists yet (headless), or the key is not reported Add the action to input.json ; see the headless note above OnStart did not run again after a rebuild started is part of the node's state and survives hot reload Do set-up in a way that tolerates old State, or reset State on a version change An event I emitted arrives one tick late Events and bus messages are delivered on a later tick, never in the emitting tick Plan for the delay; remember the editor does not install levels or saves Two runs give different StateHash Map iteration order, math/rand , time , goroutines, NaN, or floats converted to ints unclamped See the rules ; bisect with -hash-every fmt.Println prints nothing stdout and stderr are discarded on success Logf updates to go.mod needed on the first build the project's go.mod was written by an older burrow with a go line below the SDK's go mod tidy once no required module provides package burrow-engine/sdk/burrowsdk go.mod lacks the require / replace pair or the replace path is wrong See getting started the Go toolchain cannot build GOOS=wasip1 Go older than 1.24 or a build without the wasip1 port Install a current Go from go.dev Replay fails with needs module sha256:...
