Limits Pressure acts through full cells only and moves at most one layer per body per step; a body larger than FinePressure cells only equalises locally. Sources do not take part in pressure. The coarse/fine seam has a tolerance of one level (1/8 block): fine water can rest up to that much above or below a calm coarse neighbour. Folding may move less than one level of water inside a calm connected body (never across a wall, never changing the total). A spill refused by a cap keeps its brick dirty, so a world at FineMaxBricks is not idle until the overload folds have made room (bounded cost, no growth). Scenes that keep moving (springs filling a closed cave, terraces draining into a closed pool) stay at the cap while they move: the water there spreads at the rate the pool and the folds allow. A forced fold turns the front of a sheet into coarse cells for a while: the look changes from the fine surface to the coarse one there until the front is refined again. Streams: the water in the air is not stored in a .voxworld (a load replaces it, ledgered as displaced); a fall deeper than 256 cells lands in mid-air (a new brick, then a new stream below it, starting from rest); the fluid bounds stop at y=512 by default ( Config.Max : a pillar taller than that loses its spring into the void); the water of a stream lands in the column of its lip (no horizontal drift in the simulation: the curtain's bend is drawn, not simulated); a drop of a single cell still spawns the brick below. Rendering: the cascade is drawn after the scene copy, so SSR on the pool does not reflect it; at sunset the aerated curtain takes the sky's lilac ambient and looks a little too bright next to the shadowed cliff. A pool of coarse sources is drawn full but holds the bricks beside it at its constant head (a quarter block at the default level): where the two meet, the source cell slopes down to the bricks over one block. Lateral spreading is diffusive (half the difference per sub-cell pair and step): under a strong spring the water still heaps into a low mound around the impact before it spreads (drawn as one smooth sheet).

Water physics Water flows, pushes and carries. Three layers, each deterministic and cheap when nothing moves: layer package domain what it does flow fluid simulation (20 Hz) cellular automaton on the voxel grid: sources, levels, fall, spread, drain, lava interaction physics , app simulation / frame immersion, Archimedes' push, drag, currents, swimming, climbing out data for rendering voxel , mesh read only surface height of a water cell, smooth corner heights, flow direction Rendering itself (refraction, foam, caustics, underwater fog) is a separate stage and is not part of this page; it reads the data listed in For the renderer . This page describes the coarse automaton (blocks water , water_1..7 ), kept for runtime.plugins.fine_water: false . The fine water (the default of the fluid plugin, fluid.Config.Fine ) replaces it with a conserved volume in sub-cell bricks where water moves: see water-fine.md . Data model: levels are blocks The water of the world is voxels . There is no side table of "water levels": block meaning water source: a full cell, never changes by itself (the worldgen sea is made of sources) water_7 ... water_1 flowing water, height level/8 of the cell (7 = highest) fluid.Install (called by fluid.Plugin ) registers water_1 .. water_7 after the terrain blocks ( voxel.Block.Liquid = level; a block of Fluid kind water without Liquid is level 8; the name never matters: a custom block with "fluid": "water" flows). Ids are appended, so existing ids, worlds and .voxworld files stay valid (a file that lists fewer blocks than the registry loads). Why blocks and not metadata or a sidecar: Overlay and StateHash . Flowing water is written like any edit: it lives in the sparse overlay, in Chunk.Hash , in snapshots, .voxworld , undo and the editor's DocHash , with no new storage and no new serialization. A sidecar would need its own hash, snapshot, undo and world-file story, and could disagree with the voxels. Pure base. The sea stays a field of sources in the base terrain. It never moves by itself; only cells next to an edit (the overlay) are ever evaluated. Digging next to the sea clones the base chunk into the overlay like any edit. Rendering and tools see ordinary blocks: the mesher merges per block id, palettes and the place tool work unchanged. Cost : 8 ids instead of a per-voxel byte. A chunk with water has a palette of at most 9 water entries. The only extra state is the work list ( fluid.State , a sim.Extra named fluid ): the cells that may be unstable plus the wake-ups not merged yet. It is derived from the voxels (a cell that is not in it is stable; TestWorkListIsDerivable rebuilds it by sweeping the overlay and reaches the same settled world), so: it is serialized in Snapshot (a restore taken in the middle of a flow resumes exactly), rolled back with a failed tick, it is not in StateHash : "place a source then undo" leaves the same hash as before, and a world without moving water has the same hash with or without the plugin. Only a non-default fluid.Config and the count of shed cells are hashed. Rules (one automaton step) A step runs every Interval ticks (default 5: water advances 4 cells per second). Each candidate cell is evaluated against the unchanged world (two phases, so order cannot matter), then the changes are applied in canonical order. Solid cells, bounds and sources never change. A free cell is air, flowing water, a fragile block, or lava. Fall. Water directly above makes the cell falling water ( water_7 ). Spread. Otherwise the cell takes the highest spread of its four side neighbours: a source spreads 7, a falling cell 7, a flowing cell of level k spreads k-1 . A flowing or falling cell only spreads sideways when it rests on a solid block (otherwise it falls); a source always does. Range from a source: 7 cells. Infinite sources. A free cell with two side neighbours that are sources, over a solid or source block, becomes a source ( Config.NoInfiniteSources turns this off). Drain. Unfed flowing water becomes air; a puddle recedes one cell per step from its edge. Fragile blocks. voxel.Block.Fragile (non-solid: plants, torches) are replaced by flowing water. No default block is fragile. Other non-solid blocks (a pane, a sign) block the flow like walls. Lava. A block of Fluid kind lava reached by water becomes the block named by Config.CoolSource (default obsidian ), flowing lava CoolFlow ( cobblestone ), water met by lava CoolWater ( stone ); a name that is not a registered solid block means no conversion and lava simply blocks water. Without Config.Lava lava does not flow itself (see "Flowing lava"). Bounds. Config.Min/Max (default x,z +-2^20, y -128..512) delimit the world the automaton may touch. Outside is the void: never written and not solid, so a stream at the edge falls out of the world. Streaming and the void. The simulation world is total (pure base terrain plus overlay): there is no "unloaded chunk" in the sim, and streaming never changes results, so water flows into terrain that is not meshed yet exactly as into meshed terrain. What is bounded is the work (below) and the box (above). Waking: no dedicated command needed A voxel.Observer on the chunk map reports every effective voxel write and every SetChunk . A written voxel wakes 15 cells (the cell and the cells whose result depends on it). So placing or removing a source, breaking a dam, undo , scripts, fill_box and the automaton's own writes all start the flow. fluid_wake {min,max} queues a scan of the chunks of a box (use it for a world saved mid-flow; world loads already queue their chunks). Writes may arrive in any order (a command looping over a Go map): nothing depends on it. Below 8192 queued writes the cells are a multiset consumed sorted; at the first write past it the queue becomes the sorted set of the chunks of all the writes (later writes add their chunk), so the outcome is the union of the chunks whatever the arrival order. A chunk scan covers a chunk that holds water or touches (6 neighbours, base terrain included) a chunk that does. More than 4096 distinct queued chunks start a sweep of the overlay chunks (128 examined per step); the cell wake-ups are kept, and a chunk the cursor has not reached is covered by the sweep itself. SetChunk (world load, agent history) queues a chunk only if it, its predecessor or a neighbour holds water. Cost and denial of service Per step, Config bounds the work: cap default meaning MaxUpdates 2048 cells changed; an ocean breach or a dam failure spreads over many steps MaxActive 262144 unstable cells waiting for MaxUpdates room (3 MiB); beyond it the highest cells are shed and counted ( Dropped , hashed) ChunkScans 2 whole-chunk scans per step (32768 evaluations each) Every step evaluates all candidates (the work list plus 15 cells per queued write, at most 15 x 8192 in a burst; the threshold was 65536 before the fine-water stage, when one burst of scattered writes could cost a 257 ms step, now 30 ms at worst), so stale wake-ups cost time but never a budget and the future depends only on the voxels. Lower cells are served first, so a falling stream is not starved by its sides. Idle cost is a branch (12.9 us per tick including Step overhead). Measured on an M2 Max ( go test ./fluid -bench . -run X , TestOceanCostBounded ): sea of 66k source cells with its east wall removed: 82 steps, 28520 cells changed, at most 1132 per step, work list peak 95k cells (1.1 MiB), 0.12 ms per tick on average, worst tick 12 ms (the first merge of 65k wake-ups); a one-column breach in a 29x5x59 reservoir with MaxUpdates 64: never more than 64 changes per step. Memory growth is bounded by the caps, the 8192-entry wake queue, the 4096-entry chunk queue and the world box. A flood can still create overlay chunks as far as water can legitimately reach (range 7 from a source, unbounded only through infinite sources filling a basin that is open to a source). Determinism contract Same seed, same journal, same config: same StateHash . Everything in fluid is integer arithmetic over sorted slices; no map iteration, no float, no goroutine. Tests ( go test ./fluid ./physics ./editor/core ): two runs, journal replay, snapshot/restore in the middle of a flow (and into the same engine, which re-attaches the observer), rollback of a failed tick, write-order independence, queue overflow, dam break and ocean bounds, 6 fuzz seeds, derivability of the work list, engine.VerifyCacheNeutrality with water and bodies. Interaction (physics) physics.PhysicsPlugin reads liquids from the registry ( voxel.LiquidTable ); a world without liquid blocks pays nothing and physics.Config.Water.Off ignores them. Tuning: physics.WaterConfig . Immersion ( LiquidTable.Sample ): the exact volume of the box under the liquid surfaces it overlaps, a fraction 0..1, plus the volume-weighted current. Query.Immersion(entity) and Query.WaterAt(box) expose it to frame and fixed code. Dynamic bodies : Archimedes' push Density * submergedVolume / mass against the scaled gravity (a body floats when its density Mass / (8 hx hy hz) is below WaterConfig.Density , default 1), and drag toward the current speed ( FlowSpeed * flow direction, default 1.6 m/s). Semi-implicit drag: a floating body settles instead of ringing ( TestBodyFloatsAndSettles : bobbing under 5 mm). Characters ( physics.MoveCharacterWater , used by physics.character ): gravity is reduced by CharBuoyancy (an idle swimmer floats with the head just out), vertical speed is damped, the walking intent is scaled to SwimFactor and pushed by the current. From 30% immersion the character swims: Jump or Move.Y > 0 swims up, Move.Y < 0 dives; jumping from a pool floor is a swim up. With the head out of the water, pushing against a ledge up to one block above the surface climbs onto it. State and API. CharacterController.Submerged (fraction) and HeadUnder are written each tick (hashed only when non-zero, so dry scenes keep their hashes); InWater() and HeadUnderWater() read them. app.Controller (the sandbox walker) has the same model with InWater() / HeadUnderWater() and FrameState.InWater / HeadUnder for the HUD and an underwater view. Input. No new action: the default jump action swims up and the crouch / fly_down key dives ( KeyDown in the sandbox). Scripts. fluid_amount , fluid_pour and fluid_drain (module vox , ABI 1: additive imports) expose the same volume a pump needs: fluid.UnitsPerBlock = 64 units per full cell ( FluidFull in the SDK), a source counts 64, a coarse flowing level 8, and a fine pour adds sub-cell units (rounded down to the script's unit). They return UNAVAILABLE without the automaton and INVALID outside the world or for 0 or more than 64 units. They act at once , like the physics3d calls: the returned amount is exact, a later fault of the same call does not undo the water, and fluid_amount sees the result; the water then flows by the rules above. A fine pour is entered in the Ledger ( Created ) and a fine drain in Displaced , so the conservation invariant still holds. A script also reads names ( water , water_1 .. water_7 ) with voxel_get + block_id_by_name , a character's physics.character component with entity_get_component ( submerged , head_under ), and swims by setting the intent ( move , jump ) like walking. Machine examples (a pump and a tank): blocks . Editor and agents The editor installs the fluid plugin by default ( core.Config.NoFluids removes it). Placing water is the normal place / box tool with block water : one undo step, journaled, replayable; undo removes the source and the flow recedes when the simulation ticks. Edit mode never lets water move : the simulation only ticks in Play (and editor_step , which is refused in edit mode). Stop restores the snapshot taken at Play, flowing water included, bit for bit. editor_water {pos} (read only): block, level (0 none, 1..7 flowing, 8 source), height , falling , flow (unit vector) and the automaton state ( idle , active_cells , pending_wakeups , dropped ). burrowd sessions ( vox_act / vox_step ) have the automaton too: set_block / fill_box with water , then step. fluid_wake is a normal command kind. vox.project runtime.plugins.fluid (default off) controls burrowplay . For the renderer Read-only, pure functions of the voxels and the registry (no state): mesh.NewLiquidTable(reg) -> table (rebuild after registering blocks) mesh.LiquidHeight(t, r, p) float32 surface height inside the cell, 0..1 (1 when water is above) mesh.LiquidCornerHeights(t, r, p) [4]float32 top corners (-x-z, +x-z, +x+z, -x+z), smooth across cells mesh.LiquidFlow(t, r, p) mathx.Vec3 unit push direction (Y < 0 when falling), for ripples and foam Block names water_1 .. water_7 alias the water texture and tint in assets/blocktex ; Vertex.Block of a quad tells the level. The mesher itself is unchanged (a flowing cell still meshes as a full unit cube; sloping its top face is the renderer's job). Limits No pathfinding toward holes (Minecraft spreads toward the nearest drop); no waterlogged blocks; no evaporation by weather or rain inflow (the weather module exposes RainSupply and Phase , nothing consumes them yet); lava flows only with Config.Lava (see "Flowing lava"). Water is a stepped automaton at 4 cells/s: no momentum, no pressure, no waves; levels are 1/8 cell. A flowing cell takes the full cell for collision purposes except its surface height; characters are pushed by the average flow, not per-face. Past the caps the oldest-cell guarantee is lost: shed cells ( Dropped > 0) freeze until a neighbour changes or fluid_wake . The rolling back of a caller-owned voxel undo recording ( BeginUndo outside the engine) restores chunks without telling the automaton; engine commands, the editor and Restore are covered. Compatibility. The plugin appends water_1 .. water_7 to the registry and adds an extra state, so a snapshot saved before it (a burrowctl state.snap , an editor Play snapshot kept on disk) no longer restores into an engine that has it; Restore says so ("a snapshot saved before an optional module such as the water flow ... cannot be restored") and the fix is to save a new one. .voxworld files and journals of the plain world still load (the registry prefix is accepted). A journal in which a character enters water replays to another hash than before this stage (it now swims); dry journals are unchanged. Voxel size (coarse water) The coarse automaton works in units of 1/ Scale level ( fluid.Blocks.Scale = the world's Subdiv at install time): flowing water loses one unit per cell, so it spreads the same 7 m at every voxel size, and the step runs Scale passes (one cell of front each) per Interval , so the front keeps its metres per second. Each level 1..7 (the visual height, Block.Liquid ) has Scale phase blocks: water_L is the full phase, water_L_p (p = 1..Scale-1) the thinner ones, so the blocks of a finer world are the 28/56 flowing blocks of Subdiv 4/8. Scale 1 registers and behaves exactly as before (a world that never leaves one metre voxels never registers a phase block). The fine water has its own section in water-fine.md . The scale follows the voxel size at runtime. Install registers the classic water , water_1..7 ; the phase blocks ( water_L_p , p = 1..7, for every level, one canonical order) are appended after every other block when the world needs a finer scale: by the plugin's late setup stage (a world that starts at 0.25 m), by sim.Engine.ChangeSubdiv through Engine.OnSubdiv (a scene switch: game.SceneSwitch.Apply runs it, so the growth is journaled with the command and a replay reproduces it) and, for a bare Install , at the first tick. Ids are append-only and never renumbered; the phases of a finer scale stay registered after switching back and read as their full level ( water_L ). The registry gets the phases of every scale at once, so it does not depend on the history (an editor that switched 1 m -> 0.25 m, a game that started at 0.25 m and a replay list the same blocks, which a .voxworld palette needs). State.rescale also repairs a snapshot restore or a rolled-back command at the next tick and fluid command. The registry is locked ( sim.Engine.RegistryLock , the mesh workers' lock) while it grows on a live app. Flowing lava ( Config.Lava ) Opt-in: fluid.Config{Lava: true} registers lava (source) and lava_1..lava_3 right after the water blocks (an existing non-solid lava block of Fluid kind lava is reused). With it off nothing is registered and every hash is unchanged; the Config hash gains the lava fields only when on. Not available with Fine (Install refuses it); the lava blocks are not Liquid blocks (no buoyancy, no flow height in meshes, which see a plain non-solid block). Emission and heat are set on the blocks (15 for the source). There is no block damage hook in the engine, so lava does not hurt by itself; scripts read the block name. Speed. Lava rules run every LavaInterval ticks (default 3*Interval = 15: a third of the speed of water). A multiple of Interval . Unstable lava cells wait in the work list between lava steps. Reach. A source spreads 3 cells ( lava_3 , lava_2 , lava_1 ), falling lava is lava_3 and spreads again where it lands. No infinite sources. Unfed flowing lava drains to air. Fragile blocks are replaced. The reach is in voxels (not scaled by Subdiv ). Water onto lava. Source -> Config.CoolSource ; flowing -> Config.CoolFlow ; not a registered solid block: lava blocks the water. Lava onto water (source or flowing, also falling onto it): the water cell becomes Config.CoolWater ; not registered: the water stays and the lava does not enter. The defaults are obsidian, cobblestone and stone ( blockset.DefaultLavaCooling ); the names are hashed with the Config. Integers only; two runs, replays and snapshots give the same StateHash ( lava_test.go ).

Time of day without the weather simulation
x: Weather burrow-engine/weather is a deterministic weather simulation: a seeded state machine of fronts (clear, cloudy, fog, light rain, heavy rain, storm, snow), smoothed intensities, a slowly turning wind, a day clock with an optional seasonal cycle, lightning and thunder, and a per-position sampler ( At ) that turns the front into the weather felt at one place. This page is the simulation foundation and its API; rendering the weather (visible rain and snow, lightning flashes, fog, wet surfaces, wind on clouds and leaves, overcast sky) is the shader stage S3 ( rendering.md ), which reads the weather.State described below through weather.RenderFX . The simulation never depends on the renderer. Enabling it, and why it is off by default weather.Plugin{Options{Enabled: true, Seasons: true}} installs the module; the zero Options installs it inert : nothing evolves, At answers "clear", and the StateHash of the app is bit for bit what it was without the plugin (an inert extra contributes nothing to the hash). That keeps every existing project, golden and journal valid. It is on where a game wants it: where how burrowplay / game projects "runtime": {"weather": true, "seasons": true} in vox.project (the sandbox template sets both) code app.AddPlugin(&weather.Plugin{Options: weather.Options{Enabled: true}}) after ScenePlugin editor, burrowd sessions always installed, disabled; turn it on with editor_weather {enabled:true} , the View > Weather panel, or vox_act weather_set a bare sim.Engine weather.Install(e, seed, opts) from sim.Config.Setup A journal recorded with weather enabled replays only on an engine that installs the module (the editor, burrowd and the app plugin all do). Model All evolving state is integer (Q16 fixed point, permille, splitmix64 of (world seed, counter, salt) ); there is no wall clock, no math/rand , no floating point in the state, so every platform reaches the same hash. Floats exist only in the frame-domain State / Local values. Fronts. A front ( Kind ) lasts a drawn number of ticks (20 ticks = 1 s): clear 5 to 20 min, cloudy 4 to 14 min, fog 2 to 6 min, light rain 3 to 10 min, heavy rain 2 to 7 min, storm 1.5 to 5 min, snow 3 to 10 min. The next front is drawn from a transition table (clear -> cloudy -> rain -> clearing; storms end in heavy rain; fog burns off), adjusted by the mean temperature (no snow above 2 C, snow x4 below 0 C, no storm below 4 C) and the hour (morning fog x3). Each front draws its targets: precipitation, cloud cover, fog, humidity. Smoothing. The current values move toward the targets by a bounded step per tick (precipitation 0 to 1 over 60 s, cover 45 s, fog 75 s), so a change of front never jumps. Surface wetness rises under rain and dries over about 9 minutes. Wind. Every 30 s a new target heading (at most 45 degrees from the previous) and speed (3 to 17 m/s plus a boost from the front) is drawn; the heading slews at 2.7 deg/s, the speed slowly. Heading is where the wind blows toward, radians in the XZ plane (0 = +X, pi/2 = +Z). Lightning and thunder. In a storm with precipitation >= 0.5 a strike occurs with probability proportional to the precipitation (about one every 6 s at full intensity), at a drawn bearing and distance (80 to 2480 blocks) from the listener. Thunder arrives distance / 343 m/s later (up to 4 pending). Both are state ( StrikeSeq , ThunderSeq ), and the plugin turns new ones into LightningEvent / ThunderEvent . Time and seasons. Clock is the day clock in ticks, starting at 6000 (sunrise, the renderer's existing sky offset): scene.NewSky(State.Clock) is the matching sky. A day is 24000 ticks (20 min). With Seasons the temperature follows a 12 day year (288000 ticks) of +-9 C. Temperature. 10 C mean + seasonal + diurnal (+-4 C, warmest at 14:24) + climate noise ( worldgen.ClimateAt , +-8 C) - 0.15 C per block above RefY (20) - cover and precipitation cooling (up to 3 C). Integer milli-degrees; rain falls as snow where Temp <= SnowC (0 C) , so one front can be snow on a mountain and rain in the valley. There is no biome system yet, so the climate noise stands for biomes; a sand-storm front is not modelled (no desert biome exists). API st := weather.Res(ctx) // *weather.State, refreshed each frame (Update stage); also valid from Startup l := st.At(pos) // weather.Local at a world position (no allocation) ex := weather.ExposureAt(st, blocks, reg, blockPos) // sheltered? under rain/snow? wet? st.SkyLightFactor(); st.SkyLightLevel( 15 ) // cloud/precipitation dimming for a sky-light level weather.State (frame domain, plain copyable values): Enabled , Frozen , TimeFrozen , Kind , Intensity (precipitation 0..1), Cover , Fog , Humidity , Wetness , Wind{Dir, Speed, Vec, Gust} , Temp , Clock , DayTime (0..1), Day , Season , TicksLeft , Strike and Thunder ( {Seq, Tick, Bearing, Dist} ), Overcast , and FlashAt(tick) (lightning illumination envelope 0..1). weather.Local (from At ): Kind (snow only where it is cold enough), Phase (none/rain/snow), Intensity , Temp , Humidity , Cover , Fog , Wetness , Wind , Lightning (a storm in the rain phase), RainSupply , SnowSupply , Extinguish . ExposureAt scans the voxel column above the point (up to MaxSkyScan = 96 blocks) for a Solid or Opaque block: Sheltered , CeilingY , UnderRain , UnderSnow , Wet (open sky under rain >= 0.15), Wetness . It is deterministic and does not allocate. Gameplay hooks (the sim does not edit voxels) The repository has no fire and no sky-light level yet, so those are hooks, not behaviour: Local.Extinguish (rain strong enough to put a fire out) and State.SkyLightFactor() (0.3..1) are what a fire system or a sky-light consumer should read, from FixedUpdate through weather.Of(sim).At(pos) (journal-safe: it reads state only). Local.RainSupply / SnowSupply (0..1) are the rain inflow hook for the water simulation (W1) : the water layer reads them per column; weather itself never places water, snow cover or ice. Snow accumulation and ice on water are out of scope here and are extensions tied to the water/physics layer. Commands, editor and agents One journaled command, weather_set ( weather.Set ), with optional fields: enabled , type ( clear|cloudy|fog|light_rain|heavy_rain|storm|snow ), intensity 0..1 (precipitation for rain/storm/snow, fog density for fog, cloud cover for clear/cloudy), cover , wind_dir (degrees), wind_speed (m/s, holds the wind until wind_auto ), time (day fraction), freeze (stop the front), freeze_time (stop the clock), seasons , instant (skip the smoothing), plan (the weather plan, below) and day_length (seconds per day, 60 and up). Anything but enabled needs the weather enabled. Validation happens before any change; a failed command leaves no trace. weather_restore replaces the whole state (the inverse used by undo). Editor : Tools > Environment is a full-screen tool: the world with a wind compass (drag the dial to turn the wind), the Day strip (a 24 h band coloured by the sky, a sun marker you drag to set the time of day, and the plan lane), and Environment settings on the right (weather cards, intensity, wind, plan segments, time, start time, day length, freeze). The header switch (Frozen, Live x1, x60, x600) previews the time of day and the plan running in the editor at that speed: it is not saved, makes no undo step and no dirty flag, and leaving the tool, editing, or pressing Play puts the edited time and weather back (the preview is not journaled; strike flashes do not animate in it). Freeze time stays a separate setting that Play and the game obey. One change or one slider drag is one undo step; it is journaled, replayed by editor_verify_replay and restored exactly by Stop. The weather is a runtime setting of the world: saving a scene does not store it, except the plan and the day length, which go to environment.json . The weather plan Params.Plan is a schedule of segments over the day: {"from":250,"to":380,"type":"light_rain","intensity":600} ( from and to are permille of the day, 0..1000, sorted and not overlapping; type is a kind name; intensity is permille, as the intensity of weather_set ). While the day clock is inside a segment the front is that segment's kind (the random fronts are held, Sim.PlanSeg says which segment runs); between segments the weather changes by itself as before. Entering a segment starts its front with the smoothing of any other change. At most 24 segments. Set it with weather_set {"plan":[...]} (an empty list clears it). The editor writes the plan and day_length to environment.json at the root of the project and reads them back when the project opens; a game that installs weather.Plugin sets Options.Params.Plan itself. environment.json and the game environment.json is {"enabled":true,"plan":[...],"day_length":1200,"start_time":0.25} ( weather.Env ). start_time is the time of day the game and the editor's Simulate (Play) start at, a day fraction (0 midnight, 0.25 sunrise, 0.5 noon); it is Params.ClockStart , set with weather_set {"start_time":0.5} (changing only day_length keeps the start fraction). A standalone game ( burrowplay , the editor's Play window) that finds the file loads it into the weather.Plugin options ( Env.Apply ): the weather is on unless enabled is false (older files without the field mean on), the plan runs, and the sky, time and rain use the same render.WeatherFX as the editor. Without the file the game behaves as before ( runtime.weather ). MCP : editor_weather (same fields; no arguments reads; at:[x,y,z] also samples the local weather). burrowd / burrowctl : vox_act with {"kind":"weather_set","data":{...}} . Determinism contract The plan ( Params.Plan , Sim.PlanSeg ) is part of the hashed state, so enabling the weather gives a different StateHash than before the plan existed (the 100k-tick golden changed once). StateHash includes the weather (type, counters, targets, smoothed values, wind, strikes, clock, parameters, seed) when it is enabled, in the engine extra "weather" ; it is rolled back with a failed tick, snapshotted and restored, and replayed from the journal. Tests: 100k tick golden hash, no per-tick jump, transition statistics, snow only below the threshold, journal replay, snapshot/restore, undo, zero allocation per tick ( weather/*_test.go , editor/core/weather_test.go ). A snapshot taken before the module was installed does not restore into an engine that has it (the extra count differs); this only affects snapshots saved by an older build. Time of day without the weather simulation An env.time node with frozen: true (a day fraction, 0 midnight, 0.25 sunrise, 0.5 noon, 0.75 sunset) freezes the sky and sun of the running scene without runtime.weather : the renderer builds scene.NewSky(time * 24000) from the frame-domain engine.SceneRuntime , the weather module stays inert, the clock does not advance and the StateHash is bit for bit the same as without the setting ( internal/game test TestSceneSettingsApplyAndKeepStateHash ). It overrides the weather clock while the scene runs. See lighting.md . Environment components and the weather env.time and env.weather ( lighting.md ) are the declarative way to set the clock and the front. Both are hashed (simulation state): the running game resolves them each frame and hands the clock and the front to this module as journaled weather_set commands ( weather.SetFromEnv ), once per change, so they replay and enter the StateHash like any weather command. env.time sets the day clock ( start , day_length , frozen ), env.weather holds a front ( kind , intensity , wind, frozen ) and works with the weather module enabled or not. env.sky.clouds , env.fog and env.sun are renderer-only and never reach the module: a thick env.fog volume thickens the aerial perspective on top of the weather fog ( WeatherFX.Fog takes the larger), env.sky.clouds on / off replaces the cloud cover the weather asks for. The editor viewport shows env.time as the sky time; it does not run the weather from it. What the shader stage (S3) consumes The plugin's weather.render system (PostUpdate) reads weather.Res(ctx) once per frame, samples st.At(camera position) and writes the frame resource *render.WeatherFX ( weather.RenderFX(st, cam, tick) ); RenderPlugin hands it to the Vulkan renderer, and the editor viewport computes it for the editor camera. All levels low .. ultra draw it; -shaders off ignores it. effect inputs sky time State.Clock -> scene.NewSky(Clock) when Enabled (otherwise keep the existing sky tick) cloud cover / overcast State.Cover (target for -clouds auto ; the CLI -clouds keeps priority), State.Overcast , Local.Cover rain / snow particles Local.Phase , Local.Intensity , Wind.Vec (slant), temperature for flake vs drop; draw only where the column is open ( ExposureAt or a height map) fog / mist Local.Fog , Local.Humidity , State.Kind == KindFog wet surfaces State.Wetness / Local.Wetness (darker albedo, higher specular on opaque, non-sheltered pixels) lightning State.FlashAt(tick) (global fill light + sky), State.Strike{Seq,Bearing,Dist} for the bolt, LightningEvent / ThunderEvent for audio wind on clouds and foliage Wind.Vec , Wind.Speed , Wind.Gust (0..1), Wind.Dir precipitation size render.WeatherFX.Unit (voxels per metre, weather.RenderFXUnit ): drop length and width, fall speeds, wind drift and the spawn box are in metres; the precipitation height map spans 64 m at every voxel size ( engine.PrecipGrid : 64 x 64 texels of 1 voxel at 1 voxel per metre, up to 256 x 256 texels of several voxels, a texel being roofed by any of its columns) ambient dimming SkyLightFactor() on the sun term (the CPU twin scene.Sky.Atmo(cover) already takes a cover) Limits and extensions No biome system: the climate is worldgen.ClimateAt (render-tint noise) plus altitude. A biome table would replace Sim.at 's two inputs. No sand storm (no desert biome), no snow cover, no ice on water, no fire, no per-entity wetness component; the hooks above are in place. Lightning is global (bearing and distance from the listener), not tied to a world column; a bolt that ignites or electrifies a block is a gameplay layer on top of StrikeSeq . Rendering (S3): snow does not accumulate, the bolt is a sky effect (no ground strike), BURROW_LIGHTNING=<deg> forces a bolt for captures.

h: Defender reports a threat (names ending in !ml )
x: Windows security warnings Burrow programs are not code-signed yet. A new, unsigned program has no reputation with Windows, so two things can happen. "Windows protected your PC" (SmartScreen) Click More info , then Run anyway . This message appears for any program without a known publisher and goes away as a signed program gains reputation. Defender reports a threat (names ending in !ml ) Microsoft Defender uses a machine-learning heuristic on new files. The Hub downloads archives, unpacks them, starts programs and replaces itself when it updates, which is also what some malware does, so a young unsigned build can be flagged by mistake. What the Hub does and does not do: It contacts the network only after you agree to check for updates. Every download is described by a manifest signed with an Ed25519 key (the public key is published with each release). The signature and the SHA-256 of each archive are checked before anything is unpacked. It does not install a service, a scheduled task or an autorun entry, and it never asks for administrator rights. It sends no telemetry. If Defender flags a file: Compare the file's SHA-256 with the one on the download page ( certutil -hashfile <file> SHA256 ). If they match, open Windows Security, Protection history , select the item and choose Restore (or Allow on device ). You can also report it to Microsoft as a false positive at the Security Intelligence submission page so the detection is reviewed. If the sums do not match, delete the file and download it again from the official site.

World generation Two terrain generators (and a blank one) ship with Burrow. Both are pure functions of (seed, position) : a chunk never depends on which other chunks were generated, in what order, or on which goroutine. generator runtime.generator.kind what it is v1 omitted or "heightmap" the original hills with trees ( worldgen.Heightmap ). Frozen: worlds, scenarios, goldens and StateHash never change. Also "flat" . empty "empty" all air ( worldgen.Empty ): a blank world to build or script from scratch. No terrain, no trees; the other generators are untouched. v2 "biomes" biomes, rivers, lakes, mountains, caves, ores and vegetation ( worldgen.Biomes ), 4 chunk layers high (y 0..127). A project, .voxworld or scenario without a generator field stays on v1 forever. New projects from the sandbox template, the editor's World settings dialog ("biomes (v2)") and the biomes session generator of burrowd / burrowctl use v2. The sandbox example takes -gen v2 (default v1 ). Settings vox.project -> runtime.generator : { "kind" : "biomes" , "sea_level" : 36 , "scale" : 1 , "amp" : 100 , "caves" : true , "trees" : true } sea_level is the top water voxel (0 = 36, 8..90), scale the horizontal feature-size factor (0 = 1, 0.25..4), amp the vertical relief in percent (0 = 100, 20..150), caves and trees (trees and ground plants) switch the features. The seed is runtime.seed (or the World settings dialog). Block ids: the default blocks first, then the biome blocks ( worldgen.BiomeBlockNames() ), registered by the engine when the generator is installed; the same ids result in every engine, editor and agent session. How v2 builds a column Everything below is a function of (seed, x, z) ; heights are continuous values rounded with a small position-hashed dither, so level lines are stippled rather than straight stair lines. Domain warp , horizontal axes only (no 3D warp, so cliffs stay clean): x and z are displaced by two low-frequency fBm fields. Climate fields : continentalness (huge oceans, continents of varied size), erosion (picks the relief class: mountains, hills, plains, flat swampy lowlands), temperature in latitude-like bands along z bent by noise and lowered with altitude (a lapse rate), humidity. The area around the origin is biased to land and a temperate climate so a new world starts on grass. Height : a spline of continentalness (abyssal plain, shelf, a short coastal rise so beaches are a few blocks wide, rolling inland), plus ridged-noise mountains weighted by erosion and distance from the coast, plus rare cliff steps, plus detail noise whose amplitude depends on the relief class. Rivers : level lines of "position along a seed-chosen axis + wandering noise", repeated every 560 blocks. Because the noise displacement stays below the axis gradient, every river is an open curve that crosses the land and meets the sea (tested over three 3600x3600 windows). Valleys are deep and wide in mountains, the channel is flat, and the river level follows half the height above sea level, so rivers step down to the sea. Mountain gorges are dry (water would run down a slope as a wall). Lakes : one candidate per 192-block cell, accepted only on flat land away from rivers, a bowl with a flat water level and an embankment. Cell results are cached; a column evaluates the 1-4 cells within reach. Biomes : ocean, deep ocean, beach, plains, flower meadow, forest, birch woods, taiga, tundra, desert, savanna, jungle, swamp, mountains, snow peaks, river, lake ( worldgen.BiomeList() ). Water columns are rivers, lakes or ocean; land by altitude and slope, then by temperature and humidity with patch noise for forests and meadows. Transitions follow the fields, there are no biome borders on a grid. Surface rules per biome (grass over dirt, sand over sandstone, mud in swamps, gravel/clay/sand sea and river beds, snow where it is cold). Slope exposes stone: steep faces are rock in every biome and medium slopes mix rock with the surface material by hash. Snow only where the local temperature is below 0.2 (or on snow peaks), ice only below 0.15. Caves : two 3D noise fields sampled on a 4-voxel lattice and interpolated trilinearly (tunnels where both are near zero) plus larger caverns; at least 6 blocks of rock stay under the surface (9 under water) except at rare designated entrance columns (no plant or tree grows there). Bedrock at y 0..2, deepslate below y 14. Ores (coal, iron, copper, gold, lapis, redstone, diamond, emerald): one candidate blob per 16-voxel cell and kind, positioned by a hash of the cell. Vegetation : per-column plants (tall grass, flowers, mushrooms, cactus, dead bush) and trees from a 4-block candidate grid with a dart-throwing priority rule (blue noise), thinned by the biome density and by clearing noise. Species: oak, large oak, birch, spruce, acacia, jungle, swamp oak, bushes. A chunk evaluates every candidate whose crown can reach it, so trees that straddle chunks are identical on both sides. Plants are Solid , non-opaque cubes (the mesher draws every non-solid, non-opaque block as a liquid); tall_grass , jungle_leaves and acacia_leaves reuse the oak leaves texture with a biome tint, cactus, flowers, mud and the acacia/jungle logs are flat colours, everything else (sandstone, gravel, snow, ice, clay, deepslate, bedrock, ores, birch, spruce) uses its pack texture. Water is the one existing water block (a source block); v2 places it in oceans, lakes and rivers and freezes the top layer in the cold. Biome tint Biomes.TintAt(seed, kind, x, z) returns the grass (1), foliage (2) or water (3) tint multiplier: the biome colour of the column averaged over a 5x5 lattice of samples (4-block step, about 20 blocks wide) and bilinearly interpolated, so colours fade between biomes. The engine uses it automatically for v2 worlds ( engine.SetBiomeGen ; the editor updates it when the world is regenerated); v1 keeps ClimateAt . blocktex itself is unchanged. API b := worldgen.DefaultBiomes() // v2, default parameters, palette for a default registry b.BiomeAt(seed, x, z) // Biome (also worldgen.BiomeAt(seed, x, z) for the defaults) b.Height(seed, x, z) // top solid y b.ClimateOf(seed, x, z) // local temperature, humidity (0..1) b.BiomeGrid(seed, x0, z0, w, h, step) // minimap data worldgen.BiomeList() // id, name, map colour, grass/foliage/water tint ClimateAt (used by weather/ and the v1 tint) is unchanged and stays a v1-style climate: weather in a v2 world therefore does not follow the biome temperature (a snowy biome can get rain). Making weather read Biomes.ClimateOf is a possible follow-up. Editor and agents: editor_biomes (generator kind and version, seed, biome list) and editor_biome_at {x,z} (biome, height, temperature, humidity of one column, the data a minimap needs); the seed and generator are set in View > World settings (undoable) or runtime.generator in vox.project . Distance LOD sampling Biomes implements worldgen.ColumnSource : the engine draws LOD 2 and LOD 3 columns from ColumnSampler(seed) (ground, water level and the surface rule of each column, the slope taken from the four neighbouring columns) instead of generating chunks. Caves, ores, ice and vegetation are not sampled; Generate is unchanged. Cost and memory Measured on an Apple M2-class laptop: about 1.0 ms per 32x32x32 chunk generated cold (including the column window that the four layers of a column share), about 0.3 ms per chunk with 4 workers for a radius-12 disc (2500 chunks in 0.7 s). Memory is bounded: 96 column windows (about 20 KiB each), at most 4096 lake cells, the tint caches are cleared at 131072 / 262144 entries, at most 6 samplers live at once. None of these caches is state: dropping them never changes a result. Testing go test ./worldgen covers determinism, order and cache independence, biome distribution over four seeds, per-voxel rules (no plant in water, no floating plant or log, snow only in the cold, bedrock, caves, ores, no holes in the surface), tint smoothness, palette stability and a fuzz target. Behind the slow tag: rivers reach the sea (or the window border, or a dry mountain gorge) over three seeds, the same rules on wide regions, and a radius-12 generation. Inspiration and licence Larion's published ideas (latitudinal temperature bands, an erosion parameter choosing the relief class, horizontal-only warp, long valleys, exposed stone on slopes) inspired the design; nothing was copied: all code, names, tables and values are original, so no third-party notice is needed. No other mod or generator was consulted. Voxel size A world can have voxels smaller than one metre: runtime.generator.voxel_size (or the scene's world file, set from World settings > Voxel size in the editor) is 1 (default), 0.5, 0.25 or 0.125 metres. The voxel grid stays integer and the simulation (chunks, raycasts, block edits, node transforms) stays in voxels; everything authored in real units is metres and converts through the size: The generator parameters ( base , amp , scale , sea_level , surface_y , depth , trees) are metres: a 0.25 m world is the same landscape at 4 times the detail. heightmap samples its noise at the finer grid (smooth terrain, trees keep their size in metres); flat , biomes and empty are upsampled voxel for voxel. The player (1.8 m tall, 1.62 m eye, 0.6 m wide), player.move speeds, jump height, step height, player.build / player.interact reach, gravity, physics.character , physics and physics3d gravity, particle sizes, speeds and gravity, and audio min/max distances are in metres and seconds. The load radius grows with the finer voxels (same distance in metres, capped at 24 chunk columns). A scene switch into a world of another voxel size carries the size; it is part of the world identity and of the state hash (absent at 1 m, so those worlds hash as before). Still per voxel: block light falloff (15 levels, one per voxel, so a torch lights a smaller radius in metres), fluid flow distance, nav agent profile sizes, camera rig offsets, fog and weather sizes, and block textures (one texture per voxel face). The editor refuses to change the voxel size of a world while keeping its edits (regenerate without keeping edits, or make a new scene).

0.8.3 - 2026-11-06 Fixed: two buttons bound to the mouse wheel, one per direction ( scroll with scale 1 and scale -1), were both pressed by any notch: a button takes an analog input by its length, which ignored the sign, so a game that changes slot with hotbar_prev / hotbar_next saw one step forward and one back and nothing moved. A wheel binding now presses a button only in the direction of its scale. Test TestScrollButtonsArePerDirection . Added: a game customizes its loading screen and a network client's wait: gogame.Game.Loading ( LoadingScreen : Title , Paint(cv, w, h, t, title, stage) draws the whole screen, Ready() ), engine.LoadingScreenPlugin.Hold/Stage/Paint and game.Window.OnLoading . For a client ( gogame.Connect/Join ) the screen stays up until the connection is complete ( netplay.Guest.Ready : the server accepted it, its player exists, the terrain under it arrived) and the game says it is ready ( LoadingScreen.Ready : its first data from the server): nothing of the world shows before. Stages given to Paint : world , connect , terrain , arrival . The simulation is not paused while a Hold keeps the screen up. Fixed: Enter in a text field only sent its event; it now also runs the ui: parts of its action like a button ( sim:chat:say;ui:set:chat_text=;ui:hide:chat_input sends, clears and closes). Test TestInputSubmitRunsItsUIActions . Added: the server streams the terrain, as Minecraft does ( replica.ServerConfig.StreamBase , always on for netplay.StartHost ): every non-empty chunk of the base terrain in a client's view is sent whole (version 0, compressed once and shared: basestream.go ), not only the chunks the game edited; the first edit of such a chunk is a delta from the terrain (the client holds it: chunkEnt.baseDelta , the whole chunk only past MaxDeltaEdits ) and starts the delta references; terrain chunks are deflated at BestCompression (once, shared: 10% under BestSpeed on biome terrain; a shared dictionary added only 4% more and a protocol change, so none), and a client's frame generates at most 8 new terrain chunks ( maxGenPerFrame ), so a joining player does not stall the server's ticks. A client ( netplay.Join ) removes its base terrain ( ChunkMap.SetBase(0, 0, nil) ): it generates nothing, needs no seed and no generator of the game, and the pin net.stream_base makes a client of another kind refuse; the world seed is no longer a pin. The client's prediction waits for the chunk under the player ( Client.HoldsChunk , 3 s at most) instead of walking through the void. Cost: the terrain in view crosses the network once per client (a few hundred KiB to a few MiB, at the 256 KiB/s budget). Tests TestStreamBaseSendsTheTerrain . Added: gogame.Ctx.BlockBoxes(x, y, z) : the boxes that make the shape of the block at a cell, {minX, minY, minZ, maxX, maxY, maxZ} in blocks from the cell's corner (the selection boxes a ray tests, resolved for that cell: stairs with their corner shape, a slab low or high, a torch, a fence with its connections); nil for air and for a full cube. A game that draws something around or over a block (the mining cracks, an outline) follows the model with it instead of the whole cell. Test TestBlockBoxesFollowTheShape . Fixed: on a network client, typing in a text field of the game UI also played the game: the input sent to the server carried the walking and the buttons of the keys pressed (typing "wood" in a command box walked the avatar and pressed the game's keys). While a text field has the focus ( UI.FocusedIsInput ), internal/netplay.InputFromState sends no walking and no buttons, only the look. Test TestTypingSendsNoGameInput . Fixed: gameui grids and lists, found with the project's inventory: (1) a click that moved a few pixels between the press and the release became a drag, and released over its own cell the click was lost; at 4K a hand moves 6 pixels easily. The drag threshold now grows with the interface scale, and a release over the cell the press started on, without the pointer ever having left it, is a click (a drag that left the cell and came back still cancels); (2) an item picked up by a first click now follows the cursor like a dragged one until the next click puts it down ( UI.carried ); (3) Widget.ScrollOffset() exposes the offset a list uses to find the row under a click, for a painter that draws the list itself: the project's skin counted the wheel on its own and never saw it (a modal screen zeroes the app input before the skin reads it), so the engine scrolled the list while the skin drew the top rows, and clicks landed on rows other than the ones shown. Tests TestClickWithJitterIsStillAClick , TestDragStillMovesAndCancels , TestListScrollOffsetIsExposed , TestClickPickedItemFollowsTheCursor . Fixed: in a network session the window and the server never agreed on where the player was (measured up to 1.6 blocks), so the server aimed, broke and picked up from a place the player did not see, and any correction felt like a rollback. The client and the server stepped the player with two different models (the first person controller at frame rate, with its own physics and creature collisions; the server one step per input received, about 15 a second), and the controller kept its prediction forever. Now, as in client-side prediction with server reconciliation (Gambetta; Overwatch's command frames): the server applies every movement input once, in order, one per tick (a backlog two per tick; net/replica.Server.runTick , test TestServerAppliesEachInputOnceInOrder ); the walk model is one exported function, netsim.Walk ( netsim.WalkState ), that the server's moveNode and the client both call; a client with a first person controller builds one input per tick of real time, predicts it with netsim.Walk , keeps it until acknowledged and draws the prediction interpolated between its last two ticks ( app.Controller.SetPrediction / SetPredicted : the controller runs no physics of its own then); each server frame compares the node's position for the acknowledged input ( FrameInfo.InputAck , replica.Client.InputSeq ) with the prediction, and on a difference (a knockback, a push, water, a teleport) restarts from the server's position and replays the inputs in flight, the on-screen jump fading over a few frames ( internal/netplay predict.go). Asset thumbnails are sharper and resizable. The script panel is now a code editor with tabs, find and replace, autocomplete, format, folding and a minimap. It has syntax colours for eight languages and live errors for Go and JSON. Open in VS Code hands a file off to your own editor. Ctrl+E opens Go to File, and Ctrl+Shift+F searches the project with replace all. Console lines are clickable, and a History panel jumps to any undo step. A welcome window greets new sessions. The character panel has a turntable and opens the skin in the texture editor. The animation timeline gained keyboard transport keys. The inspector can filter properties, and the code editor can detach into its own window. Fixed voxel edits lost when a project was closed and reopened. Save now also writes world.voxworld , and opening a project loads it back. 0.3.2 - 2026-10-31 Fine water fix: a stream running over a river bank no longer draws broken sheets. Water Fixed: fine water spilling down a slope of 1-block steps drew loose rectangles flashing in the air. Fine water on such a slope now draws one sheet down each step. 0.3.1 - 2026-10-31 Fine water by default, a game inventory, water particles and determinism fixes. Game Inventory in the running game. Blocks placed on the ground follow the ground. Water particles, plus renderer and chunk stream tweaks. Water burrow migrate turns the fine water on for projects that never chose, when the Hub upgrades the engine. Every burrow new template starts with the fine water. The StateHash of projects with water changes, and a coarse-water save is refused with an error. The Hub's backup and Revert go back after the upgrade. Determinism physics3d rounds every float product explicitly, so results are identical on arm64 and amd64. Fixed an evaporation snapshot that could stall a brick until the clock caught up with it. 0.3.0 - 2026-10-31 Buoyancy and swell for physics bodies, variable voxel size, a creative mode in the editor, a building guide for agents and multiplayer fixes. Editor Creative mode (F9): captured mouse, fullscreen viewport, hotbar, inventory, flying and walking. The finite full-water block is hidden from the creative inventory. Picking, selection and framing bounds of a voxel model follow the model size and its scale . Multiplayer Fixed kicks for a too high input rate, a deadlock on submit, ghost joins, chat, message ordering and missing startup files. Agents New package buildguide distils the public Minecraft building guides into building rules. It has 16 styles with block palettes, roof recipes, proportions and furniture recipes. Every block a palette names is checked against the block set. New tools editor_build_guide , editor_build_plan and editor_build_review , with vox_* twins on burrowd. The plan generates roofs, solids and whole houses from a style in one call. The review scores a finished structure and lists fixes. editor_blocks gained query, category, material and family filters over the full block list (about 1500 entries). Rendering Variable voxel size: render.voxmodel keeps its per-instance scale , with one source for the default. Fixed: dynamic voxel bodies drawn by p3render were invisible on the GPU. Physics Variable voxel size for physics3d bodies ( RigidBody.cell ): mass, inertia, collision, buoyancy and rendering follow the cell size. Buoyancy is computed from displaced-volume samples instead of one immersion fraction. Floating bodies now right themselves, trim by their load and can capsize. A sealed hollow hull floats. Open hulls displace water and flood when the rim goes under, so an overloaded boat sinks. Optional swell ( Water.Swell ): three deterministic travelling waves, shared by buoyancy and the rendered water surface. A body asleep on water wakes when the water moves. Replays of worlds with bodies in water change. New host function physics3d_water_at reads the water surface height (swell included) and the depth of a point. 0.2.3 - 2026-10-31 Blocks runtime.blocks: "shapes" is now the default and the only supported block registry. classic and extended still load but resolve to shapes . Classic worlds' hashes and replay journals change. Hub Simpler navigation: four tabs instead of six. One updates summary with a single Update all button. Optional background self-update (re-signed on macOS). Projects: secondary actions moved into a More menu. Home folds Multiplayer and Learn. Editor The left tool column scrolls when the window is short. Frame selection stays pinned at the bottom. 0.2.2 - 2026-10-31 Sound, Hub and scripting fixes, plus a new Scripting documentation category. Upgrade recommended: the sound bug affects every game and the editor. Audio Fixed a sound that looped, grew louder with every new sound and ended up saturating. The default pack gained rain, wind, thunder, flowing water and lava sounds. The harsh synthesized builtin:* sounds are removed. Block, jump and landing sounds no longer spam, and the low rumbling thuds are gone. Landing is silent unless you fall 1.6 blocks or more. Hub Selection frames only show for keyboard navigation. Idle CPU use dropped from about 107% to about 2.5% of one core. The window is movable again by its title bar on macOS. Editor New Play > Run as a Game: starts the project in its own game window, like burrow run . Scripting Spawn("name") works in every runtime, loading prefabs from the project. Fixed SetTransform with a zero scale making the node invisible. Fixed the SDK vector accessors ( PhysicsBodyHalf , NavAgentVel , ...) reading NaN and rejecting writes. Fixed NetPlayerInfo always reading zeros. Fixed the first burrow script build after burrow script new failing. Fixed Play mode not routing the mouse, keyboard and gamepad to the game. The project templates no longer call the removed builtin:* sounds. New Scripting category in the documentation (12 pages). 0.2.1 - 2026-10-31 Performance and Windows fixes. Upgrade recommended on Windows. Performance Moving the mouse no longer drops the frame rate (was 14 fps with a 1000 Hz mouse). The editor viewport runs at 60 fps on discrete GPUs (was 27 fps). Continuous block editing is lighter on the CPU. Windows Security: a directory junction inside a project could write files outside it. Links and junctions are refused now. Importing a character skin without a project no longer stores an absolute path. Installers Installers and archives rebuilt for Windows, macOS and Linux. 0.2.0 - 2026-10-31 Multiplayer Multiplayer is playable ( networking ). Host with burrow serve or from the editor. Join with a link from the Hub or burrowplay -connect . It has TLS, per-player input, late joins, reconnection and desync repair. Games without the net plugin are unchanged. Display Windows follow the display scale on Windows, macOS and Linux. New UI scale setting and Ctrl/Cmd plus/minus/0. Engine The simulation, 3D physics included, gives the same result on arm64 and amd64 ( determinism ). Installers One installer per OS: Windows setup, macOS disk image, Linux AppImage, .tar.gz and .deb . The installers are unsigned for now. 0.1.0 - 2026-10-30 First public version of Burrow: a deterministic voxel game engine in Go, with an editor, scripting, a Vulkan renderer and an interface made for AI agents. Early version, MIT licensed. Engine Same seed and same inputs always give the same world, so any session can be replayed ( burrow test ). Voxel worlds with biomes, rivers, mountains and caves, plus physics, pathfinding, particles, weather and water. Scene tree with prefabs and saves, a game UI toolkit and six camera types (first and third person, top-down, isometric, side-scroller, cinematic). Nine project templates: sandbox, builder, scripted, platformer, physics puzzle, top-down strategy, survival, models, empty. Rendering Vulkan renderer with quality levels from off to ultra: sky, clouds, shadows, ambient occlusion, bloom, water reflections, rain, snow and storms. Anti-aliasing and upscaling (FXAA, SMAA, TAA, FSR 1 and 2) and optional ray tracing. A CPU renderer makes the same images without a window or GPU, for tests and screenshots. Editor and tools burrowedit : viewport, hierarchy, inspector, asset browser, profiler, terrain tools, undo and redo, Play mode and built-in tutorials. burrow command line: new, run, edit, test, build, script, assets, doctor, docs. Everything the editor does also works headless over MCP and a JSON CLI. Scripting Scripts are written in Go, compiled to WebAssembly, or built as visual graphs with no code. They run inside the simulation, so they replay like everything else. Hub and distribution Burrow Hub manages projects and engine versions, opens the editor, plays and exports. Update checks are optional and only signed manifests are accepted. No telemetry is sent. A Windows x64 download holds the editor, Hub, command line, script SDK, docs and templates. A website hosts the documentation, news and this changelog. Known limits This is an early version and the API may change. Windows builds are untested on real hardware and unsigned, so SmartScreen may warn. Windowed use is supported on macOS Apple silicon only. There is no multiplayer yet. Textures are not animated, and blocks added after Minecraft 1.16 use flat colours.

mygame A multiplayer lobby and match starter. Players connect to a lobby (team, colour, ready), the host picks the map and the time limit and starts, a countdown runs, the chosen map loads, the first avatar to reach the golden pad in the middle wins, and everybody comes back to the lobby with the results. burrow serve . # host: prints the join link burrow run . -- -connect <link> # join from another machine/CLI Pieces: runtime.lobby in vox.project : 2 to 8 players, 2 teams, 5 s countdown, two settings ( map : meadow or canyon, length ). See docs/lobby.md . ui/lobby.ui.json : the Lobby game UI screen (player list, ready toggle, team and colour buttons, settings, host start and cancel, countdown, results with "back to lobby"). Its buttons carry lobby:* actions that the engine turns into the lobby commands; no code is needed for the input. It is the Lobby template of the game UI designer, edit it freely. scripts/lobby : publishes the lobby into the screen's values, loads the chosen map when the match starts, checks the win condition and calls lobby_end_match with {"placements": {"<player id>": place}} (the convention a dedicated server forwards to a matchmaker). scripts/avatars : the base multiplayer script (one avatar per connected player); see the multiplayer template. levels/meadow.level , levels/canyon.level : two 64 x 64 arenas with a goal zone; add more maps by adding levels and choices of the map setting ( go run ./templates/mkassets lobby_match in the Burrow checkout shows how they are built). burrow script build # compile scripts (burrow run / test / build do it automatically) burrow run | burrow edit | burrow test | burrow build -o game A dedicated server can host the matches of this project in lobby mode ( docs/dedicated-server.md , "Lobby mode"). Set "texture_pack": "none" in the runtime section of vox.project (flat colours) or build with burrow build --no-default-textures to ship without it. mygame A multiplayer-ready starter: a flat world, the first-person controller (its camera and movement stay local even in a session), and one WebAssembly script, avatars , that draws and moves one avatar per connected player from that player's input in the server's player registry. burrow serve . # host: prints the join link burrow run . -- -connect <link> # join from another machine/CLI In a session, sdk.Action() is empty by design (a local input cannot enter the hashed shared simulation state), so the script reads NetPlayerInfo(id).Input instead — see docs/scripting/08-multiplayer.md . Solo, with no connected players, the same script falls back to Action() and drives its own player node. Overloading the base script The script is a normal project script — edit scripts/avatars/main.go and burrow script build (or just burrow run , which rebuilds), or tweak the script component's props in scenes/main.voxscn ( speed , sprint_mul , jump_bit , sprint_bit , auto_test ). Set "auto_test": true to walk forward regardless of input, so movement is verifiable headlessly. burrow script build # compile scripts (burrow run / test / build do it automatically) burrow run | burrow edit | burrow test | burrow build -o game In a session the scene's own player node is hidden (its mesh and character are removed), and each avatar is spawned and despawned with its player. The jump and sprint button bits default to the positions of jump and sprint in input.json (every action but move / look , in name order). A test checks them; if you add or rename actions, set jump_bit and sprint_bit in the script props. Each script remembers things only in components (props, state), so snapshots, undo and replay are exact. go.mod points at your Burrow checkout ( replace burrow-engine => ... ). Texture licence The terrain uses the default block texture pack, Pixel Perfection CE (CC-BY-SA-4.0: credit the authors and keep the textures under the same licence; commercial use is allowed). burrow build prints the notice. Set "texture_pack": "none" in the runtime section of vox.project (flat colours) or build with burrow build --no-default-textures to ship without it. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and docs/texture-packs.md .

mygame A 2.5D platformer built only from engine features: a side-scroller camera, two hand-built levels ( levels/*.level ) with checkpoints and a goal, kinematic moving platforms (physics3d), coins, hazards, a kill plane, a HUD, a pause menu, quick save and load, particles and sounds. All game rules are in one Go script ( scripts/game/main.go , compiled to WebAssembly); the engine has no platformer code. burrow run # A/D or arrows: move Space: jump P or Esc: pause F5 / F9: quick save / load burrow test # headless: 200 ticks three times, replay, StateHash burrow script build Levels are authored with go run ./templates/mkassets platformer in the Burrow repository (plain block boxes); the node list of a level (coins, platforms) is part of the .level file. Edit a level in burrow edit (View > Levels) and save it back. scripts/game/main.go has three named scripts: player (input, rules, HUD, saves), coin and mover . Game data (score, lives, checkpoint) lives in the save key/value store, so a quick save restores it with the world. Texture licence The terrain uses the default block texture pack, whose licence is restricted: it is fine for development, but check it before you distribute a game. Set "texture_pack": "none" in vox.project or build with burrow build --no-default-textures to ship without it. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and docs/texture-packs.md in the Burrow repository.
